name: rs_0439
text:
The drawing shows a cyclohexane ring with a methoxy group (MeO) at the left carbon and an NHCH3 group at the right carbon, which are para (1,4) to each other. Both substituent bonds are drawn as bold wedges, so the two groups are on the same face of the ring, which is the cis isomer.

To write the stereo SMILES, I place the two stereocentres in the ring: C1 bears OMe and C4 bears NHMe.

SMILES: CO[C@H]1CC[C@@H](NC)CC1 — I need to check whether this is cis or trans.

For the first centre, C1 is written as [C@H] with neighbours in the order O, H, ring-closure 1 (which is the last ring atom, C6), and C2. Looking from O, the sequence H, C6, C2 runs counterclockwise.

For the fourth centre, [C@@H] has neighbours in the order C3 (preceding), H, N, C5. Looking from C3, the sequence H, N, C5 runs clockwise.

Determining cis or trans directly from these chirality tags is error-prone, so I use a known reference instead. Trans-1,4-dimethylcyclohexane is C[C@H]1CC[C@@H](C)CC1, and the pattern I wrote has the same form, so it is trans. The cis isomer therefore needs the same tag on both centres: CO[C@H]1CC[C@H](NC)CC1.

Both bonds are wedged, which gives cis.

SMILES: CO[C@H]1CC[C@H](NC)CC1

name: rs_0453
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-benzyl isatin.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. Its neighbouring ring carbon (meta position) is bonded to the second ring. On the second ring, the carbon next to the biaryl bond bears OH, and the carbon next to that bears the NH–N= group.

**Hydrazone and isatin part.** The NH is bonded to N=, which double-bonds to C3 of the indolin-2-one. C2 is the C=O and N1 carries a benzyl group.

**Geometry.** The drawing shows a double bond with HN on one side and the ring on the other. The C=N is drawn with NH going down-left from N, and the ring C3 is lower-right of N. At the N= atom, the NH substituent is to the left. At C3, the C2 (carbonyl) is down-left and C3a is to the right. The N is at upper-left of C3, so the NH on N points left/down, on the same side as C2 (carbonyl), which is the usual Z form with an intramolecular H-bond to C=O. I'll encode that.

Writing the SMILES as `N/N=C1/C(=O)N(...)c2ccccc12` with stereo: N(H) on one side and C2 on the same side gives Z.

Ar–N/N=C1\C(=O)... Here the bond from Ar-N to N is "/", so the NH-aryl lies below N (written before it). After `=C1`, the next atom C(=O) is written with "\", meaning it lies below the C. Both substituents are on the same side, which is Z.

Full SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(Cc3ccccc3)c3ccccc23)c1O

In this ring-closure form, the stereo marks on `C2/C(=O)` are relative to the written order. `N/N=C2/C(=O)` places N above and C(=O) below the double bond, which is E, so I need `N/N=C2\C(=O)` to get Z.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(Cc3ccccc3)c3ccccc23)c1O

text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-substituted isatin.

So the second ring is 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl, with the aryl group at position 1.

**Isatin part.** The oxindole has C=O at C2 and the C3=N hydrazone carbon. The ring nitrogen bears a 3-methylthiophen-2-yl group. The thiophene is drawn with C2 attached to N, a methyl on C3, then C4, C5 and S.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH sits on the lower left of the N, and the C=N carbon is C3 of the oxindole. At C3, the substituent toward C2 (C=O) is on the left and the aromatic ring is on the right.

At the double bond, the top atom (C3) is at about (405, 405) and the lower atom (N) is at about (405, 335). The N's other substituent, NH, is at the left (350, 310). On C3, the carbonyl carbon C2 is at the lower left (345, 440) and the aryl carbon C3a is at the lower right (450, 440). The NH is on the left, the same side as C2 (C=O), which gives Z in the usual priority analysis: on C3, C2 (O,O,N) outranks C3a (C,C,C), so C2 is the higher priority, and NH is on that side.

The SMILES below is written with this geometry, N(H)/N=C3 with C2 on the same side.

name: rs_0561
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon carrying an H, an OH, a phenyl group (Ph), and a group labeled "PH3C".

"PH3C" is most likely a misprint of H3C, which would make the molecule 1-phenylethanol. Read literally, though, "PH3C" means a carbon bearing a PH3 group, i.e. a phosphonium-like or phosphorane-type substituent. Written out, that is a CH2 attached to PH3, so the drawing could be read as PH3-CH2-CH(OH)Ph. The label is probably the pre-formatted "H3C" with a stray "P", but the instruction is to read the structure from the drawing itself.

Taking the label literally, "PH3C" is a carbon with a PH3 attached. The carbon would then be bonded to P, to the central CH, and to H atoms. With P as PH3 (neutral, a phosphine) and the carbon needing four bonds, the substituent is P–CH2–: the P is bonded to C, and the label gives it 3 H.

This gives the literal SMILES for PH3 bonded to CH2, which is a pentavalent phosphorane-like P: PH3(CH2...) → P(H)(H)(H)CC(O)c1ccccc1. Only the P–C bond is drawn, so phosphorus carries 3 H plus 1 C, which is four bonds, and the SMILES would be written with explicit hydrogens as [PH3]. In SMILES, writing P with its implied hydrogens would give PH3 only for valence 3, so I would write [PH3] explicitly. The carbon attached to P is then CH2, so the SMILES is [PH3]CC(O)c1ccccc1.

SMILES: [PH3]CC(O)c1ccccc1

**Hydrazone and isatin part.** The NH–N= group ends in a C3=N double bond on an oxindole. C2 is a C=O, and N1 bears a thiophen-3-yl group. In the drawing, the C=N sits at the top of the five-membered ring, with the N-substituent at the lower left and the thiophene attached through its 3-position.

**Stereochemistry.** The hydrazone C=N geometry is drawn. HN is on the left of the N=, and the lower-left carbon of the ring is C2 (C=O). Taking the NH–N=C unit: the NH is up-left of the N, and the C3 is below-right of the N. At C3, the carbonyl C2 is on the left and the aromatic carbon C3a is on the right.

For the C=N bond, the N= atom is at (410, 340) with NH at (340, 310) to its upper left. C3 is at (410, 400) directly below. On C3, C2 is at the lower left (340, 430) and C3a is at the lower right (480, 430). The NH is on the left of the bond and C2 is also on the left, so they are on the same side (cis, Z-like).

Writing the SMILES with N/N=C3/ and checking the directions: `Oc1c(c2cccc(C(=O)O)c2)cccc1N/N=C1/C(=O)N(c2ccsc2)c2ccccc12`.

Reading the bond marks: `N/N=C1/C(=O)...` puts the NH below the first bond and C(=O) above the second, which makes them trans. For cis (NH and C2 on the same side), I need `N/N=C1\C(=O)`.

SMILES: OC1=C(C2=CC(C(=O)O)=CC=C2)C=CC=C1N/N=C1/C(=O)N(C2=CSC=C2)C2=CC=CC=C12

The SMILES above does not match the geometry I derived, so I rewrote it in the cis form:

In `N/N=C1\C(=O)N(...)c2ccccc12`, NH sits before the N= with "/" and C2 after C3 with "\", which gives the same side (Z-like). That is the form I use.

SMILES: Oc1c(-c2cccc(C(=O)O)c2)cccc1N/N=C1\C(=O)N(c2ccsc2)c2ccccc12

name: rs_0586
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

**Core.** This is a pyrazolo[1,5-b][1,2,4]triazole drawn in its quinone-imine (dye) form.
- The five-membered ring contains C7 (bearing COO–), C6 (bearing CN), C5 (=N exocyclic), N4 (the bridgehead N), and C3a.
- The triazole ring contains the bridgehead N, N, C(aryl)=N, and C3a.
- C7 is double-bonded to C6, and C5 is double-bonded to the exocyclic N.

**Core SMILES.** Starting from the ester carbon:
- C7: C(=O)(O-R)C1=C(C#N)C(=Nc...)n2nc(Ar)nc12
- Ring closure: C7 is C1, C6 is C(C#N), C5 is C(=N...), the bridgehead is n2, then n, c(Ar), n, and c12 is C3a, bonded to both C7 and the bridgehead N.
- Ring 1 is the five-membered ring: C7, C6, C5, N, C3a. Ring 2 is the triazole.
- The triazole drawing has N–N from the bridgehead N to N, then C(aryl)=N, then C3a=N. The aromatic form n2nc(Ar)nc12 captures this.

**Aryl on the triazole.** 4-tert-butylphenyl: c1ccc(cc1)C(C)(C)C.

**Imine aryl.** The imine N is attached to a benzene ring. Its ortho position carries CH3. Para to the imine N is N(Et)CH2CH2NHSO2CH3, drawn as "H3CO2SHNH2CH2C", which is the CH3SO2NH–CH2CH2 group.
- Ring SMILES: N=C... c1ccc(N(CC)CCNS(C)(=O)=O)cc1C

**Ester group.** The cyclohexyl ring is attached through the O at C1. Both ortho positions (C2 and C6) carry tert-butyl groups. C4 carries a methyl group.
- Ring SMILES: C1(OC=O)C(C(C)(C)C)CC(C)CC1C(C)(C)C

**Assembly.**
CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)-c1nc2c(C(=O)OC3C(C(C)(C)C)CC(C)CC3C(C)(C)C)c(C#N)c(=Nc3ccc(N(CC)CCNS(C)(=O)=O)cc3C)n2n1

For the aromatic form I need the pattern c(=N...) with an exocyclic double bond. A Kekulé-style version is safer:

CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)C1=NN2C(=C(C#N)C(C(=O)OC3C(C(C)(C)C)CC(C)CC3C(C)(C)C)=C2... 

This has to be written carefully. Atoms:
- C3a: C2(=N1...) is part of the triazole.
- Triazole: C1(Ar)=NC2=C(C(=O)OR)C(C#N)=... 

The drawing has C3a=N in the triazole, C7=C6, and C5=N exocyclic, so:

C1(Ar)=NC2=NC... 

Writing it out: Ar-C1=NC2=C(C(=O)OR)C(C#N)C(=NAr')N2N1 would not work, because C3a would have two double bonds.

Instead, following the drawing: C3a is double-bonded to N (the triazole N next to C-aryl is the one at the top right). The bonds are then:
- N(bridgehead)–N=C(Ar)–N=C3a, so the ring is N1(bridgehead)–N=C(Ar)–N=C3a–N1.
- C3a is bonded to C7, and C7=C6.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)C1=NC2=C(C(=O)OR)... 

C3a has a double bond to N and a single bond to C7. Therefore:
C1(Ar)=NC2=NN... does not fit. The correct form is:

name: rs_0593
text:
The drawing shows a 3-hydroxy-4-methoxypyridine-2-carboxamide whose amide nitrogen is attached to a substituted cycloheptane ring.

**Pyridine part:** N1, C2 (bearing the C(=O)NH group), C3 (OH), C4 (OMe), C5 and C6 (both CH).

**Cycloheptane ring** (7 atoms), going around from the NH-bearing carbon:
- C1 carries the NH.
- C2 is CH2 (top left).
- C3 is the quaternary carbon with gem-dimethyl (top).
- C4 carries Cl.
- C5 carries Cl.
- C6 is CH with a hashed methyl.
- C7 is CH with a methyl (bottom left), adjacent to C1.

That is seven ring atoms: C1, CH2, CMe2, CHCl, CHCl, CH(Me), CH(Me).

**Stereochemistry:** Only the hashed methyl is a drawn stereo bond, so only that centre gets a stereo label.

**SMILES construction:** I wrote it starting from the pyridine:

COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2CC(C)(C)C(Cl)C(Cl)[C@H](C)C2C)c1O

The hashed methyl sits on the ring carbon between CHCl and CH(Me). Its neighbours in the drawing are:
- the CHCl carbon at the upper right,
- the CH(Me) carbon at the left,
- the methyl, pointing down and hashed (away from the viewer),
- an implicit H.

The ring carbon is at roughly (393, 250), with the CHCl neighbor at (440, 210), the CH(Me) neighbor at (330, 237), and the methyl at (415, 300) on a hash.

In my SMILES the atom is written `[C@H](C)C2C`, with the preceding atom being CHCl. The neighbour order is therefore CHCl, H, methyl, CH(Me).

To assign chirality, I viewed the centre from the CHCl neighbour. The methyl is hashed, so it is behind the plane. The H is in front, so I took it as toward the viewer. The remaining neighbours then run H, CH(Me), methyl.

Working this through from the 2D geometry: with the H toward the viewer, the other three neighbours in the plane appear in this order:
- CHCl at upper right (angle about 40°),
- CH(Me) at left (about 165°),
- methyl at bottom (about 290°).

Going CHCl → CH(Me) → methyl is counterclockwise as seen from the front. Since H points toward the viewer, the sense seen from the side opposite H is clockwise.

SMILES order is CHCl, H, Me, CH(Me). Looking from CHCl, the sequence (H, Me, CH(Me)) must be assigned @ or @@. An equivalent way to see this is to permute the order to H first: (H, CHCl, CH(Me), Me) takes one swap from (CHCl, H, CH(Me), Me), and another swap gives (CHCl, H, Me, CH(Me)), so the parity is even overall. For the order (H, CHCl, CH(Me), Me), looking from H (which is toward the viewer), CHCl → CH(Me) → Me is counterclockwise, which is `@`. The parity is even, so the original order is also `@`.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2CC(C)(C)C(Cl)C(Cl)[C@H](C)C2C)c1O

I read the molecule as three parts joined in a chain: a diethylaminophenyl group, a two-carbon bridge, and a chloro-carbazole.

- **Left end:** a para-substituted benzene ring carries an N(CH2CH3)2 group.
- **Bridge:** the ring is joined through –CH2–CH2– to the carbazole.
- **Carbazole:** the ring nitrogen bears an ethyl group. The bridge is attached at C3 of the upper ring, which sits two bonds from the ring-fusion carbon. Chlorine is on C6 of the lower ring, which is the equivalent position on the other side.

In the SMILES, `c2ccc3n(CC)c4ccc(Cl)cc4c3c2` traces the carbazole: C3 (bridge), C2, C1, the N-bearing carbon, N-ethyl, then the lower ring with Cl on C6, and the fusion carbons closing back to C3. I checked that the Cl carbon is separated from the fusion carbon C4b by one CH, as drawn. There are no stereocentres or wedge bonds.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1ccc(CCc2ccc3n(CC)c4ccc(Cl)cc4c3c2)cc1

name: rs_0609
text:
Reading the drawing: a phenyl group and a CH2–CHO chain are attached to the central carbon (C3), and so is an isopropyl group, whose CH bond is drawn as a hashed wedge. The molecule is 3‑phenyl‑4‑methylpentanal, Ph–CH(CH(CH3)2)–CH2–CHO.

Stereochemistry at C3:
- The hashed bond puts the isopropyl group behind the plane, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- CIP priorities are Ph (C,C,C) > iPr (C,C,H) > CH2CHO (C,H,H).
- In the drawing, Ph (upper left), iPr (down) and CH2 (upper right) run counterclockwise. With H toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is R.
- In the SMILES `O=CC[C@@H](c1ccccc1)C(C)C`, the neighbour order is CH2, H, Ph, iPr, and `@@` corresponds to R.

SMILES: O=CC[C@@H](c1ccccc1)C(C)C

name: rs_0613
text:

  - Numbering the ring: C1 bears the NH, C2 bears the C(=O), C3 is the CH next to C2, C4 bears Cl, C5 and C6 are CH. In the drawing, the C bearing NH is at the top left, and the C bearing C(=O) is below it. Moving from C2 to the lower right gives the CH, then the carbon bearing Cl, then the CH at the top right, then back to C1. So Cl sits on C4 of this numbering, which is para to C1 (the NH carbon).
- **Pyridine ring:** the amide NH is attached to the pyridine carbon next to N (C2), and Br is on C5 (the carbon para to C2).

SMILES, with the central ring written as c1(NC(=O)Ar)c(C(=O)N...)cc(Cl)cc1:

N#Cc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1

The next carbon after that bears the NH of the hydrazone. So the substituent pattern on this ring is aryl, OH, NH.

**Hydrazone and isatin.** The NH is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C3 of the indolin-2-one. C2 is a carbonyl (O=) and the ring nitrogen N1 carries the aryl group. The N-aryl group is 4-chloro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond is drawn with the NH on one side and the ring carbons on the other. In the drawing, HN is at lower left and the N= is at upper right of the double bond, with C3 below. The NH points to the left and up, while the C2 carbonyl lies toward the lower left of C3 and the benzo ring toward the right. The geometry is therefore likely Z, with NH syn to the C=O, which is the usual hydrogen-bonded form. I will leave the stereo out of the SMILES.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)
- Central ring: c2cccc(NN=C3...)c2O
- Isatin: C3=C... written as N=C3C(=O)N(Ar)c4ccccc34

- N2, at about 397,122, carries the benzyl group.
- C3 is the carbonyl carbon (C=O).
- N4 is the bridgehead nitrogen at about 372,222.
- C8a is the other fusion atom.

**Six-membered ring:**
- Bridgehead N4 is bonded to N (at about 372,290).
- That N is double-bonded to C6, which carries the 2-chlorophenyl group.
- C6 is bonded to C7, which carries the 4-chlorophenyl group.
- C7 is bonded to C8 (CH), which is bonded to C8a.

**Substituents:**
- N2 carries CH2 attached to a 4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring.
- C7 carries the 4-chlorophenyl group.
- C6 carries the 2-chlorophenyl group.

**SMILES assembly:**
O=C1N(Cc2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)N=C3C=C(c4ccc(Cl)cc4)C(c5ccccc5Cl)=NN13

**Check of the ring closures:**
- C1 (carbonyl) is bonded to N(Bn), then N=C3, where C3 is C8a.
- C8a is followed by C=C(Ar): C8 is CH and C7 carries the aryl group, so the C8a–C8 bond is single and C8=C7 is double.
- C7 is followed by C6(Ar)=N, then N, then N13, which closes both ring 1 (to the carbonyl carbon) and ring 3 (to C8a). This makes N4 bonded to C3, N5 and C8a, as required.

The drawing shows C8a=N in the triazole and C6=N in the pyridazine, with C7=C8 as the remaining double bond. The SMILES matches this arrangement.

name: rs_0623
text:
The drawing shows an isatin 3-hydrazone: a 2-oxindole whose C3 is double-bonded to N, which is attached to NH and then to a substituted phenyl ring.

**Acrylic acid part.** The acid is drawn as CO2H on a trans alkene: HO2C-CH=CH-Ar. The alkene is drawn with the acid carbon at the top and the aryl at the bottom right, so I take it as E.

**Central phenyl ring.** The vinyl group is at C1. The OH is at C3 (meta to the vinyl group). The NH-N is at C4 (para to the vinyl group), adjacent to the OH carbon.

**Hydrazone and oxindole.** The chain is Ar-NH-N=C3 of the oxindole. C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. The CF3 sits on the oxindole benzene ring at C6. The ring fusion carbons are C3a and C7a. C3a is bonded to C4, then C5, then C6 bearing CF3, then C7, then C7a, which is bonded to N1. In the drawing, the CF3 is on the lower-right carbon. The right-hand ring runs from C3a (upper left) to C4 (top), C5 (upper right), C6 (lower right, with CF3), C7 (bottom) and C7a. This is consistent with CF3 at C6.

**Stereochemistry of the C=N bond.** The NH is drawn on the upper left of the N, and the C=N is drawn with the N toward the upper right of C3. The C2 carbonyl is on the left, and the NH points toward the carbonyl side. I am not fully certain of this geometry, so I leave the C=N bond unspecified and specify only the alkene.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid and alkene: OC(=O)/C=C/c1ccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc23)c(O)c1
- Check of the central ring: c1 (vinyl), c, c, c(N…) is C4, then c(O) is C3, then c1 (C2). This gives vinyl at C1, NH at C4 and OH at C3, as required.
- Check of the oxindole: C2(=N…) is C3, C(=O) is C2, N is N1, then c3 is C7a, c is C7, c(CF3) is C6, c is C5, c is C4, c23 is C3a. This closes back to C3, as required.

SMILES: OC(=O)/C=C/c1ccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc23)c(O)c1

name: rs_0624
text:
I read the molecule as a 3-hydroxy-4-methoxypicolinamide of O-acetyl-threonine, whose carboxyl group is esterified to a 1-methyl-2-isobutyroyloxy-3-benzyl-3-(benzyloxycarbonyl)propyl unit.

**Pieces of the structure**
- **Pyridine ring:** a ring N, with OMe at C4, OH at C3, and the amide carbonyl at C2.
- **Threonine unit:** NH–CH(C=O)–CH(CH₃)–OAc. The N and the CH₃ are on hashed bonds. I assigned the alpha carbon as S and the beta carbon as R, which is the L-threonine configuration.
- **Ester chain:** O–CH(CH₃)–CH(OC(=O)CH(CH₃)₂)–CH(CH₂Ph)–C(=O)OCH₂Ph.
- **Chain stereocentres:** the CH₃ wedge on the first carbon and the O wedge on the second give S and R. The CH₂Ph wedge on the third carbon gives R.

I assigned each centre by CIP priorities from the wedge and hash drawing. I then converted those assignments into @/@@ tags by permutation parity, so the tags come from hand derivation rather than a toolkit check.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)O[C@@H](C)[C@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)[C@@H](Cc2ccccc2)C(=O)OCc2ccccc2)[C@@H](C)OC(C)=O)c1O

text:
I read the molecule as a 2-(N-methylamino)benzoxazole linked through an N-CH2CH2-O chain to a para-substituted benzene ring. That ring carries a CH2 group attached to a stereogenic carbon bearing COOH, H and OCH2CF3.

With H pointing away, the sequence O → COOH → CH2 runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` written after the COOH carbon encodes this S configuration.

name: rs_0638
text:
The molecule is symmetric: a central CH2 links two identical chlorinated benzene rings, and each ring carries one tertiary diarylamine nitrogen.

**Left half**
- The central ring has Cl at the position ortho to the N. The CH2 is para to that N.
- The N carries two aryl groups: a 3-(diethylamino)phenyl and a 2-(dimethylamino)phenyl.
- In the 3-(diethylamino)phenyl ring, the N attaches at the ring carbon next to the one bearing NEt2, i.e. meta.
- In the 2-(dimethylamino)phenyl ring, NMe2 sits on the carbon adjacent to the one bearing the central N, i.e. ortho.

**Right half**
- It is the same as the left: Cl ortho to N, CH2 para to N, with a 2-(dimethylamino)phenyl and a 3-(diethylamino)phenyl on the N.

**SMILES for one half:** the central ring is c1(N(c2cccc(N(CC)CC)c2)c2ccccc2N(C)C)c(Cl)cc(C...)cc1, with the CH2 attached at the para position.

**Full SMILES:**
CCN(CC)c1cccc(c1)N(c1ccccc1N(C)C)c1ccc(Cc2ccc(N(c3ccccc3N(C)C)c3cccc(N(CC)CC)c3)c(Cl)c2)cc1Cl

Check on the first central ring: c1ccc(C...)cc1Cl. The N-bearing carbon is c1, followed by c, c, then c(C), c, and c1Cl. The ring closure carbon bears Cl and is adjacent to c1. The CH2-bearing carbon is the fourth atom, which is para to c1. This is correct.

Check on the second ring: c2ccc(N...)c(Cl)c2. The CH2-bearing carbon is c2, followed by c, c, then c(N), then c(Cl), then c2. The N carbon is para to the CH2 carbon and Cl is ortho to N. This is correct.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1cccc(c1)N(c1ccccc1N(C)C)c1ccc(Cc2ccc(N(c3ccccc3N(C)C)c3cccc(N(CC)CC)c3)c(Cl)c2)cc1Cl

name: rs_0636
text:
I read the drawing in three parts and then assigned the two stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds.

**Structure read from the image**
- The left end is a morpholine ring joined through its nitrogen to a carbonyl, giving a morpholine amide.
- The carbon next to that carbonyl carries a neopentyl group (CH2–C(CH3)3, drawn on a bold wedge) and an oxygen that links to a carbamate, O–C(=O)–NH.
- The carbamate nitrogen attaches to a CH that bears a methyl (hashed bond) and a CH2–NH–aryl arm.

- Ester-bearing carbon: the neopentyl CH2 is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away. The priorities are O > C(=O)N > CH2. Going O → C=O → CH2 is counterclockwise in the drawing, so this centre is S, which is `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order used below.
- Carbamate-N-bearing carbon: the methyl is on a hash, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CH2N > CH3. Going N → CH2 → CH3 looks clockwise, and reversing for the H toward the viewer gives S, which is also `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order used below.

name: rs_0639
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-oxo-benzoxazole core (O1, C2 carbonyl, N3–H) fused to a benzene ring. On the benzene ring, one carbon bears a bromine. The adjacent carbon bears a CH2–CH(NHCbz)–CO2CH3 side chain.

- **Ring connectivity:** The ring CH next to the O-bearing carbon is bonded to the side-chain carbon. Br sits on the next carbon around the ring, with one aromatic CH between it and the N-bearing carbon.
- **Side chain:** CH2 leads to the alpha carbon. The alpha carbon carries CO2CH3 and NH–Cbz, where Cbz is C(=O)OCH2Ph.
- **Stereochemistry:** The bond from the alpha carbon to NHCbz is hashed, so N points away from the viewer and H points toward the viewer.
  - Priorities are N > CO2Me > CH2 > H.
  - Seen from the front, N (down) → CO2Me (upper right) → CH2 (upper left) runs counterclockwise.
  - H faces the viewer, so the sense reverses to clockwise, which is R.
  - In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` with neighbour order CO2Me, H, CH2, N corresponds to R.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@@H](Cc1cc2oc(=O)[nH]c2cc1Br)NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1

- CH–CH3 (wedged methyl): S, written `[C@H]`

I read this as a cholesterol 3-O-carbamate linked through a 6-aminohexanoyl chain to a pyrrolidine nitrogen. The pyrrolidine carries a succinate half-ester at C3 and a DMT-protected hydroxymethyl group at C4.

- **Pyrrolidine:** a five-membered ring containing N, with CH2–O–DMT on the adjacent ring carbon (C4).

- **Linker:** N–C(=O)–(CH2)5–NH–C(=O)–O–. I counted five CH2 vertices between the amide carbonyl and the HN, so this is a 6-aminohexanoyl chain.
- **Cholesterol:** the 5-ene steroid core (rings A–D) has the carbamate O at C3. The side chain is CH(CH3)–CH2CH2CH2–CH(CH3)2.

- Wedges are drawn only at C10 (methyl), C13 (methyl) and C17 (side chain). I assigned these as in natural cholesterol.
- C3, C8, C9, C14, C20 and the two pyrrolidine stereocentres are drawn with plain bonds, so they carry no stereo marks.

name: rs_0647
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine-2-carboxylic acid (HO2C on C2, ring N at the bottom) with a substituent at C6.

**Substituent at C6:** a vinyl carbon bearing a p-tolyl group (a para-methylphenyl, with the methyl drawn at the top right) and double-bonded to CH. That CH connects to CH2, which connects to the pyrrolidine nitrogen.

**Fragment SMILES:** the chain is C(=CCN1CCCC1)(c1ccc(C)cc1) attached to the pyridine.

**Stereochemistry:** the double bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The pyridine is at upper left on one alkene carbon and the tolyl at upper right on the same carbon. On the other alkene carbon, the CH2 goes down-right and the H is implied. The alkene runs vertically from the upper carbon at about (298,127) to the lower carbon at about (298,200), and the lower carbon's CH2 goes to the right, at about (353,235).

- Pyridine is on the left of the upper carbon and CH2 is on the right of the lower carbon, so pyridine and CH2 are trans.
- Tolyl is on the right of the upper carbon, on the same side as CH2, so tolyl and CH2 are cis.

**Writing the SMILES:** I write it as pyridyl/C(=C/CN...)c-tolyl, so the pyridyl is "before" the alkene carbon.

- `c1(...)` is the pyridyl, then `/C(=C/CN2CCCC2)` with the tolyl as the second substituent on that carbon.
- In `A/C(=C/B)C`, A and B are on opposite sides, which means the pyridyl and CH2 are trans. This matches the drawing.

**Full SMILES:** OC(=O)c1cccc(n1)/C(=C/CN1CCCC1)c1ccc(C)cc1

The pyridine ring atoms are c1 (C2, bearing COOH), c, c, c (C3 to C5), then c(n1), which is C6 attached to N. That gives a valid six-membered ring.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(n1)/C(=C/CN1CCCC1)c1ccc(C)cc1

text:
The drawing breaks down into three regions.

**Left region.** A 3,4-dihydroquinazolin-2(1H)-one. N1 carries the piperidin-4-yl group and is bonded to the C=O carbon (C2). C2 is bonded to the NH (N3), then CH2 (C4), then the benzene ring. The benzene ring carries Cl at C6, which is para to N1 (N1 sits on C8a, and C6 is the carbon across from it).

**Middle region.** The piperidine nitrogen is bonded to CH2–CH(OH)–CH2, and that chain ends at N1 of the pyrazole.

**Right region.** A 4,5,6,7-tetrahydropyrazolo[4,3-c]pyridine.
- N1 (bearing the chain) is bonded to N2, which is double-bonded to C3.
- C3 carries the 4-CF3-phenyl group and is bonded to C3a.
- C3a is bonded to CH2, then N5 (bearing SO2Me), then CH2, then CH2, then C7a.
- C7a is bonded back to N1 and double-bonded to C3a.

- Quinazolinone: O=C1NCc2cc(Cl)ccc2N1C3CCN(CC3)…
- Chain: CC(O)Cn4nc(c5ccc(cc5)C(F)(F)F)c6CN(CCc46)S(C)(=O)=O

The ring closure labels need care. The pyrazole is written n4 n c(Ar) c6 … c46, where c6 is C3a and the final c46 is C7a. C3a connects to CH2, then N(SO2Me), then CH2CH2, then C7a. C7a closes ring 4 to N1 and ring 6 to C3a.

Full SMILES: O=C1NCc2cc(Cl)ccc2N1C3CCN(CC3)CC(O)Cn4nc(-c5ccc(cc5)C(F)(F)F)c6CN(CCc46)S(C)(=O)=O

name: rs_0652
text:
The drawing shows a 7-methyl-1H-indazole whose C5 carries a vinyl group. That vinyl group is an alpha-(Cbz-amino)acrylate methyl ester.

**Indazole core.** N1 (NH) is bonded to C7a. N2 is double-bonded to C3, and C3 connects to C3a. The benzene ring runs C3a, C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a. The methyl group sits on C7, next to C7a, and the side chain is on C5.

**Side chain.** C5 is bonded to CH=, which is double-bonded to C(NHCbz)(CO2Me). The Cbz group is NH–C(=O)–O–CH2–Ph.

**Alkene geometry.** The CH on the left is attached to the aryl group, drawn lower left. The alpha carbon is lower right, and it carries N going up-right and the ester going down. The aryl group is on the lower-left side of the CH, and from the alpha carbon the NH goes up while the ester goes down. The aryl group is at the lower left of the CH carbon, pointing down-left, while the CH's other substituent is H, pointing up-left. On the alpha carbon, N is up and the ester is down. The aryl group and the ester are therefore both on the lower side, which is cis, and the aryl group and N are trans.

Priorities: on the CH carbon, aryl outranks H. On the alpha carbon, N outranks C. Aryl and N are on opposite sides, so the configuration is E by CIP, though the SMILES only needs the cis/trans arrangement.

**SMILES.** Written as c(Ar)/C=C(/N...)C(=O)OC, the aryl is "before" the first alkene carbon with the bond "/", and N comes after the second alkene carbon with "/". Two "/" markers in this pattern mean the aryl and N are trans (F/C=C/F is trans). That matches the drawing.

Full SMILES: COC(=O)/C(NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)=C/c1cc(C)c2[nH]ncc2c1

Checking this form: the ester C is written before the alpha carbon, "C(=O)/C(N…)=C/Ar". The bond "/" from the ester carbon to the alpha carbon means the ester is "below" the alpha carbon. The "/" after =C means the aryl is "above" the CH carbon. Ester and aryl would then be on opposite sides (trans), which contradicts the drawing, where they are cis. I'll flip one marker to correct this: COC(=O)/C(NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)=C\c1cc(C)c2[nH]ncc2c1. Here the ester and aryl are cis, so the aryl and N are trans, as drawn.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C(NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)=C\c1cc(C)c2[nH]ncc2c1

text:
I read the drawing as methyl N-Boc-4-[(6,7-dimethoxy-2-methylquinazolin-4-yl)oxy]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylate. I worked through it region by region.

- **Quinazoline:** a benzene ring fused to a pyrimidine. The benzo ring carries two OMe groups at C6 and C7. The pyrimidine ring has N1 at the top, a methyl on C2, N3, and C4 bearing the ether oxygen.
- **Linker:** C4 of the quinazoline is bonded through an oxygen to C4 of the pyrrolidine.
- **Pyrrolidine:** the ring nitrogen carries a Boc group (C(=O)OC(C)(C)C). C2 carries the methyl ester CO2Me on a wedge bond. C4 carries the aryl ether oxygen on a hashed bond.

name: rs_0654
text:
The structure is a dibenzobarrelene-type (9,10-dihydro-9,10-ethanoanthracene) core carrying an amide, which I read as follows.

**Bicyclic core.** Two benzene rings are bridged by a two-carbon unit. One bridgehead (lower left, CH) joins the left benzene ring and the right benzene ring. The other bridgehead (upper, CH) also joins both rings. The ethano bridge is CH2 followed by a quaternary C bearing a methyl group and the C(=O)NH group. In the picture, the quaternary C sits at the top, with CH2 below it leading to the bridgehead.

**Atom connectivity.**
- C11 is the quaternary carbon, bearing the methyl and the amide carbonyl.
- C12 is the CH2.
- C9 is the upper bridgehead, bonded to C12 and to both aromatic rings. In the drawing it is the carbon at about (200,190), joined to the CH2 and to the right ring at (255,225).
- C10 is the lower bridgehead at about (160,262), joined to the left ring and to the right ring at (255,300).
- C11 is bonded to the bridgehead at (200,190) through the CH2, so the quaternary carbon is attached to the CH2 and to the carbonyl, not directly to a bridgehead.

The left benzene ring connects to the bridgehead at (200,190) through its carbon at (130,215) and to the lower bridgehead through (105,270). The right ring has a CN substituent on the carbon adjacent to the ring carbon bonded to the lower bridgehead.

**SMILES for the core.** Writing C11 as C1(C)(C(=O)N...)CC2c3ccccc3C1c1c2cccc1C#N would place the quaternary carbon on a bridgehead, which does not match. The correct bridge is C11–C12 with C11 bonded to one bridgehead and C12 to the other:

C11 bonded to bridgehead A, and C12 bonded to bridgehead B.

In the drawing, C11 (200,110) is bonded to the CH2 (160,160) and to the bridgehead (200,190) below it. The CH2 is bonded to the other bridgehead (160,262). So the SMILES is:

CC1(C(=O)N...)CC2c3ccccc3C1c1cccc(C#N)c12

- Bridgehead A (ring closure 1) is bonded to C11, the left ring, and the right ring.
- Bridgehead B (ring closure 2) is bonded to C12, the left ring, and the right ring.
- The CN-bearing carbon is adjacent to the right-ring carbon attached to bridgehead B (the lower one, at 255,300), so CN sits on the ring carbon next to the one bonded to B.

**Right ring.** In `C1c1cccc(C#N)c12`, the first atom after A is the ring carbon bonded to A. The ring then runs c-c-c-c(CN)-c, and the last carbon closes to B. That puts CN next to the B-attached carbon, as drawn.

**Amide substituent.** The NH is attached to thiazole C2. The thiazole has S, C5(H), C4 bearing the naphthyl group, and N3. The naphthyl is 4-fluoronaphthalen-1-yl.

Amide: C(=O)Nc1nc(cs1)-c1ccc(F)c2ccccc12

SMILES: CC1(C(=O)Nc2nc(cs2)-c2ccc(F)c3ccccc23)CC2c3ccccc3C1c1cccc(C#N)c12

name: rs_0664
text:
The drawing is a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin core.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. Its meta position is bonded to the second ring. On the second ring, the carbon next to the biaryl carbon bears OH, and the next carbon bears NH. So the central ring has the aryl group, the OH and the NH-N= on three adjacent carbons.

**Isatin part.** The hydrazone N= is double-bonded to C3 of the indolin-2-one. C2 is C=O and N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. On the benzo ring, going around from C3a, the first carbon (C4) is CH, then C5 bears F, then C6 bears CH3, then C7 is CH, then C7a is bonded to N1.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows the C=N geometry, with NH on the lower left of the N and the carbonyl C2 on the left of C3. Reading the picture, the N= sits above C3, with NH to its upper left and the ring C2 to the lower left of C3. The NH is on the same side as C2 (the carbonyl side), which is the usual Z hydrazone. I will write it as Z.

**SMILES construction.**
- Write the C=N unit as `N(/N=C1/...)`, using `/` and `\` marks to fix the geometry.
- Using the form `c(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(...)c3cc(C)c(F)cc23)`: the NH is written before the N, and the N is double-bonded to C2.
- For `N/N=C2/C(=O)`, the NH is "below" the N (the `/` before N means NH is below), and the `/` after C2 puts C(=O) above the C. That makes NH and C(=O) trans, which is E.
- For Z, use `N/N=C2\C(=O)...`.

Full SMILES:
`OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C)c(F)cc23)c1O`

Check on the benzo ring: `c3cc(C)c(F)cc23` starts at C7a (attached to N), then C7 (H), C6 (CH3), C5 (F), C4 (H), then C3a, which closes to C3 via ring label 2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C)c(F)cc23)c1O

name: rs_0670
text:
I read the drawing in three parts and then fixed the stereochemistry at the one wedged carbon.

**Pyrazinone core.** The ring runs N1, C2(=O), C3, N4, C5(Br), C6(H). N1 carries the side chain, C3 carries the indoline nitrogen, and C5 carries the bromine.

**Side chain on N1.** This is a CH(CH2CH3)(CH2OCH3) group. Its carbon is the only stereocentre, and it is drawn with a wedged H.

**Indoline on C3.** The indoline nitrogen is bonded to C7a, and the five-membered ring is N–CH2–CH2–C3a. On the benzene ring, C7 carries Cl, C6 carries F, C5 carries OMe, and C4 is CH.

**Stereocentre.** The substituents on the stereocentre are N (down), CH2OMe (upper right), ethyl (upper left) and H (wedged toward the viewer). The CIP priorities are N > CH2O > ethyl > H. **Hydrazone and isatin part.** The NH is linked by N= to C3 of the indolin-2-one. C2 is the C=O, and N1 carries a 4-isopropylphenyl group.

The C=N bond runs from N (295, 400) down to C3 (325, 460). The NH on N lies to the left of this axis. The C2 carbonyl on C3 also lies to the left, at x = 290. So NH and C2 are on the same side, which makes the C2 side Z with respect to the NH.

For CIP priorities, on C3 the carbonyl C2 (O, O, N) outranks C3a (C, C, C). On N, the NH outranks the lone pair. The higher-priority groups are on the same side, so the configuration is Z.

**SMILES writing.** I wrote the fragment as N/N=C3\C(=O)..., with the whole ring system set out as follows:

OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(cc3)C(C)C)c3ccccc23)c1O

To check the notation: "N/N=C2/C(=O)" reads as the N preceding the double-bond N with a "/" bond, and the C2 followed by "/C(=O)". The N–N "/" means the NH lies below the N. The C2–C(=O) "/" means C(=O) lies above the C. These are on opposite sides, which gives E, not Z. For Z (same side) I need N/N=C2\C(=O).

**Central benzene ring.** The CH= substituent sits at C1. Going around the ring, C3 carries OH and C4 carries the NH–N= hydrazone group. This gives c1(C=...)ccc(NN=)c(O)c1.

**Hydrazone and isatin core.** The hydrazone NH–N= is attached to C3 of the oxindole. The oxindole C2 is C=O and N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. The CF3 is on the benzo ring, at the carbon that is meta to the ring-fusion carbon attached to C3 and para to the carbon bonded to N. Tracing the benzo ring:
- C3a is the fusion carbon attached to C3.
- C4 is the top-left CH, C5 is the top-right CH, and C6 carries CF3.
- C7 is the CH next to C7a, and C7a is attached to N.

This places CF3 at position 6.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows cis/trans geometry for two double bonds.
- Thiazolidinedione exocyclic C=C: S is on the ring carbon, and the aryl is drawn on the lower side, with the C=O on the other side. Using the drawing, the ring C5 has S to the lower left and C4(=O) above. The CH carries the aryl going down. The ring S is therefore on the same side as the aryl, which is the usual Z form. SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)/C(=C/Ar)S1 would need careful checking, so I write it as S1/C(=C\Ar)C(=O)NC1=O, with the S–C=C–Ar relationship cis, i.e. Z.
- Hydrazone C=N: on C3 of the oxindole, the substituents are C2 (the carbonyl, upper left) and C3a (right). On N, the NH is up and to the left, toward the C2 carbonyl side. NH is therefore cis to C2.

**Writing the SMILES.**
O=C1NC(=O)S/C1=C\c1ccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc32)c(O)c1

Checking the thiazolidinedione stereo: S/C1=C\c means S is "below" the C1 atom and the aryl is "below" the CH after the double bond. "/" before C1 and "\" after the double bond places S and aryl on the same side, so Z. This is consistent.

Checking the hydrazone: N/N=C2/C(=O). The preceding aryl–N is written with "/" before the second N, and the C2 is followed by "/C(=O)". That makes the aryl N and the C(=O) on opposite sides, which would put NH trans to C2. I want NH cis to C2, so I change the bond after C2 to "\": N/N=C2\C(=O).

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)S/C1=C\c1ccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc32)c(O)c1

**Hydrazone linkage:** The NH is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C3 of the oxindole.

- C3 is the hydrazone carbon.
- C2 is the C=O carbon.
- N1 carries the benzyl group.
- The methyl is on the benzo ring at C5, which is para to N1 and meta to C3a.

**Stereochemistry:** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH is at the lower left of the N, and C3 has C2 (bottom, bearing C=O) and C3a (right). Taking coordinates from the drawing, N(=) is at (297, 398) with NH to its upper left at (230, 380). C3 is at (330, 455), with C2 at (297, 510) and C3a at (395, 440).

Relative to the C=N axis, which runs from (297, 398) to (330, 455), the NH lies on the left side. C2 also lies on the left or lower side, while C3a lies on the right. The NH and C2 are therefore on the same side, which is the Z configuration with respect to the C=O side.

- **Cyclohexane:** The ring carbon bonded to O is C1. Going around the ring, C2 is CH2, C3 is C(CH3)2, C4 is CH2, C5 is C(CH3)2 and C6 is CH2. Full SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(OC3CC(C)(C)CC(C)(C)C3)cc2)c1O

name: rs_0756
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Pyridazine ring:** six atoms with two adjacent nitrogens. One ring carbon carries the chain, and the carbon two positions away from it, on the side away from the nitrogens, carries OMe. This gives a 3-substituted 5-methoxypyridazine.
- **Linker:** two CH2 groups join the pyridazine carbon to the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Pyrrolidine ring:** a five-membered ring with N, then C2, C3 and C4, then C5. C3 carries an OMs group (OS(C)(=O)=O) on a wedge bond.
- **Stereochemistry:** with the hydrogen pointing back, the wedged O sits up-right, C4 lower-right and C2 lower-left. Going O → C4 → C2 is clockwise. The CIP priorities are O > C2 (attached to N) > C4 > H, so O → C2 → C4 is counterclockwise, which makes C3 **S**. In the SMILES below, written as C4, H, O, C2 around that atom, `[C@H]` encodes this S configuration.

SMILES: COc1cc(CCN2CC[C@H](OS(C)(=O)=O)C2)nnc1

- In the drawing, the carbon attached to the chromone is adjacent to the acetyl-bearing carbon that is adjacent to the C–O carbon.
- Going around that ring: C(Ac) next to the C–O carbon, then C(chromonyl), then C(Ac), then CH, then C9a, which is attached to the C=O.
- The right ring has the O-bearing carbon, then CH, then C(OH), then C(OH), then C(COOH), then C9a.

**Joined SMILES.** The chromone C3 is attached to the xanthone carbon between the two acetyl-bearing carbons:

Checking the xanthone portion of this string: c1 (attached to the chromone) is followed by c(C(C)=O), then cc2 (CH, then C9a), then c(...) closing the ring.
- The branch c(c1C(C)=O) is the ring-closing carbon bearing the O, with the c1 acetyl carbon in the branch. This gives atoms: c1(chromonyl), c(Ac), c(H), c2 (C9a), c(–O) (C4a), c1(Ac), which closes back to the chromonyl carbon.

- C4a then carries O, and the ring continues: Oc1cc(O)c(O)c(COOH)c1C2=O. The last carbon c1 closes the right ring, and C2=O closes onto C9a.

name: rs_0759
text:
I read the molecule as follows. Working from left to right:

- **Indazole:** a 1H-indazole attached through C6 to a carbonyl.
- **Tetrahydroisoquinoline:** that carbonyl acylates the ring nitrogen N2. The ring carries chlorines at C5 and C7, and a carboxamide at C6.
- **Amino-acid chain:** the amide nitrogen is attached to an α-carbon bearing CO2H and a CH2–NH group.
- **Cyanoguanidine:** the CH2–NH leads to a carbon with =N–C≡N, which is bonded to the nitrogen of a piperidine ring.
- **Piperidine:** the ring carries an OH at C3, drawn with a wedge.

**Stereochemistry:**
- **α-carbon:** the wedge goes to the CH2 group. With priorities N > CO2H > CH2 > H and H pointing away, N, CO2H, CH2 run counterclockwise, so the centre is S. In the SMILES this is `N[C@@H](CN...)C(=O)O`.
- **Piperidine C3:** the wedge goes to OH. With priorities OH > C2 > C4 > H and H pointing away, OH, C2, C4 run clockwise, so the centre is R. In the SMILES, written as `N3CCC[C@@H](O)C3`, this needs `@@`.

name: rs_0763
text:
I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES from these parts.

**Biphenyl part (left, top).** The first ring carries F and CO2H on adjacent carbons. Ring atoms run C1 (attached to the second ring), C2 (CH), C3 (C–CO2H), C4 (C–F), C5 (CH), C6 (CH). So the CO2H carbon is ortho to F, and the aryl attachment is para to F and meta to CO2H.

**Second ring.** It is attached to the first ring at one carbon. The adjacent carbon bears OH. The next carbon bears the NH–N= group. The remaining three carbons are CH.

**Hydrazone and isatin part.** The hydrazone NH–N= links to C3 of the indolin-2-one. C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a 3,5-dimethylphenyl group. On the indole benzo ring, the CO2Me sits at C6. Going around the ring: C3a, C4 (CH), C5 (CH), C6 (CO2Me), C7 (CH), C7a (attached to N). In the drawing, C3a is at the upper left of the benzo ring, and CO2Me is on the lower right carbon, which is adjacent to the C7 carbon next to C7a. This matches C6.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond has drawn geometry. At the top of the hydrazone, N (=N) sits above C3. The NH is up-left of the =N, and the C2 carbonyl is on the left of C3. The N–NH substituent and C2 look to be on the same side (Z).

I write it as C3(=N/NHAr) with C2 on the same side. The SMILES fragment is O=C1N(Ar)c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2/C1=N\Nc..., and I need to check the geometry of that form.

For `C1=N\N`, the bond written before C1 is `/C1` from the aromatic carbon c2. The atom c2 precedes C1 with a `/` bond: `c2/C1=N\N`. This means c2 is "below" C1 and N–N is "below" N, so c2 and NH are on the same side. Therefore C2 (the carbonyl, ring closure 1) is on the opposite side to NH, which gives E. I want C2 and NH on the same side, so I use `c2/C1=N/N`, which puts NH on the opposite side of c2 and hence on the same side as C2. This gives Z.

**Final SMILES.**
O=C1N(c3cc(C)cc(C)c3)c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2/C1=N/Nc4cccc(c4O)-c5ccc(F)c(C(=O)O)c5

SMILES: O=C1N(c3cc(C)cc(C)c3)c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2/C1=N/Nc4cccc(c4O)-c5ccc(F)c(C(=O)O)c5

name: rs_0762
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-pyrrolidinone (γ-lactam) with two substituents, and assigned stereochemistry from the wedge and hash bonds.

- **Lactam ring:** a five-membered ring made of C=O, two CH2 groups, a stereogenic CH and N.
- **N-substituent:** a CH2CH2 linker to a benzene ring that carries CO2H at the para position.
- **Ring carbon next to N:** it bears a wedged bond to a trans CH=CH.
- **Side chain:** after the alkene comes CH(OH) on a hashed bond, then three CH2 groups, then a cyclopropyl ring.

**Stereocentres**
- **Ring carbon next to N:** the priorities are N > vinyl > ring CH2 > H. With H pointing away, N→vinyl→CH2 runs clockwise, so this centre is R. In the SMILES order (ring CH2, H, N, vinyl) this is `[C@@H]`.
- **Carbinol carbon (CH–OH):** the priorities are OH > vinyl > CH2 > H. The hashed OH puts H toward the viewer, and OH→vinyl→CH2 appears clockwise, so the true configuration is S. In the SMILES order (vinyl, H, O, CH2) this is `[C@@H]`.
- **Alkene:** drawn trans, written `/C=C/`.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@@H](N1CCc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)O)/C=C/[C@@H](O)CCCC1CC1

name: rs_0802
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an oxindole (isatin-type) core.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. It is attached to a second ring that has an OH ortho to the biaryl bond and an NH–N= group on the other side of the OH. The CO2H ring is therefore 3-substituted, and the second ring is 1-aryl, 2-OH, 3-NHN=.

**Oxindole part.**
- N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group.
- C2 is C=O.
- C3 is the hydrazone carbon, C=N–NH–Ar.
- The fused benzene ring runs C3a, C4(F), C5(H), C6(CF3), C7(H), C7a.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond is drawn with explicit geometry. The N is at the lower left of C3, and the NH continues up-left from it. On C3, the C2 (carbonyl) side lies to the left and C3a to the right. The N=C bond runs from the upper-left N down to C3. The NH is attached to N and points up-left, so it sits on the same side as the C2 carbonyl (left).

I write the hydrazone as `C(=O)` on the left, with the C3 substituent order `C3(=N/NH...)`. Using the form `N1C(=O)/C(=N/Nc...)c2...`:
- For `C(=N/N...)` preceded by `/C(`, the bond `/C` goes from C2 to C3, meaning C2 is "below" C3.
- `=N/N` places the NH "above" N, so C2 and NH are on opposite sides (trans). This is E with respect to C2.

I want NH on the same side as C2, so I use `=N\N` instead.

**SMILES:** `OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(F)c23)c1O`

Checking the stereo in this written order: `N/N=C2/C(=O)...` has NH before N with "/", so the NH is below N. Then `C2/C(=O)` places C(=O) above C3. So NH and C2 are on opposite sides (trans), which is not what I want. Changing the first bond to `\` gives `N\N=C2/C(=O)`, which puts NH and C2 on the same side (cis), as drawn.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N\N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(F)c23)c1O

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH sits upward from the N, and the N=C bond runs down-right to C3. At C3, the carbonyl C2 is on the left and C3a is on the right. I take the NH on the N to be on the same side as the C2 carbonyl, which is the usual Z form stabilised by an NH···O=C hydrogen bond.

In the drawing, HN is at (350, 300) and the imine N is at (410, 335). C3 is at (410, 405), with C2 at left (350, 440) and C3a at right (470, 440). The N=C bond is vertical, so I compare the substituents on each end. The HN substituent lies to the left of the N (x = 350 against 410), and C2 lies to the left of C3. Both are on the same side, so the geometry is Z.

**SMILES.** Writing the hydrazone as `Nc/N=C3/...` with this geometry:

`OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3cccs3)c3ccccc23)c1O`

Checking the directional bonds: `N/N=C2\C(=O)` places N (the NH) "below" the first N and C(=O) "above" the C. With the `/` before N=, the NH is on the lower side of the N. After C2, the `\C(=O)` puts the carbonyl carbon on the lower side. Both are on the same side, so this is Z, as intended.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3cccs3)c3ccccc23)c1O

name: rs_0836
text:
I read the molecule as a morpholine amide on one side of a central stereocentre and a 4-(trifluoromethoxy)anilino-ethyl amide on the other.

**Reading the drawing:**
- On the left, a morpholine ring (N, two CH2, O, two CH2) is acylated through its nitrogen: N–C(=O)–CH2.
- The CH2 leads to the stereocentre, which carries a wedged CH2–cyclohexyl group (a six-carbon ring).
- The other substituent on the stereocentre is a C(=O)NH amide, followed by CH2CH2, then an NH on a para-substituted benzene ring bearing OCF3.

1. C(=O)NH
2. CH2C(=O)N
3. CH2Cy
4. H

The CH2C(=O)N branch outranks CH2Cy because its next carbon has (O,O,N) against (C,C,H). With H at the back, the sequence 1→2→3 runs right → left → top, which is clockwise, so the centre is R.

Writing the SMILES as `O=C(N1CCOCC1)C[C@@H](CC1CCCCC1)C(=O)NCCNc1ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc1`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2CO, H, CH2Cy, C(=O). Working through the permutation, `@` gives S and `@@` gives R, so `@@` is the correct symbol.

name: rs_0839
text:
The structure is a methyl 2-(benzyloxycarbonylamino)-3-aryl acrylate (a dehydroamino acid ester). The aryl group is a benzene ring carrying two adjacent nitro groups and a methyl.

**Aromatic ring.** The ring carbon attached to the vinyl group is C1. Going around the ring:
- C2 is an unsubstituted CH at the upper left.
- C3 carries the upper NO2.
- C4 carries the lower NO2.
- C5 carries the methyl.
- C6 is an unsubstituted CH.

This is a 3,4-dinitro-5-methylphenyl group.

**Chain.** The ring is attached to CH=C(NHCbz)C(=O)OCH3. The Cbz group is NH–C(=O)–O–CH2–Ph.

**Double bond geometry.** The aryl group sits at the upper left of the double bond. At the other alkene carbon, the ester points to the upper right and the NH points down. The aryl-bearing carbon is at about (215,115) and the other alkene carbon at about (325,130).
- The aryl ring carbon lies to the left of the aryl-bearing carbon, at about (215,135), which is below-left of it.
- At the other end, the ester carbon is at the upper right (390,100) and the N is below (325,200).
- So the aryl group (lower left on the left carbon) and the NH (down on the right carbon) are on the same side, which makes them cis (Z).

Writing the SMILES with the aryl on the left carbon, `c1(...)/C=C(/N...)C(=O)OC`, the aryl–C/ /C=C(/N) form means aryl and N are on the same side only if the slashes are placed correctly. Using `Ar/C=C(\N)C(=O)OC` would put aryl and N on opposite sides, so for cis I write `Ar/C=C(/NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)OC`. In `F/C=C(/F)`, the two F atoms are on the same side (cis), so the same pattern applies here and the arrangement is Z for N versus aryl.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C(NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)=C/c1cc(C)c([N+](=O)[O-])c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

Checking this string: in `C(NC...)=C/c1...` the ester carbon is written before the double bond, so the `/` after `=C` applies to the aryl. The ester carbon precedes `C` with no bond marker, so I need explicit markers. I rewrite it as:

SMILES: COC(=O)/C(NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)=C/c1cc(C)c([N+](=O)[O-])c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

Here the ester is "/ before C", meaning the ester is below-left of C, and the aryl "/ after =C" is above-right, so the ester and aryl are trans. That puts N and aryl cis, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C(NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)=C/c1cc(C)c([N+](=O)[O-])c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: rs_0896
text:
The drawing shows three parts: a pyridine carboxamide, a cyclohexane linker, and a trifluoromethylpyridine joined through sulfur.

**Pyridine ring (left).** The ring nitrogen is at the bottom left. Going around the ring:
- C2 carries the amide C(=O).
- C3 carries OH.
- C4 carries OMe.
- C5 and C6 are plain CH, and C6 is bonded to the ring nitrogen.

This gives the fragment COc1ccnc(C(=O)N...)c1O.

**Cyclohexane.** The amide NH is on one ring carbon, and the S is on the carbon one position over, so the substituents are 1,3 to each other. The bonds are plain, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

**Right pyridine.** S is attached at C2, which is adjacent to the ring nitrogen. The CF3 sits on the carbon at the bottom right. Going around from N: N1, C2 (S), C3, C4, C5 (CF3), C6. That makes the CF3 at position 5, matching the name 5-(trifluoromethyl)pyridin-2-yl.

**Assembly.** Joining the pieces:

COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2CCCC(C2)Sc2ccc(cn2)C(F)(F)F)c1O

Checking the right ring: c2ccc(cn2) is C2 (attached to S), C3, C4, C5 (bearing CF3), C6, then N closing the ring. That is correct.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2CCCC(C2)Sc2ccc(cn2)C(F)(F)F)c1O

name: rs_0891
text:
I read this as a nine-membered dilactone core (an antimycin-type scaffold) carrying a substituted picolinamide on the nitrogen.

**Core ring.** Going round the nine-membered ring: C(=O), ring O, CH(CH3), CH(O-isobutyryl), CH(CH2Ph), C(=O), ring O, CH2, CH(NH). The last CH closes back onto the first C(=O).

**Substituents.**
- The CH(NH) carbon bears an amide NH linked to C(=O) of a pyridine. The pyridine has the amide at C2, a 4-fluorobenzoyloxy group at C3, and OMe at C4. The ring N sits next to C2.
- The CH next to the ring O carries a methyl on a wedge.
- The next CH carries the isobutyrate ester, O–C(=O)–CH(CH3)2, on a hashed bond.
- The CH after that carries the benzyl group on a wedge.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned each of the four stereocentres from the wedge and hash geometry in the drawing, with the implicit H opposite the wedged or hashed substituent where relevant:
- CH(NH): hashed N, giving [C@H].
- CH(CH2Ph): wedged benzyl, giving [C@H].
- CH(O-isobutyryl): hashed O, giving [C@@H].
- CH(CH3): wedged methyl, giving [C@H].

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@H]2COC(=O)[C@H](Cc3ccccc3)[C@@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)[C@H](C)OC2=O)c1OC(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1

name: rs_0898
text:
I read the structure region by region, from left to right.

**Left fragment (benzimidazolone):** The N-methyl benzimidazol-2-one has Me on one N and the piperidin-4-yl group on the other N. The chlorine sits on the benzene ring at the carbon adjacent to the ring carbon bonded to the piperidinyl-bearing N. In the drawing, the ring carbon bonded to that N is at the top right of the benzene, followed by a CH, and then the C–Cl carbon. So Cl is meta to that N-bearing carbon, which is position 6 of the benzimidazolone when the piperidinyl N is N1.

**Middle:** The piperidine nitrogen carries a three-carbon chain (propyl) that ends on N1 of the pyrazole.

**Right fragment (tetrahydropyrazolo[4,3-c]pyridine):**
- N1 is attached to the propyl chain and is bonded to N2, which is double-bonded to C3.
- C3 bears the 4-CF3-phenyl group.
- C3 is bonded to C3a, which is double-bonded to C7a, and C7a is bonded to N1.
- C3a connects to CH2 (C4), then N5 carrying the SO2Me, then CH2 (C6), then CH2 (C7), then back to C7a.

**SMILES assembly:**
- Benzimidazolone: CN1C(=O)N(C2CCN(CCCn3nc(-c4ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc4)c4c3CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)C4)CC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21
- Check on the Cl position: N(pip) is attached to c2, then c (CH), then c(Cl), then cc, then c21, which bears N-Me. The CH lies between the N-bearing carbon and the C–Cl carbon, matching the drawing.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)N(C2CCN(CCCn3nc(-c4ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc4)c4c3CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)C4)CC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21

name: rs_0899
text:
The molecule is a methyl ester with a 7-methylindazole on one end and a piperidine-linked dihydroquinazolinone on the other.

**Indazole.** The ring has N and NH in the five-membered ring. The CH= carbon is attached to N, which is double-bonded in the drawing, and the NH sits on the benzo ring at position 1. The methyl group is at C7, next to the C7a carbon bearing NH. The CH2 linker is attached at C5.

**Chain.** From the indazole, CH2 leads to CH(C(=O)OCH3), then CH2, then C(=O) bonded to the piperidine nitrogen.

**Piperidine and quinazolinone.** The piperidine C4 carries N3 of the 3,4-dihydroquinazolin-2(1H)-one. That ring is N3–C(=O)–NH–aryl, with the aryl ring closing back through CH2 to N3.

**Indazole SMILES.** Cc1cc(C...)cc2cn[nH]c12. Here c1 bears the methyl (C7), then cH (C6), then c(CH2...) (C5), then cH (C4), then c2 (C3a), then cH (C3), then n (N2), then [nH] (N1), and finally c12 (C7a). The ring fusion is consistent.

**Full SMILES.** COC(=O)C(Cc1cc(C)c2[nH]ncc2c1)CC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)N1Cc2ccccc2NC1=O

The stereocentre at the CH is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: COC(=O)C(Cc1cc(C)c2[nH]ncc2c1)CC(=O)N1CCC(CC1)N1Cc2ccccc2NC1=O

name: rs_0897
text:
I read the drawing as a 2-tert-butyl-3-methylimidazolidin-4-one trifluoroacetate salt.

- **Ring:** a five-membered imidazolidinone. Going round it: N(CH3), then C(=O), then CH2, then NH, then CH(t-Bu), which closes back to the N-methyl nitrogen.
- **Stereocentre:** the tert-butyl group on the CH carbon is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. From the H side, the substituents N(Me), t-Bu and NH run counterclockwise. Reordering to the SMILES neighbour order (NH, H, N(Me), t-Bu) is an odd permutation, so the centre is written `@@`.
- **Counter-ion:** "•TFA" is trifluoroacetic acid, written as a separate component.

SMILES: CN1C(=O)CN[C@@H]1C(C)(C)C.OC(=O)C(F)(F)F

name: rs_0901
text:
The drawing shows a central CH carbon bonded to three groups: a piperidine nitrogen, a 2,3-dimethoxyphenyl ring, and a hydroxy-benzodioxole ring.

**Dimethoxyphenyl ring.** The ring carbon attached to CH is C1. The adjacent carbon, C2, carries OCH3 (lower right). The next carbon, C3, carries H3CO (left). So the ring is 2,3-dimethoxyphenyl.

**Benzodioxole ring.** The ring carbon attached to CH is bonded to a carbon bearing HO. The benzodioxole oxygens sit on the right side, fused to the ring through the two carbons on that side. Numbering the ring atoms:
- a1 is attached to CH.
- a2 carries OH (bottom left).
- a3 is the bottom CH.
- a4 carries O (bottom right).
- a5 carries O (upper right).
- a6 is the top CH, bonded back to a1.

**Piperidine.** The nitrogen is attached to the CH and closes a six-membered ring of five carbons.

**SMILES assembly.** Writing the CH first with its three substituents gives:

C(N1CCCCC1)(c1cccc(OC)c1OC)c1cc2OCOc2cc1O

Checking the benzodioxole portion, c1cc2OCOc2cc1O reads as:
- c1 (a1, attached to CH)
- c (a6, CH)
- c2 (a5, with O)
- OCO (the dioxole bridge)
- c2 (a4)
- c (a3, CH)
- c1O (a2, with OH)

This matches the drawing. The CH is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: COc1cccc(C(N2CCCCC2)c2cc3OCOc3cc2O)c1OC

name: rs_0900
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an oxindole (isatin-type) core.

**Biphenyl part.** The upper-left ring carries the CO2H group. It is joined to a second ring that bears an OH ortho to the biaryl bond and the NH–N= group on the carbon next to the OH. So the second ring has the aryl at position 1, OH at position 2 and the hydrazine NH at position 3. The carboxylic acid is meta on the first ring, giving a 3'-carboxylic acid.

**Hydrazone.** The chain is Ar–NH–N=C3, where C3 is the oxindole carbon. No cis/trans geometry is clearly specified, so I add no stereo marking.

**Oxindole part.** The ring contains C3(=N), C2(=O), N1 and the fused benzene ring. N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. The SO2Me group is on the benzo ring at position 6, which is the carbon meta to C3a and para to C4. In the drawing, the benzo ring runs from C3a (attached to C3) through C4 and C5, then C6 (bearing SO2Me), then C7, to C7a (attached to N).

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c2cccc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(C)c4)c5cc(S(C)(=O)=O)ccc35)c2O
- Oxindole ring closure: C3 is bonded to C3a (c35), and the ring runs c5 (C7a), c (C7), c(SO2Me) (C6), c (C5), c (C4), c35 (C3a), which places SO2Me at C6 as drawn.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c2cccc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(C)c4)c5cc(S(C)(=O)=O)ccc35)c2O

name: rs_0903
text:
The drawing shows a central benzene ring with two substituents in a meta relationship. One is N(CH2CH3)2. The other is a nitrogen bearing two p-tolyl groups.

Reading the central ring: the top-right carbon carries the diethylamino group. The ring's left-lower carbon, reached through the lower-left vertex, carries the diarylamine nitrogen. The ring vertices run top (340,10), upper right (435,10), right (435,65), lower right (410,120), lower left (340,125), left (310,65). The diethylamino attaches at (435,65), and the diarylamine N attaches at (340,125). Going from (435,65) to (410,120) to (340,125), these two attachment points are separated by one intervening vertex, so the substitution is meta.

Each outer ring is a benzene with a methyl group para to the nitrogen, so both are p-tolyl groups.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1cccc(c1)N(c1ccc(C)cc1)c1ccc(C)cc1

name: rs_0902
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl-4-carboxamide. One phenyl ring carries SO2NH2 at the ortho position, and the other ring is the para-substituted benzoyl ring.

The benzoyl C=O is attached through NH to a central benzene ring. That ring has the following substituents:
- C1 bears the NH of the amide.
- C2 bears C(=O)NH-(5-chloropyridin-2-yl).
- NH2 sits on the carbon para to C1. Tracing the ring from the NH-bearing carbon at top left, the top right carbon is next, then the right carbon carrying NH2, then the bottom carbon (C3), then C2 bearing the carbonyl. So NH2 is on C4 relative to C1, which makes it meta to the carbonyl-bearing carbon.

The pyridine has N adjacent to the carbon attached to NH, which is C2. Cl is on C5, para to C2 across the ring.

SMILES for the central ring: c1(NC(=O)...)ccc(N)cc1C(=O)N...

Full SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1-c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cn1

Checking the central ring: c1 (NH-bearing), c, c, c(N), c, c1 (C=O-bearing). The ring atom after c(N) is a CH, then the carbonyl-bearing carbon, so NH2 is para to the amide-NH carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1-c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(N)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cn1

name: rs_0904
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring fused to a five-membered 1,3-dioxole ring. The ring carbon bearing the ethyl and methyl groups sits between the two oxygens, and a hydroxyl group is on the benzene ring.

Benzene ring positions, read from the drawing:
- Two adjacent carbons on the right side of the ring carry the oxygens: the upper one bonds to the top O, the lower one to the bottom O.
- The OH is on the lower-left carbon of the ring.
- Going around from the lower O-bearing carbon, the next carbon is the one at the bottom of the ring (CH). The OH carbon follows it.
- The OH carbon is therefore meta to the lower O-bearing carbon and para to the upper O-bearing carbon.

The dioxole carbon has an ethyl and a methyl group. It is not drawn with wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES: CCC1(C)Oc2ccc(O)cc2O1

Check: ring atoms are c2 (attached to O), c, c, c(O), c, c2 (attached to O1). The first aromatic carbon is bonded to the O at the start, and the last aromatic carbon is bonded to the closing O. The OH carbon is the fourth atom, which is para to the first carbon and meta to the last. This matches the drawing, in which the OH carbon is para to the upper O-bearing carbon.

SMILES: CCC1(C)Oc2ccc(O)cc2O1

name: rs_0906
text:
The drawing shows a quinoline core with these substituents:

- **C4:** an NH linked to a pyridin-4-yl group.
- **C3:** fluorine.
- **C2:** a 2-fluorophenyl group.
- **C7:** an NHMe group.

Ring layout: N1 is at the bottom of the pyridine ring of the quinoline, C2 carries the aryl group, C3 carries F, and C4 carries the NH-pyridyl. The benzo ring runs C4a, C5, C6, C7 (NHMe), C8, C8a. The NHMe sits on the left-hand carbon at the bottom of the benzo ring, which is C7, adjacent to C8 and then C8a (bonded to N1).

SMILES, written as 4-(pyridin-4-ylamino), 3-F, 2-(2-fluorophenyl), 7-(methylamino):

CNc1ccc2c(Nc3ccncc3)c(F)c(-c3ccccc3F)nc2c1

Check on the benzo ring: c1 (C7, with NHMe), c (C6), c (C5), c2 (C4a), then c(NHPy) (C4), c(F) (C3), c(Ar) (C2), n (N1), c2 (C8a), c1 (C8). The ring closures are consistent with this.

SMILES: CNc1ccc2c(Nc3ccncc3)c(F)c(-c3ccccc3F)nc2c1

name: rs_0907
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring, an amide linker, and a spiro-fused macrocyclic diester.

**Pyridine ring.** The nitrogen is at the bottom left. The carbon attached to the carboxamide (C2) is next to it, then C3 bearing OH, then C4 bearing OMe. The remaining two ring carbons are C5 and C6, and C6 is bonded to N.

**Amide.** C2 carries C(=O)NH, and the NH is bonded to the CH of the large ring.

**Large ring.** Going around from the CH:
- CH, then CH2, then O, then C(=O), then CH2, then the spiro carbon.
- From the spiro carbon: CH2, then C(=O), then O, then CH2, and back to the CH.
- This gives 10 ring atoms: CH, CH2, O, C(=O), CH2, C(spiro), CH2, C(=O), O, CH2.
- The spiro carbon is also part of a cyclohexane ring.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Pyridine part: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2COC(=O)CC3(CCCCC3)CC(=O)OC2)c1O
- Ring closure check: c1 (C4, OMe), c (C5), c (C6), n, c (C2, with the amide), c1O (C3, OH). The ring closes correctly.
- Macrocycle part: C2 (CH) – C – O – C(=O) – C – C3(CCCCC3) – C – C(=O) – O – C – back to C2. This is correct.

No stereo is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2COC(=O)CC3(CCCCC3)CC(=O)OC2)c1O

name: rs_0909
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Thiophene:** a thiophene ring attached through its 2-position to C2 of the imidazole.
- **Imidazole:** C2 carries the thiophene. N3 (unlabeled ring N, top) connects to C4, which bears the CH2CH2NH chain. C5 bears the 4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group and is bonded to N1(H) at the bottom.
- **Side chain:** the imidazole C4 carries CH2CH2–NH–S(=O)(=O)–, and the sulfonyl sulfur is bonded to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Piperazine:** the other piperazine nitrogen carries an n-butyl group (4 carbons).

SMILES, written as the imidazole c1(CCNS(=O)(=O)N2CCN(CCCC)CC2)nc(-c3cccs3)[nH]c1-c1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1:

SMILES: CCCCN1CCN(CC1)S(=O)(=O)NCCc1nc(-c2cccs2)[nH]c1-c1ccc(cc1)C(F)(F)F

name: rs_0910
text:
The structure is a Boc-protected thyronamine analog (a T2-type compound), read as follows.

**Left ring:** a phenol with the OH at the para position relative to the ether oxygen, and an iodine ortho to the OH (meta to the oxygen). Numbering from the ether-bearing carbon (C1), the iodine sits at C3 and the OH at C4.

**Right ring:** the ether oxygen is attached at C4, with iodines at C3 and C5 (both ortho to the oxygen). C1 carries the CH2CH2NH-Boc chain.

**Chain:** two CH2 groups, then NH, then Boc, which is C(=O)OC(C)(C)C.

**SMILES assembly:**
- Left ring: Oc1ccc(Oc2...)cc1I
- Right ring: c2c(I)cc(CCNC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)cc2I

Atom check on the left ring: c1 (OH-bearing) → c → c → c(O-) → c → c1(I). The ring closure puts the iodine-bearing carbon adjacent to the OH-bearing carbon. The O-bearing carbon is the fourth atom, so it is para to the OH carbon. The iodine-bearing carbon is meta to the O-bearing carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NCCc1cc(I)c(Oc2ccc(O)c(I)c2)c(I)c1

name: rs_0908
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring bearing 4-OMe and 3-OH, with a 2-carboxamide. The amide N is attached to the alpha carbon of a serine unit. That carbon carries an isopropyl ester (CO2iPr) and a CH2-O-C(=O)-CH(CH3)-CH2Ph side chain.

**Pyridine ring.** The N is at the bottom, with C2 bearing the C(=O)NH group. C3 carries OH and C4 carries OMe. Written as a SMILES fragment: c1(C(=O)N...)nccc(OC)c1O.

**Stereochemistry.** The alpha carbon has a bold wedge to the NH, so it is a defined stereocentre. The 2-methyl carbon in the side chain is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

To assign the alpha carbon, I place it at the centre with these neighbours:
- NH to the left, on a wedge (toward the viewer)
- C(=O)O above
- CH2 below
- H implied, pointing away

CIP priorities are N > C(=O)O (O,O,O) > CH2O (O,H,H) > H. With H pointing away, I read N (left) → COOR (up) → CH2 (down). Going from left to up to down is clockwise, which gives R. L-serine is S in its usual form, so this is the D-serine configuration, which is fine.

Now the SMILES. Writing the centre as N[C@H](C(=O)OC(C)C)COC(=O)..., the neighbour order is N, H, C(=O), CH2. Viewed from N, the sequence H → C(=O) → CH2 is counterclockwise for @. I need R, so I check this ordering.

With H as the second neighbour, the order N, H, COOR, CH2 is an even permutation of H, N, COOR, CH2, so the two have the same chirality sense. Looking from H, @ means N → COOR → CH2 appears counterclockwise. Looking from the opposite side (H pointing away), the same sequence appears clockwise, and that is R. So @ gives R.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)OC(C)C)COC(=O)C(C)Cc2ccccc2)c1O

name: rs_0905
text:
Reading the chain from the aldehyde end: O=CH–CH2–CH(Et)–CH2–CH(CH3)–CH3. This is 3-ethyl-5-methylhexanal.

**Stereochemistry:** C3 is the only stereocentre drawn with a wedge, and the wedge goes to the ethyl group. The implicit H therefore points away from the viewer.

CIP priorities at C3:
1. C2 is highest. Its branch leads to the CHO carbon, which carries (O,O,H).
2. C4 is next. Its branch leads to C5, which carries (C,C,H).
3. The ethyl group is below those two.
4. H is lowest.

Viewed from the front with H at the back, C2 (upper right) → C4 (upper left) → Et (down) runs counterclockwise, so C3 is S.

In the SMILES `O=CC[C@H](CC(C)C)CC`, the neighbour order at C3 is C2, H, C4, Et. The `@` symbol corresponds to S for that order.

SMILES: O=CC[C@H](CC(C)C)CC

name: rs_0911
text:
The drawing shows a coumarin (2H-chromen-2-one) core.

- **Pyranone ring:** O1 is bonded to C2, which carries the C=O. C3 bears the CH2COOH group and C4 bears the aryl group. C4a and C8a are the ring-fusion carbons.
- **Benzo ring:** C5 is an H-bearing carbon next to C4a. C6 carries the methyl group and C7 carries the Cl. C8 is an H-bearing carbon next to C8a, which is bonded to O1.
- **C4 substituent:** a phenyl ring attached at its C1, with CHO on the meta position (C3).

SMILES, written in order:

- Acid and ring: OC(=O)CC1=C(c2cccc(C=O)c2)c3cc(C)c(Cl)cc3OC1=O
- Fusion carbon C4a (written `c3`) is followed by C5 (`c`), then C6 with methyl (`c(C)`), then C7 with Cl (`c(Cl)`), then C8 (`c`), then C8a (`c3`), which closes the benzo ring and connects to O1.
- O1 connects to C2 (`C1=O`), which closes the pyranone ring back to C3.

The atoms match the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)CC1=C(c2cccc(C=O)c2)c3cc(C)c(Cl)cc3OC1=O

name: rs_0912
text:
The drawing shows a quinoline core with these substituents:

- C4 carries an NH linked to a pyridin-4-yl group.
- C3 carries F.
- C2 carries a 2-fluorophenyl group.
- C7 carries OMe.
- The ring nitrogen is N1.

Writing the SMILES from C4: C4(Nc1ccncc1) is bonded to C3(F), then C2(-c2ccccc2F), then N1, then C8a, which leads around the benzo ring to C7 (OMe), C6, C5 and C4a, which closes back to C4.

SMILES: COc1ccc2c(c1)nc(-c1ccccc1F)c(F)c2Nc1ccncc1

Check of the benzo ring: c1 (C7, bearing OMe), c (C6), c (C5), c2 (C4a), then c(c1) is C8a, which closes the ring to C7 through C8. Written out, "COc1ccc2c(c1)nc..." gives C7, C6, C5, C4a, C8a, with C8 as the branch (c1) closing to C7. C8a is then bonded to n (N1), then c (C2) with its aryl group, then c(F) (C3), then c2 (C4) with the NH-pyridyl, closing to C4a. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccc2c(c1)nc(-c1ccccc1F)c(F)c2Nc1ccncc1

name: rs_0914
text:
The structure is a terphenyl sulfonamide of glycine, read in four parts.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying a phenoxy group (O–Ph) at the position ortho to the bond to the next ring.
- **Middle and right rings:** two para-linked benzene rings, so the chain is a 2-phenoxyphenyl–phenyl–phenyl terphenyl. The last ring bears the sulfonyl group.
- **Sulfonamide:** the sulfonyl S(=O)(=O) is bonded to a nitrogen. That nitrogen carries a 3-(trifluoromethyl)benzyl group and a CH2COOH group.
- **Benzyl ring:** the CF3 sits meta to the CH2 attachment, consistent with the drawing.

Assembled as SMILES: OC(=O)CN(Cc1cccc(c1)C(F)(F)F)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1Oc1ccccc1

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN(Cc1cccc(c1)C(F)(F)F)S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1Oc1ccccc1

name: rs_0913
text:
The drawing shows a [1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-b]pyridazin-3-one bicycle.

**Five-membered ring.** The atoms are N (upper left, double bonded to the ring-fusion carbon), N2 (bearing the benzyl group), C3 (the C=O), N4 (ring-fusion nitrogen, bonded to the pyridazine N), and C8a (the ring-fusion carbon).

**Six-membered ring.** Starting from the fusion carbon C8a, the atoms are CH, then C(aryl) carrying the 4-chlorophenyl group, then C(Cl), then N, then N4 (the fusion nitrogen).

**Substituents.** N2 carries a CH2 linked to a 4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring. The carbon next to the pyridazine N bears Cl, and the adjacent carbon bears the 4-chlorophenyl.

**SMILES construction.** Writing the five-membered ring first: O=C1N(Cc2ccc(cc2)C(F)(F)F)N=C3C=C(c4ccc(Cl)cc4)C(Cl)=NN13

Ring check:
- C1 is the carbonyl carbon, bonded to N2 (the benzylated nitrogen).
- N2 is bonded to N=, which double bonds to C3 (the fusion carbon).

The drawing is a copolymer of two norbornane repeat units, written with subscripts 42 and 58. In each unit the ring is attached to the chain at two adjacent carbons (the two bonds leaving the top of the ring). The substituent sits on a carbon of the lower part of the ring.

**Ring skeleton.** Each unit is a norbornane drawn as a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane. Its top two carbons, C2 and C3, are the polymer-chain carbons. C1 and C4 are the bridgeheads, joined by the one-carbon bridge C7. C5 and C6 form the lower two-carbon bridge, and the substituent is on C5.

**Unit 1 (42).** The substituent is CH2–C(CF3)2OH, where C(CF3)2OH is the carbon bearing two CF3 groups and the hydroxyl.

**Unit 2 (58).** The substituent is CH2–C(CF3)2–O–CH2–O–C2H5, an ethoxymethyl ether.

**SMILES for each unit.** Treat the polymer as a chain with the two chain carbons as connection points, `*C1C2CC(C1*)C(C2)...`. Here the chain carbons are C2 and C3, attached to bridgeheads C1 and C4 respectively.

- Unit 1: `*C1C2CC(C1*)C(CC(O)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F)C2`
- Unit 2: `*C1C2CC(C1*)C(CC(OCOCC)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F)C2`

Check on the ring closures, using `*C1C2CC(C1*)C(R)C2`:
- C(a) is the chain carbon, with ring label 1.
- C2 is a bridgeheads carbon, with ring label 2.
- C is the bridge carbon C7.
- C(...) is the other bridgehead; its branch `(C1*)` is the second chain carbon, which closes ring 1 with the first chain carbon.
- C(R) is C5, carrying the substituent.
- The final C2 is C6, which closes to the first bridgehead.

This gives a bicycle in which the bridgeheads are connected by C7 and by the C5–C6 bridge, and by the C2–C3 bridge. The ring is valid.

I write the copolymer with the two units in sequence, using the subscripts as repeat counts.

text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left:** two benzyl groups (each a CH2 on a phenyl ring) are attached to one nitrogen, which is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Middle:** the ring carbon opposite the nitrogen carries a CH2 that leads to the stereocentre.
- **Stereocentre:** this carbon bears an OC2H5 group on a bold wedge, a CO2Et group, the CH2 and an implicit H.
- **Right:** the ester is C(=O)OEt.

The molecule is therefore ethyl 3-[4-(dibenzylamino)phenyl]-2-ethoxypropanoate.

**Stereochemistry.** The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are OEt > CO2Et > CH2Ar > H.

- The OEt group points down on the wedge, so it is toward the viewer, and the H is at the back.
- Viewed from the front, OEt (down), then CO2Et (upper right), then CH2Ar (upper left) runs counterclockwise.
- With H pointing away, counterclockwise means S.

In the SMILES `CCO[C@@H](Cc1...)C(=O)OCC`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is O, H, CH2, C(=O). Working through the permutation, `@@` corresponds to S for this order.

SMILES: CCO[C@@H](Cc1ccc(N(Cc2ccccc2)Cc2ccccc2)cc1)C(=O)OCC

name: rs_0936
text:
The drawing shows a dibenz[b,e]oxepine core (the olopatadine scaffold) with a piperidylidene group and a propanoic acid chain.

**Dibenzoxepine core.** The upper benzene ring carries a CH2OH group. It is bonded to an oxygen, and the oxygen connects through a CH2 to the lower benzene ring. Both benzene rings are bonded to the exocyclic alkene carbon, which closes the seven-membered ring.

**Piperidine and side chain.** The exocyclic double bond joins the core to C4 of a piperidine ring. The piperidine nitrogen bears a CH2CH2COOH chain, which gives the 3-(piperidin-1-yl)propanoic acid fragment.

**Substituent position on the upper ring.** Label the upper ring atoms as follows:
- a1: the carbon bonded to O
- a2: the carbon bonded to the alkene carbon
- a3: the CH next to a2
- a4: the carbon bearing CH2OH
- a5: the CH at the top right
- a6: the CH next to a1

CH2OH is on a4, which is para to a1 (the carbon bonded to O). This is the same position as the carboxymethyl group in olopatadine, where the CH2COOH is para to the O-bearing carbon.

**SMILES.** Writing the upper ring starting from the alkene-bound carbon:
- C1(=C2CCN(CCC(=O)O)CC2) is the alkene carbon.
- c2cc(CO)ccc2OCc2ccccc12 is the remainder, where c2 is a2, then a3, a4 (CH2OH), a5, a6, a1 (O), then OCH2, then the lower benzene ring closing back to the alkene carbon.

Full SMILES: OCc1ccc2OCc3ccccc3C(=C3CCN(CCC(=O)O)CC3)c2c1

No stereochemistry is specified in the drawing, so none is included.

SMILES: OCc1ccc2OCc3ccccc3C(=C3CCN(CCC(=O)O)CC3)c2c1

name: rs_0932
text:

- **Central ring:** a 9-membered dilactone. Going round it: C(=O), O, CH(CH3), CH(O-acyl), CH(CH2Ph), C(=O), O, CH2, CH(NH). That is 9 ring atoms.
- **Ester group:** the O-acyl substituent is a cyclopentanecarbonyl ester.
- **Benzyl group:** the CH(CH2Ph) carbon carries a benzyl substituent.
- **Stereochemistry:** four stereocentres have wedges or hashes.

  - The CH(O-acyl) carbon has a hashed bond to O.
  - The CH(CH3) carbon has a wedged CH3.

text:

name: rs_0947
text:
The drawing shows a benzodioxole: a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring containing two oxygens and a central carbon (C2). That C2 carries two CH(CH3)2 groups, and the benzene ring carries an OH.

To place the OH, I numbered the benzene ring from the drawing. The upper fused carbon is attached to the top O, and the lower fused carbon is attached to the bottom O. The top-left vertex of the ring is bonded to the upper fused carbon, and the OH sits on the left-lower vertex. Going around the ring: top (CH), upper-right fused carbon C3a, lower-right fused carbon C7a, bottom (CH), lower-left carbon bearing the OH, upper-left CH, and back to the top. The OH carbon is therefore adjacent to the bottom CH, which is adjacent to the lower fused carbon. That makes the OH at position 5 of the benzodioxole.
