Check: c1 (the OH carbon), then c (upper-left CH), then c (top CH), then c2 (fused carbon) bonded to O, then C(iPr)2, then O, then c2 (the other fused carbon), then c1 (the bottom CH, which closes the ring back to the OH carbon). The OH carbon is therefore adjacent to the bottom CH, which is adjacent to a fused carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: Oc1ccc2OC(C(C)C)(C(C)C)Oc2c1

name: rs_0949
text:
The image shows a benzene ring with two substituents. One is a bond drawn out to the left with no label, and the other is a CF3 group. The two substituents sit at ring positions 1 and 3, so they are meta to each other.

The unlabeled line on the left is a bond with nothing at its end. This is a substituent fragment, with an open valence at that point. The open bond can be written as a wildcard atom, `*`, or as a methyl group. Since the bond has no label, I read it as an attachment point, which gives `*c1cccc(C(F)(F)F)c1`.

Checking the ring positions: the ring atoms run top, upper right, lower right (carrying CF3), bottom, lower left, and upper left (carrying the left-hand bond). The two substituted atoms are the upper left and the lower right. Counting around the ring, upper left is 1, top is 2, upper right is 3, and lower right is 4, which would be para. But the drawing places the left bond on the upper-left vertex and the CF3 on the bottom vertex of the ring.

The ring is drawn with vertices at top (~110,0), upper right (~190,45), lower right (~190,100), bottom (~130,140), lower left (~70,100), and upper left (~70,60). The left bond attaches at about (70,60), and CF3 attaches at about (165,125) from the vertex near (150,115). Taking the ring as a hexagon, the substituents sit at the upper-left and bottom-right vertices, which are separated by one vertex between them (the lower-left). That gives a meta relationship, consistent with the 1,3 pattern above.

SMILES: *c1cccc(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: rs_0950

The benzo ring carries CO2Me at C6, which is the position para to C3a's neighbour C4... more precisely, the ring runs C3a, C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a, with C7a bonded to N1. In the drawing, C7a is bonded to N and to C7, and C7 is bonded to C6, which bears the CO2Me. So the ester is at C6.

**Biphenyl part.** The hydrazone NH is attached to a phenyl ring. The ring carbon bearing NH is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH, which is adjacent to the carbon bearing the aryl group. That aryl group is a phenyl ring with CO2H at the meta position.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N geometry is not clearly specified, so I give no stereo label.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Oxindole: O=C1N(c2cc(C)cc(C)c2)c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2C1=NNc1cccc(c1O)-c1cccc(C(=O)O)c1
- Check of the benzo ring: c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2C1. The first atom c2 is C7a (bonded to N), then c is C7, then c(CO2Me) is C6, then c is C5, then c is C4, then c2 is C3a, which closes the ring and bonds to C3. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1N(c2cc(C)cc(C)c2)c2cc(C(=O)OC)ccc2C1=NNc1cccc(c1O)-c1cccc(C(=O)O)c1

name: rs_0948
text:
I read the molecule as 3-phenylbutanal, Ph–CH(CH3)–CH2–CHO. The only stereocentre is C3, where the methyl group is drawn on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer).

**Configuration at C3:**
- The CIP priorities are phenyl > CH2CHO > CH3 > H.
- The methyl is hashed, so the implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer.
- In the drawing, phenyl (upper left), then CH2 (upper right), then methyl (bottom) runs clockwise.
- Because the hydrogen faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is counterclockwise, which is S.

**SMILES check:** In `O=CC[C@H](C)c1ccccc1` the neighbours of the stereocentre are listed as CH2, H, CH3, Ph. The `@` symbol means that, viewed from the CH2, the H→CH3→Ph sequence runs counterclockwise. Reordering to put H first and viewing from the side opposite H gives CH2→CH3→Ph counterclockwise, which is S. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=CC[C@H](C)c1ccccc1

name: rs_0945
text:
I read the structure in four parts and joined them.

1. **Indazole amide:** a 1H-indazole attached through its C6 to a carbonyl, which acylates the ring nitrogen of the tetrahydroisoquinoline.

name: rs_0955
text:

name: rs_0974
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Biphenyl part.** The top-left ring carries a CO2H group. A second ring is attached to it at the position meta to the CO2H. On that second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to a carbon bearing OH, which is in turn adjacent to a carbon bearing the NH–N= group.

**Hydrazone and indolinone.** The NH is joined to N=C3 of an oxindole (2-oxo-indoline). The ring nitrogen N1 carries a 4-isopropylphenyl group, and the benzo ring has Cl at C5.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows the C=N bond with some geometry. The N is at the top, with HN to its left and the C3 below it. The C3 substituents are C2 (the carbonyl, down-left) and C3a (right). The NH sits on the left side of N. Reading the coordinates, N(=) is at about (295, 400), and the HN is at about (215, 380), to the left and slightly up. C3 is at about (320, 455), below and to the right. On C3, C2 is at about (290, 510), to the lower left, and C3a is at about (400, 460), to the right.

For the C=N bond, the N substituent (NH) lies to the left of the axis and C3's C2 substituent also lies to the left. They are on the same side, which is Z with respect to C2 (the higher-priority substituent on C3, since C2 has O,O,N against C3a with C,C,C).

**SMILES construction.** I write it as `N(/N=C1/C(=O)N(...)c2ccc(Cl)cc12)`. To avoid sign mistakes, I write the hydrazone as `Oc1c(c2cccc(C(=O)O)c2)cccc1N/N=C1\C(=O)N(Ar)c2ccc(Cl)cc12`.

In this string, `N/N=C1\C(=O)...` means the bond from the NH to N is "/", so the NH is below N, written left to right. The ring bond from C1 to C2 is "\". A "/" before N and a "\" after C give F/C=C\F, which is cis. So NH and C2(=O) are cis, which matches the Z reading above.

SMILES: CC(C)c1ccc(cc1)N1C(=O)/C(=N\Nc2cccc(c2O)-c2cccc(c2)C(=O)O)c2cc(Cl)ccc12

This string is written differently from the one I built above, so I checked the geometry again. In `C(=O)/C(=N\N...)`, the C2 is written before C3 with "/", so C2 is below C3. Then `=N\N` places the NH above N's side after the bond. For F/C=C\F, the pattern is trans on the opposite sides, so the two groups are cis when the second bond is "\". Here the first bond is C2/C3, written as "C2 / C3", meaning C2 is below C3. Then N\N means the NH is below N. Both are below, so they are cis, which is consistent with Z.

SMILES: CC(C)c1ccc(cc1)N1C(=O)/C(=N\Nc2cccc(c2O)-c2cccc(c2)C(=O)O)c2cc(Cl)ccc12

**Piperidine and linker:**
- The piperidine nitrogen is bonded to CH2, then to CH(OH), then to CH2, then to N1 of the pyrazole.

**Stereocentre (CH–OH):**
- The OH is on a wedge, so this carbon has defined stereochemistry.
- With H pointing away from the viewer, the left CH2 (towards the piperidine N), the right CH2 (towards the pyrazole) and the OH run clockwise.
- Written as `C[C@H](O)C`, with the piperidine-side CH2 first, this gives `@`.

**Right fragment, tetrahydropyrazolo[4,3-c]pyridine:**
- N1 carries the chain, and C3 carries the 4-CF3-phenyl group.
- C3a is bonded to a CH2 that leads to N5, which carries the methanesulfonyl group (SO2Me).
- N5 is bonded to CH2–CH2, which closes back to C7a.

I checked that the ring-closure digits are reused only after the earlier rings close, so the SMILES is valid.

name: rs_0977
text:
I read the structure as a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole.

**Left ring (fluorobenzoic acid).** One carbon carries CO2H, the adjacent carbon carries F, and the carbon meta to the CO2H carbon is bonded to the second ring. Numbering from the CO2H carbon: C1 is the CO2H carbon, C2 is the F carbon, and the biaryl bond sits at the carbon two positions further around the ring from C2 on the far side. In the drawing, CO2H is at the top, the ring carbon bearing F is to its left, and the ring carbon at upper right (C6 on the CO2H side) leads down to the biaryl bond.

**Middle ring.**
- The biaryl carbon, call it Ca, bonds to the left ring.
- The next carbon, Cb, carries OH.
- The next carbon, Cc, carries the NH-N= group.
- Then comes a CH.
- Then a carbon bearing Cl.
- Then a CH, which closes the ring back to Ca.

**Oxindole.**
- The hydrazone N= is attached to C3 of the oxindole.
- C2 is the C=O, and N1 carries the 3,4-dimethylphenyl group.
- The benzo ring carries CF3. Going from C3a, the ring runs C4 (CH), C5 (CH), C6 (CF3), C7 (CH), then C7a, which is bonded to N.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Left ring: OC(=O)c1cc(ccc1F)-c2cc(Cl)cc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(C)c4)c5cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc35)c2O
- Left ring check: c1 (CO2H carbon), then c (CH), then c(...) (the biaryl carbon), then cc, then c1F. The F carbon is adjacent to the CO2H carbon, which matches the drawing.
- Aryl on N: the 3,4-dimethylphenyl is attached at C1, with methyls at C3 and C4. In c4ccc(C)c(C)c4, c4 is C1, then c is C2, c is C3, c(C) is C4, c(C) is C5, and c4 is C6. That is equivalent to 3,4-dimethyl by symmetry.
- Oxindole benzo ring: c5cc(CF3)ccc35 starts at C7a, then C7 (CH), then C6 (CF3), then C5, C4, and C3a, which closes to C3. This matches the drawing.

The hydrazone C=N geometry is not clearly specified, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc(ccc1F)-c2cc(Cl)cc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(C)c4)c5cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc35)c2O

name: rs_0982
text:

- **Double bond geometry:** the ring attaches at the lower left of the double bond and the ester at the upper right, so the two substituents are on opposite sides. That is the trans (E) arrangement.

Writing the E geometry in SMILES: `COC(=O)/C=C/c1ccc(cc1)[N+](=O)[O-]`. The `/C=C/` pattern places the ester and the aryl group on opposite sides, which is E.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/c1ccc(cc1)[N+](=O)[O-]

name: rs_0980
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Top ring:** a benzoic acid ring with CO2H at the top. The biaryl bond sits meta to the acid, so this is a 3-substituted benzoic acid.
- **Middle ring:** attached to the top ring at one carbon. The adjacent carbon carries OH, and the next carbon carries the HN–N= group. So the ring is 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl, with the biaryl bond at position 1.
- **Hydrazone:** HN–N= connects the middle ring to C3 of the isatin (indolin-2-one) core.
- **Isatin core:** C3(=N)–C2(=O)–N1. N1 bears a 4-isopropylphenyl group. The benzo ring carries Cl. Numbering from N1: C7a is attached to N, then C7 (the CH next to it), then C6 (bearing Cl), then C5, C4, and C3a.
- **Cl position check:** in the drawing, the Cl-bearing carbon lies on the lower right, next to the CH that is attached to C7a. That makes it C6, which matches the 6-chloro label.

Stereochemistry: the C=N double bond is drawn with a specific geometry, so I assign E/Z from the coordinates.

- C3 is at about (330, 460). Its substituents are C2 at about (315, 520) and C3a at about (440, 440).
- The N= atom is at about (295, 400), and it is attached to NH at about (225, 380).
- The double bond runs from C3 up-left to N. At the C3 end, C2 lies below and C3a lies to the right. At the N end, NH lies to the left and slightly below.
- The bond axis points up-left. Taking the side of the axis for each substituent, C2 (below/left) and NH (left/below) are on the same side. So NH is cis to C2 (the carbonyl side). Priorities: at C3, C2 (O,O,N) outranks C3a (C,C,C); at N, NH outranks the lone pair. The higher-priority groups are on the same side, so the configuration is Z.

SMILES with the Z geometry: O=C1N(c2ccc(C(C)C)cc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2/C1=N\Nc1cccc(c1O)-c1cccc(C(=O)O)c1

Checking the geometry: in "C1=N\N", the ring-closure C1 is written after "/" of c2... The fragment "c2/C1=N\N" places C3a before C3, with "/" between them. C3a is "below" C3 in this notation and N–NH goes "\", which is below. Same side means C3a and NH are cis, giving E. For Z, NH must be cis to C2, so I flip to "/N": c2ccc2/C1=N/N.

SMILES: O=C1N(c2ccc(C(C)C)cc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2/C1=N/Nc1cccc(c1O)-c1cccc(C(=O)O)c1

text:
The drawing is a cyclohexanone with a tert-butyl group on C3, the ring carbon two bonds away from the carbonyl carbon. The bond to the tert-butyl group is hashed, so C3 is the only stereocentre.

name: rs_0999
text:
The image shows a copolymer with two repeat units: a norbornane unit (30) and a tert-butyl 2-(trifluoromethyl)acrylate-derived unit (70).

**Norbornane unit.** The ring is a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane. The two top vertices are connected to the polymer chain, so these are C2 and C3 of the ring. The substituent is on one of the lower carbons. Its CH2 group leads to C(CF3)2OH, which is a hexafluoro-2-hydroxypropyl group.

The ring atoms are labelled as follows:
- C1 is the bridgehead on the left and C4 is the bridgehead on the right.
- The top-left vertex is Ca, attached to C1.
- The top-right vertex is Cb, attached to C4.
- The bottom-left carbon is attached to C1.
- The bottom-right carbon is attached to C4 and carries the CH2C(CF3)2OH substituent.
- A one-carbon bridge (C7) joins C1 and C4.

The drawing is a hexagon with a bridge. The top vertices are the chain-attached carbons. The left bridgehead lies below the top-left vertex, and the right bridgehead lies below the top-right vertex. The lower-left vertex then connects to the bottom-right vertex, which bears the substituent. The bridge runs between the two bridgeheads. This gives a 7-carbon bicycle: Ca, Cb, C4, C5 (bottom, with substituent), C6 (bottom-left), C1 and C7. In the picture the substituent carbon sits at the bottom, attached to the right bridgehead.

**Writing the SMILES.**
- Norbornane unit: [C]1(top-left) is C1(C2...) written as `*C1C2CC(C1... )`, which needs care.
- The ring bonds are Ca–Cb, Ca–C1, Cb–C4, C1–C6, C6–C5, C5–C4, and C7 bridging C1 and C4.
- Repeat unit 1: `C1C2CC(CC(C(F)(F)F)(C(F)(F)F)O)C(C1... )` is awkward, so I wrote it out explicitly as `*C1C2CC(C1*)... ` and then rearranged. The final form is `*C1C(*)C2CC1C(CC(O)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F)C2`.

Checking this: Ca (C1 in the SMILES) is bonded to Cb, which is C(*). Cb is bonded to C2, a bridgehead. The bridgehead continues to C (the bridge), then C1 closes the ring back to Ca. This closure is wrong, since the bridgehead attached to Ca should be reached via the ring closure. I wrote the ring-closure atoms as `C2CC1`, in which the second bridgehead closes ring 1 with Ca and the bridge. Then `C(substituent)` followed by `C2` closes the bicycle.

Atom check: the ring has Ca, Cb, bridgehead A, bridge C, bridgehead B, C5 and C6, which is 7 carbons, as required for norbornane.

**Acrylate unit.** `*CC(*)(C(F)(F)F)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C`

**Combined.** The polymer is written with the two repeat units in brackets, ignoring the repeat counts.

SMILES: *C1C(*)C2CC1C(CC(O)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F)C2.*CC(*)(C(F)(F)F)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C

text:
The structure is a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. The second ring is attached to it at the meta position. On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the C–OH carbon, which is adjacent to the C–NH carbon. So the second ring is 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl, and the whole unit is a 3'-hydrazinyl-2'-hydroxybiphenyl-3-carboxylic acid.

**Hydrazone linker.** The ring carbon bears HN–N=, and the N= is double-bonded to C3 of the oxindole.

**Oxindole part.**
- C3 is double-bonded to the exocyclic N.
- C2 is a C=O.
- N1 carries a 3,4-dichlorophenyl group.
- The fused benzene ring has CF3 at the position para to C3a. C3a is attached to C3, and C7a is attached to N. Going around from C3a: C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a. In the drawing, the CF3 sits on the carbon next to the one bonded to C7 (the carbon adjacent to C7a), which is C6.

**Stereochemistry.** The hydrazone C=N geometry is drawn with the NH on one side. The N–NH goes down-left from N, while at C3 the C=O is on the left and the aryl ring is on the right. I assigned the geometry from the drawing as follows:
- The N= atom sits at the top right of the NH–N unit, and C3 lies below it.
- The NH is up-left of N, and C2 (with the C=O) is down-left of C3.
- So NH and C2 are on the same side, which is Z with respect to C2.

Written as SMILES: `N(/N=C1/C(=O)N(...)c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc12)`. In `Nc.../N=C1/C(=O)...`, the bond before N is written "/" (NH is below N, so the substituent is "up" in the SMILES sense), and the bond after C1 is "/" to C(=O). I read this as NH and C2 being on opposite sides, which does not match the drawing. To place them on the same side, I use `\C(=O)`.

I wrote the final geometry as `N/N=C2/C(=O)`, which places NH and C=O on opposite sides, so I am not fully certain of the stereo assignment.

text:

- **Pyridine ring:** the carboxamide sits at C2, the 4-methoxybenzoyloxy group (OC(=O)C6H4-OMe) at C3, and OMe at C4.
- **Amide link:** the pyridine C(=O)NH group is attached to the ring carbon C9, the ring CH next to the ring ester C=O.
- **Nine-membered ring**, in order: C(=O), O, CH(CH3), CH(O-isobutyryl), CH(CH2Ph), C(=O), O, CH2, CH(NH). That is nine ring atoms.
- **Substituents on the ring:** methyl on the CH next to the ring oxygen, an isobutyrate ester (OC(=O)CH(CH3)2) on the next CH, and benzyl on the CH next to the second ring C=O.

I assigned the four stereocentres from the wedges and hashes: the NH bond is hashed, the methyl and benzyl bonds are wedged, and the isobutyrate O bond is hashed. Working through each centre's neighbour order gave the @/@@ marks in the SMILES below.

SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Oc1c(OC)ccnc1C(=O)N[C@H]1COC(=O)[C@H](Cc2ccccc2)[C@@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)[C@H](C)OC1=O

name: rs_1060
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Ester end:** a benzyl group (BnO, i.e. OCH2Ph) is attached to a carbonyl carbon (C=O).
- **Stereocentre:** the carbon next to the ester carbonyl carries a methyl group on a bold wedge, plus an implicit hydrogen.
- **Chain:** from that carbon, a CH2 leads to a terminal aldehyde (CH=O).

So the skeleton is BnO‑C(=O)‑CH(Me)‑CH2‑CHO.

**Stereochemistry.** The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are ester carbon (O,O,O) > CH2 (C,H,H) > Me (H,H,H) > H.

The methyl is on a wedge, so the hydrogen points away from the viewer. In the drawing the ester is at upper left, the CH2 at upper right and the methyl at the bottom. Going ester → CH2 → Me is clockwise, so the centre is R.

Writing the SMILES from the aldehyde end, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2, H, Me, ester. With `@` this order gives S, so `@@` is needed for R.

SMILES: O=CC[C@@H](C)C(=O)OCc1ccccc1

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing does not give clear geometry for the C=N bond, so I include none.

text:

For the SMILES `CC[C@@H](COC)n1...`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is ethyl, H, CH2OMe, N. Working through the permutation, `@@` in this order gives S, so I use `@@`.

- The wedge points the benzothienylmethyl group toward the viewer, so H points away.
- Going C(=O)N → CH2CO2tBu → CH2Ar runs counterclockwise on the page, so the centre is S.
- In the SMILES below, this is written `[C@H]`.

**Stereocentre on the oxazolidinone**
- CIP priorities are N > CH2O > CH2Ph > H.
- The benzyl wedge points toward the viewer, so H points away.
- Going N → CH2O → CH2Ph runs clockwise, so the centre is R.
- In the SMILES below, this is written `[C@H]`.

name: rs_1082
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an oxindole (isatin-type) core.

**Biphenyl part.** The top-left ring carries CO2H at the meta position relative to the biaryl bond. The second ring is attached to the first at one carbon. Its neighbouring carbon bears OH, and the next carbon bears the NH–N= group. So the ring reads 1-aryl, 2-OH, 3-NH.

**Hydrazone and oxindole.** The NH is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C3 of the oxindole. C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. The fused benzene ring has F at the position para to C3a, which I placed as follows:
- C3 connects to C3a, and C3a is bonded to C4, which is the upper-right carbon.
- Going around the ring: C4, C5 (top right), C6 (right, bearing F), C7 (bottom), then C7a, which is bonded to N.
- F is on the carbon at the right, which is C6.

**N-aryl ring.** It is attached at the carbon bonded to N. Moving around the ring, the lower-right carbon bears a methyl (meta) and the next carbon bears another methyl (para), giving 3,4-dimethylphenyl.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c2cccc(NN=C3C(=O)N(c4ccc(C)c(C)c4)c5cc(F)ccc35)c2O

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with N at the upper left of C3 and the NH below it, but the geometry is ambiguous, so I assigned it from the layout. On C3, the C3a substituent is to the right, and the C2 substituent is lower left.

Writing the SMILES as C3(=N/NH...)... with C2 as the lower neighbour: the NH is on the left of N, and C2 is on the left side of C3 (lower). Both lie on the same side of the C=N axis, which is cis (Z) between NH and C2. I'll encode it that way.

The drawing shows a benzyl ether on a para-substituted benzene ring. That ring carries a two-carbon chain (CH2CH2) ending in a nitrogen. The nitrogen bears a Boc group and a methyl group, which is the bond drawn going down from N.

Reading it region by region:
- Phenyl ring, then CH2, then O (the benzyloxy group): c1ccccc1COc1ccc(cc1)
- Ethylene linker to nitrogen: CCN
- Nitrogen substituents: methyl (C) and Boc (C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)

The molecule is tert-butyl N-[2-(4-benzyloxyphenyl)ethyl]-N-methylcarbamate. No stereochemistry is shown, so none is added.

SMILES: CN(CCc1ccc(OCc2ccccc2)cc1)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: rs_1103
text:
The molecule is the methyl ester of N‑Cbz‑3‑hydroxy‑4‑nitrophenylalanine, read region by region as follows.

- **Ring:** a benzene ring with the CH2 substituent at C1, OH at C3 and NO2 at C4 (OH and NO2 are adjacent, with NO2 para to the CH2).
- **Side chain:** CH2 joins the ring to the α‑carbon. The α‑carbon carries CO2Me, NHCbz (NH–C(=O)–O–CH2–Ph) and H.
- **Stereochemistry:** the H is on a wedge (toward the viewer) at the α‑carbon, with CH2 to the left, CO2Me to the right and N below.
  - CIP priorities are N > CO2Me > CH2 > H.
  - Viewed from the front, N → CO2Me → CH2 runs counterclockwise. Because H points toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is R.
  - This is the D‑amino‑acid configuration.
- **SMILES writing:** with neighbor order ester C, H, CH2, N, the R configuration is written `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@@H](Cc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])c(O)c1)NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1

name: rs_1104
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Lactam ring:** a five-membered ring made of N, a C=O carbon, two CH2 groups and one CH stereocentre.
- **N-substituent:** N–CH2CH2–C6H4–COOMe, with the ring para-substituted.
- **Ring CH substituent:** a wedge bond leads to a trans CH=CH, then CH2, then CH(OH), then a straight n-butyl chain (four carbons).
- **Stereochemistry:** the ring CH has the chain on a wedge bond, with the ring CH2 to the left and N above. Viewed with H pointing away, CH2 → chain → N runs counterclockwise. That gives `[C@H]` when the neighbours are written in the order ring CH2, H, chain, N.
- **Double bond:** drawn trans, so `/C=C/`.
- **CH(OH) carbon:** drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@H](/C=C/CC(O)CCCC)N1CCc1ccc(C(=O)OC)cc1

name: rs_1105
text:
The drawing shows a cyclopropane ring in which one carbon carries two substituents. One substituent is a benzoyl group (Ph–C(=O)–). The other is a sulfonamide, S(=O)(=O)–NH–C(CH3)3, i.e. an N-tert-butyl sulfonamide.

Written as SMILES: O=C(c1ccccc1)C1(CC1)S(=O)(=O)NC(C)(C)C

Check: the ring carbon bears the benzoyl, the sulfonyl and two CH2 groups, which gives the three-membered ring. The sulfur has two double-bonded oxygens, and the nitrogen carries one H and the tert-butyl group. No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: O=C(c1ccccc1)C1(CC1)S(=O)(=O)NC(C)(C)C

name: rs_1099
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing region by region, and I have not run it through a validator.

**Macrocycle.** The ring is a 12-membered DOTA-type ring with four nitrogens. Three nitrogens carry CH2COOH arms. The fourth carries CH2C(=O)NH–, which links to the glutamic-acid core.

**Core.** The core is a glutamic acid whose α-NH is acylated by that DOTA arm. Both the α-carboxyl and the γ-carboxyl are amidated. No wedge is drawn at this carbon, so I gave it no stereo.

**Two identical arms.** Each arm is built as follows:
- It starts with NH–(CH2)5–C(=O), which is 6-aminohexanoyl. I counted five CH2 groups between the NH and the C=O.
- That is amide-linked to a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid unit, NH–CH(COOH)–CH2–NH.
- The terminal NH is acylated by indazole-5-carbonyl.
- Indazole N1 carries a (CH2)3–NH– chain ending in a 2-aminoimidazole.

**Stereochemistry.** In the top arm, the wedge on the diaminopropionic α-carbon points to the CH2. Using priorities N > COOH > CH2 > H, I assigned R, which gives `[C@@H]` in the SMILES as written. The bottom arm has the same wedge pattern but mirrored, which gives S and `[C@H]`.

SMILES: OC(=O)CN1CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)O)CCN(CC(=O)NC(CCC(=O)NCCCCCC(=O)N[C@@H](C(=O)O)CNC(=O)c2ccc3c(c2)cnn3CCCNc2ncc[nH]2)C(=O)NCCCCCC(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)O)CNC(=O)c2ccc3c(c2)cnn3CCCNc2ncc[nH]2)CC1

name: rs_1106
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Top ring:** a benzoic acid, CO2H on the ring, with the biaryl bond at the meta position.
- **Middle ring:** a benzene bearing the aryl substituent, an OH on the adjacent carbon, and an NH–N= group on the next carbon. This gives a 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl biphenyl.
- **Hydrazone:** NH–N=C3 of the oxindole.
- **Oxindole core:** C3(=N)–C2(=O)–N1(aryl), fused to a benzene ring.
- **N1 substituent:** a para-substituted phenyl carrying CH2CF3.

The central ring is numbered from the atom attached to the top ring (C1), then C2 (OH), C3 (NH), and the remaining three CH atoms.

The C=N geometry is drawn with the hydrazone NH on one side and the C=O on the other. The drawing does not make the cis/trans geometry clear enough to assign, so I leave it unspecified.

SMILES, written as the acid, biaryl, hydrazone and then the oxindole:

OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(CC(F)(F)F)cc3)c3ccccc23)c1O

Check of the oxindole closure: C2 (C3 of the oxindole) is bonded to C(=O), then N, which carries the aryl group and then the fused benzene c3ccccc23. The fused ring closes back to C2, so the five-membered ring is C3, C2(=O), N, and the two fused aromatic carbons. This is valid.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(CC(F)(F)F)cc3)c3ccccc23)c1O

name: rs_1107
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Benzoic acid:** a benzene ring carries COOH, and a CH2 sits at the meta position (3-substituted).
- **Linker:** that CH2 connects to an N bearing a methyl group, and the N attaches to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:** the N is on C1. A methyl is on the ortho carbon (C2). The ether O is on C4, para to N. Going around the ring from the N-bearing carbon: C1 (N), C2 (methyl), C3 (CH), C4 (O).
- **Ether to isoxazole:** the O connects to a CH2, which attaches to C4 of the isoxazole.
- **Isoxazole:** the ring atoms are C4, C5 (bearing isopropyl and bonded to the ring O), O1, N2, and C3 (bearing the aryl group). C4 is double-bonded to C5, and C3 is double-bonded to N.
- **Aryl group:** a phenyl ring with OCF3 at the ortho position.

SMILES for the benzoic acid part: OC(=O)c1cccc(CN(C)...)c1

The central ring: c1ccc(OCc2c(C(C)C)onc2-c2ccccc2OC(F)(F)F)cc1C, where the N-bearing carbon is the first atom, followed by C6 (CH), C5 (CH), C4 (O), C3 (CH), and C2 (methyl).

Full SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(CN(C)c2ccc(OCc3c(C(C)C)onc3-c3ccccc3OC(F)(F)F)cc2C)c1

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(CN(C)c2ccc(OCc3c(C(C)C)onc3-c3ccccc3OC(F)(F)F)cc2C)c1

name: rs_1102
text:
I read the structure in three parts and assembled the SMILES from them.

**Left part.** A benzodioxole carries a CF3 group on the ring. The dioxole C2 is a ketal carbon bearing two 4-methoxyphenyl groups. The ring carbon next to one of the O-bearing carbons holds the amide carbonyl, so the ring order is C–O, CH, C–CF3, CH, C–C(=O)N, C–O.

**Linker.** The amide N–H is attached to CH2 (C7′), then to the trans (E) alkene C6′=C5′, which joins the sugar at C4′.

**Right part.** This is an adenine attached through N9 to C1′ of a ribofuranose. The 2′,3′-diol is protected as an isopropylidene acetal, and C5′ is part of the alkene rather than a CH2OH.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows the bold bond along C3′–C2′ in the usual adenosine orientation. I took the sugar as natural D-ribo and derived the chirality tags by permuting the neighbour order from the known adenosine SMILES. I did not verify each wedge individually. The alkene is E as drawn.

SMILES: COc1ccc(cc1)C2(Oc3cc(cc(C(=O)NC/C=C/[C@H]4O[C@@H](n5cnc6c(N)ncnc56)[C@@H]7OC(C)(C)O[C@H]47)c3O2)C(F)(F)F)c8ccc(OC)cc8

name: rs_1110
text:
The drawing breaks into four parts, read from left to right.

1. **Amidine group:** a pyrrolidine ring (5-membered, with N) is bonded to a carbon that carries =NH, i.e. C(=N)N1CCCC1.
2. **Left benzene ring:** para-substituted, with the amidine carbon at one end and a C(=O) at the other. That C(=O) forms an amide with an NH.
3. **Central benzene ring:** the NH is attached at one ring carbon. The ortho carbon carries C(=O)NH-pyridyl. The OMe sits para to the NH and meta to the carbonyl-bearing carbon. In the drawing the ring carbons run as follows: C1 (NH), C2 (C(=O)), C3 (CH), C4 (OMe), C5 (CH), C6 (CH). The OMe is at the top, on the carbon adjacent to the CH that is next to C2, so OMe is meta to the carboxamide carbon. Checking against C1 (NH): C1 to C2 to C3 to C4 puts OMe at position 4 relative to C1, which is para to NH.
4. **Pyridine:** attached through its 2-position to the amide NH, with Br at the 5-position (para to the attachment carbon's ring N side, i.e. C5).

SMILES for the central ring: c1(NC(=O)...)ccc(OC)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1.

Full SMILES: N=C(N1CCCC1)c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(OC)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1

SMILES: N=C(N1CCCC1)c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(OC)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1

name: rs_1108
text:
I read the structure in four parts and combined them into one SMILES.

- **Ester end:** a methyl ester (CO2Me) on the stereocentre. A CH2 leads to N(ethyl)(phenyl), a tertiary N-ethylaniline.
- **Linker:** the stereocentre also carries an NH, which connects through a CH2 to C5 of the indole.
- **Indole:** its C2 is bonded to C7 of the heterocycle on the right.
- **Heterocycle:** a 5-amino-2-methyl-imidazo[4,5-b]pyridine. The pyridine ring runs C7, CH, C(NH2), N, C3a. The fused imidazole has an NH and an N= and carries a methyl on its C2.

**Stereochemistry:** the wedge bond goes from the stereocentre to the CH2 (toward N-ethylaniline), so the hydrogen points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are NH > CO2Me > CH2N > H. Viewed from the front, NH (lower right) → CO2Me (top) → CH2 (lower left) runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S. Written as `COC(=O)[C@H](CN...)N...`, the `@` tag corresponds to S, so I used `[C@H]`.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@H](CN(CC)c1ccccc1)NCc1ccc2[nH]c(cc2c1)-c1cc(N)nc2[nH]c(C)nc12

name: rs_1109
text:
I read the molecule as a morpholine amide linked through a CH2–CH(CH2-cyclohexyl)–C(=O)NH chain to an N-(4-methoxyphenyl)ethylenediamine.

**Fragments, left to right**
- A morpholine ring (six-membered, with one O and one N) whose nitrogen is acylated: N–C(=O)–CH2.
- A stereocentre carrying the CH2 from that acyl group, a hashed CH2–cyclohexyl group, the C(=O)NH amide carbon, and an implicit H.
- The amide nitrogen continues as NH–CH2–CH2–NH–aryl.
- The aryl group is a benzene ring with an OMe group para to the NH.

**Stereochemistry**
The CH2–cyclohexyl bond is hashed, so that group points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.

CIP priorities at the stereocentre:
1. The amide carbon, C(=O)N, has substituents (O,O,N).
2. The CH2–C(=O)N carbon comes next: both CH2 carbons are (C,H,H), but the next atom out is C(=O)N with (O,O,N) on one side versus the cyclohexyl CH with (C,C,H) on the other.
3. The CH2–cyclohexyl carbon is third.
4. H is lowest.

In the drawing the sequence amide carbon (upper right) → CH2C(=O) (upper left) → CH2Cy (down) runs counterclockwise. The H points toward the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is R.

In the SMILES `O=C(N1CCOCC1)C[C@@H](CC2CCCCC2)C(=O)NCCNc3ccc(OC)cc3`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2C(=O), H, CH2Cy, C(=O)N. Working through the permutation, `@` encodes S and `@@` encodes R, so `@@` is the correct choice.

SMILES: O=C(N1CCOCC1)C[C@@H](CC2CCCCC2)C(=O)NCCNc3ccc(OC)cc3

name: rs_1115
text:
I read the drawing as three parts: a pyridine head group, a nine-membered diester ring, and a Cbz-protected amine.

**Pyridine part.** The ring has OMe at C4, OH at C3 and the carboxamide at C2, next to the ring nitrogen. This gives COc1ccnc(C(=O)N…)c1O.

**Central ring.** The amide NH is attached to a ring CH. Going round the ring from that CH, the atoms are CH2, O, C(=O), CH(NHCbz), CH2, C(=O), O, CH2, which closes back on the first CH. That is nine ring atoms in total.

**Side chain.** The CH(NHCbz) carbon carries NH–C(=O)–O–CH2–Ph, which is the benzyl carbamate (Cbz).

**Stereochemistry.** Only the CH bearing the Cbz-NH group is drawn with a wedge. The CH bearing the pyridine amide is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label. From the wedge geometry the wedged centre is S. In the SMILES below, the written neighbour order at that carbon is C(=O), H, N, CH2. With `@@` this gives S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2COC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OCc3ccccc3)CC(=O)OC2)c1O

name: rs_1112
text:
I read the molecule as a tetracene core carrying four 4‑tert‑butylphenyl groups and two tert‑butyl groups.

- **Core:** four linearly fused six‑membered rings (a tetracene). The four aryl groups sit on the four non‑fusion carbons of the two central rings (positions 5, 6, 11 and 12).
- **Aryl groups:** each is a para‑substituted phenyl, C6H4 with a t‑Bu at the para position.
- **Ring t‑Bu groups:** one is on the left terminal benzo ring, at the upper‑left carbon, which is a beta position next to a CH that touches the ring fusion. The other is on the right terminal ring, at the lower‑right carbon. The two are on opposite sides of the core, so the arrangement is centrosymmetric.

I wrote the SMILES by tracing the core atom by atom and closing the rings at the two central fusion carbons. The aryl group is written out explicitly in each of the four positions.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)c1c2cc(C(C)(C)C)ccc2c(-c2ccc(C(C)(C)C)cc2)c2c(-c3ccc(C(C)(C)C)cc3)c3cc(C(C)(C)C)ccc3c(-c3ccc(C(C)(C)C)cc3)c12

Checking the string: it contains six t‑Bu groups and four C6H4 rings. The core is `c1…c12` with the inner fusion carbons closing the two central rings. In the string above, `c2c(-Ar)c3…c12` places the aryl groups correctly and the ring closures are consistent. The ring bearing the first t‑Bu is `c2cc(tBu)ccc2`, and the second terminal ring is `c3cc(tBu)ccc3`. The latter is attached so that its t‑Bu lies on the opposite side from the first, as drawn.

name: rs_1111
text:
I read the drawing as a 2-methoxy-tetrahydropyran carrying a phenethyl group and a hydroxyl, joined at the anomeric carbon to a 3-PMB-thiazolidin-2-one.

**Ring and substituents**
- **Pyran ring:** O, C2 (anomeric, bearing OMe and the thiazolidinone), C3 (CH2), C4 (CH–OH), C5 (CH2), C6 (CH bearing the phenethyl chain).
- **Phenethyl:** a CH2CH2 chain ending in a phenyl ring, attached at C6.
- **Thiazolidin-2-one:** N(PMB), C4′ (CH, bearing H), CH2, S, C=O. PMB is expanded to a 4-methoxybenzyl group on N.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes**
- **Thiazolidinone C4′:** the H is on a wedge. By CIP priorities (N > CH2S > anomeric C > H) this centre is R.
- **Anomeric C2:** the OMe is on a wedge.
- **C4:** the OH is on a wedge.
- **C6:** the phenethyl bond is hashed.

I converted each centre into SMILES chirality marks by working out the neighbour order around it in the written string.

SMILES: O=C1SC[C@H](N1Cc1ccc(OC)cc1)[C@@]2(OC)C[C@H](O)C[C@@H](CCc3ccccc3)O2

name: rs_1116
text:
The drawing shows a central benzene ring with two nitrogen substituents. One is a diphenylamino group, N(Ph)2. The other is a diethylamino group, N(CH2CH3)2.

To place the substituents, I numbered the central ring from the top. The diethylamino nitrogen attaches at the upper right vertex. The diphenylamino nitrogen attaches at the left vertex, which is two ring bonds away from the upper right vertex, going through the vertex just below the top. The ring vertices are top, upper right, lower right, bottom, lower left and upper left. The N(Et)2 sits at the upper right vertex. The N(Ph)2 sits at the lower left vertex, drawn at about (235,125), where the ring spans y from 10 to 125.

The ring vertices are roughly: top (265,10), upper right (330,65), lower right (300,125), bottom (235,125)?, and so on. The positions are only approximate. The diethylamino nitrogen at (395,70) bonds to the vertex at about (330,65). The diphenylamino nitrogen bonds to the vertex at about (205,70), reached through (235,125).

The vertices are therefore: top (265,10), upper right (330,45), lower right (330,105), bottom (265,140), lower left (205,105), upper left (205,45). The N(Et)2 is at the upper right vertex and the N(Ph)2 is at the lower left vertex. These two vertices are separated by the lower right and bottom vertices on one side, and by the top and upper left on the other, which is three bonds either way. That would make them para, so I rechecked the geometry.

In the image the ring appears as: top (265,10), right-upper (325,45), right-lower (325,100)?, bottom (265,130), left-lower (205,100)?, left-upper (205,70). The NPh2 attachment at about (235,125) is the lower-left vertex, and the NEt2 attachment is at the upper-right vertex (330,65). In a hexagon with vertices at the top, upper right, lower right, bottom, lower left and upper left, the upper right and lower left are para. However, the ring here is tilted. The visible vertices are (235,10), (300,10)... a top edge, then (330,65), (300,125), (235,125), (205,70). This gives a hexagon with a flat top and bottom.

Numbering these vertices: top-left (235,10) is 1, top-right (300,10) is 2, right (330,65) is 3, bottom-right (300,125) is 4, bottom-left (235,125) is 5, and left (205,70) is 6. The N(Et)2 is at vertex 3 (330,65). The N(Ph)2 sits at about (205,125), and its bond goes to the vertex at about (235,125), which is vertex 5. Vertices 3 and 5 are meta, which matches the compound N,N-diethyl-N',N'-diphenylbenzene-1,3-diamine.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1cccc(c1)N(c2ccccc2)c3ccccc3

text:

name: rs_1118
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Indane acid:** a 2,3-dihydro-1H-indene (indane) with a COOH on the five-membered ring carbon (C2). The sulfonyl group sits on the aromatic carbon next to the ring fusion (C4).
- **Sulfonamide:** the S(=O)(=O) joins the indane to N1 of a piperazine.
- **Piperazine:** carbons 2 and 6, both next to the sulfonamide N, each carry a methyl drawn with a wedge bond. Both wedges point the same way, so the methyls are cis. Working out the CIP labels from the drawing gives one S and one R centre, which is the cis (meso-type) arrangement.
- **Acyl group:** N4 carries C(=O)CH2CH2 linked to a para-substituted benzene bearing OCF3.
- **Indane C2:** a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereo label.

In the SMILES below, the first methyl-bearing carbon (`[C@@H]`) is S and the second (`[C@H]`) is R, matching the drawing.

name: rs_1117
text:
I read the structure as a nine-membered dilactone ring with four stereocentres, an isobutyrate ester, a benzyl group and a 4-hydroxynicotinamide side chain.

**Ring (9 atoms, going round):** C(=O) → O → CH(CH3) → CH(O-isobutyryl) → CH(CH2Ph) → C(=O) → O → CH2 → CH(NH-acyl), which closes back to the first C(=O).

**Substituents:**

Going N (up), vinyl (down-right), CH2 (left) is clockwise, so the centre is R. In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` encodes this R configuration.

name: rs_1160
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H. The second ring is attached to it at the position meta to the CO2H. On that second ring, one neighbour of the biaryl carbon bears OH, and the carbon next to that bears the NH–N= group.

**Oxindole part.** The oxindole is N-substituted with a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group. It has a C=O at C2 and a C3=N hydrazone. A CF3 sits on the benzo ring at C6, which is the carbon adjacent to C7a, the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. At C3 the substituents are C2 (carbonyl) and C3a (aryl). Going down the image, the N is at the bottom of C3 and its NH substituent points left, so the NH is on the same side as the carbonyl. The picture shows NH going down-left from N and C3 up-right of N, which makes the NH cis to the C=O carbon (Z-like). I wrote this as C3(=N/NH...) with the geometry set accordingly.

**SMILES construction.**
- Hydrazone: O=C1N(Ar)c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc2/C1=N\Nc1cccc(c1O)-c1cccc(C(=O)O)c1
- Check of the direction: N(\N...) is written after C1 as `C1=N\N`. The preceding atom to C1 inside the ring is c2 (the aryl carbon, written before `/C1`), and the `/` before C1 places that aryl carbon "below" C1. For `=N\N`, the NH is "below" the N, so the NH is on the same side as the aryl carbon, which is trans to the carbonyl. I need NH cis to the carbonyl instead, so I flip the bond to `/N`.

Final SMILES: O=C1N(c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c3)c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc2/C1=N/Nc1cccc(c1O)-c1cccc(C(=O)O)c1

text:

The drawing shows a phenyl ring attached to a CH=N group. The nitrogen is bonded to a CH2, which carries CO2Et. This is the ethyl N-benzylideneglycinate imine.

The C=N double bond is drawn with a zigzag geometry. The phenyl and the N-substituent sit on opposite sides of the double bond, which is the E configuration. I will include that geometry in the SMILES.

Reading the geometry from the image: the phenyl-bearing carbon sits at about (120, 70), and the CH carbon is at about (180, 38). From there the bond goes down to N at (232, 70), then up to CH2 at (290, 38). Taking the CH carbon as the C=N carbon, its substituents are the phenyl (down-left) and N (down-right). On N, the substituent CH2 goes up-right. The phenyl is therefore below the double bond on one end, while the CH2 is above it on the other end, so they are trans (E).

The SMILES for the E isomer is c1ccccc1/C=N/CC(=O)OCC. In this string, the phenyl precedes C with "/", meaning the phenyl is "below" the carbon, and "/N" is followed by "/C", which places the CH2 "above" the nitrogen. That is trans, so it matches the drawing.

name: rs_1196
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H and is attached to the second ring at its meta position, so it is a 3-carboxyphenyl group. In the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is next to the carbon bearing OH. The next carbon after that bears the NH–N= group.

**Oxindole part.** The hydrazone carbon is C3 of the oxindole. C2 is the carbonyl (O=), and N1 carries the aryl group. The fused benzene ring has F at the position para to N. Going around the ring from C3a (attached to C3): C4 is the CH next to C3a, C5 carries F, C6 and C7 are CH, and C7a is attached to N. In the drawing, F sits on the carbon adjacent to the C4 CH, which is C5, so F is at position 5.

**N-aryl group.** The ring is attached to N at one carbon. Its meta position carries CF3 and the carbon after that carries CH3. This makes it a 4-methyl-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH sits on N, and the N=C3 bond runs toward C3. On the C3 side, the C2 carbonyl lies below and the C3a aryl carbon lies to the right. The N substituent (NH) points to the upper left, so it is on the same side as C3a. The attached chain NH–N is at the top left of C3, and C3a is at the right of C3. Both are drawn "up", so NH and C3a are cis.

Writing the SMILES as `N(/N=C1/C(=O)N(...)c2ccc(F)cc12)`: the NH precedes N=, and ring closure 1 leads to C2 (the carbonyl). Writing `Nc...\N=C1/C(=O)...` becomes complex, so I write it as `[NH]/N=C1\C(=O)N(Ar)c2ccc(F)cc21`. Here the NH is "before" N with a "/" bond, which places it below the N. After C1, `\C(=O)` places C2 below, since "\" after the atom means down. A bond "/" before N and "\" after C1 gives the NH and C2 on opposite sides. That puts NH on the same side as C3a, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(c3)C(F)(F)F)c3ccc(F)cc23)c1O

name: rs_1205
text:
The structure has a 3-hydroxy-4-methoxypyridine-2-carboxamide joined through the amide N to a bicyclic epoxide ring.

**Pyridine part.** The ring N is at the bottom. C2 carries the C(=O)NH group, C3 carries OH, C4 carries OMe, and C5 and C6 are CH. SMILES: c1cnc(C(=O)N...)c(O)c1OC.

**Seven-membered ring.** Going around from the amide-bearing carbon:
- C1 bears the NH.
- C2 is a CH2.
- C3 is C(CH3)2, the gem-dimethyl carbon at the top.
- C4 is an epoxide CH, bonded to C5.
- C5 is the other epoxide CH, bonded to C6.
- C6 is CH(CH3), drawn with a hashed methyl.
- C7 is CH(CH3), bonded back to C1.

That gives seven ring atoms: C1, CH2, CMe2, epoxide CH, epoxide CH, CHMe (hashed), CHMe. The epoxide O bridges the two adjacent CH carbons.

**Stereochemistry.** Only the hashed methyl is drawn with stereo, so only that carbon is marked. The other centres are drawn with plain bonds and get no stereo labels.

I wrote the ring as C1(NC(=O)...)CC(C)(C)C2OC2C(C)C1C, with the hashed carbon being "C(C)" next to the epoxide: N-C1 CC(C)(C)C2OC2[C@H](C)C1C.

For the chirality at the hashed carbon, I'll write `[C@@H]` as a best estimate.

Its neighbours in SMILES order are the preceding epoxide C, H, the methyl, and the next ring carbon C7. In the drawing, the hashed carbon sits at the lower right. The epoxide carbon is up, C7 is to the left, and the methyl points down, hashed (away from the viewer).

Viewed from the front, the order is epoxide C (up), then methyl (down, behind), then C7 (left). Looking from the epoxide C, with the H implicit and toward the viewer, the sequence H, Me, C7 is hard to judge by eye, so I'm settling on `@` or `@@` by an approximate analysis. Taking the viewer's side as the H side, the order epoxide C (up), C7 (left), Me (down-right) runs counterclockwise from the front. From the side opposite H, this appears clockwise.

SMILES order is: preceding atom (epoxide C), H, Me, C7. With the first neighbour as the viewpoint, the remaining three (H, Me, C7) need to appear anticlockwise for `@`. Swapping to put H first gives the order H, epoxide C, Me, C7, which is one swap from the original. Viewed from H (the viewer's side), epoxide C (up) → Me (down-right) → C7 (left) runs clockwise. That is `@@` for the order H, epC, Me, C7, and one swap converts it to `@` for the original order.

name: rs_1226
text:
The drawing shows a propyl group on a cyclohexane ring (marked H), which is joined to a second cyclohexane ring (also H), which is joined to a benzene ring. The benzene carries a CH2–CH(CH3)–C2H5 side chain. The CH carbon is marked with * to flag it as a stereocentre, but all its bonds are plain, so I give no stereo there.

The dots at the ring junctions on the cyclohexane rings are the usual liquid-crystal notation for trans-1,4 substitution. They are not wedges or hashes. Since the dots do indicate trans geometry, I include trans stereochemistry on the two cyclohexane rings.

Trans-1,4 on the first ring: CCC[C@H]1CC[C@@H](CC1)... Writing this out carefully:

For a trans-1,4-disubstituted cyclohexane, the pattern `[C@H]1CC[C@@H](CC1)` is trans. Check: in `C[C@H]1CC[C@H](C)CC1`, the two centres share the same tag, and this is the trans isomer. I'll use the same-tag pattern.

First ring and second ring: `CCC[C@H]1CC[C@H](CC1)[C@H]1CC[C@H](CC1)c1ccc(CC(C)CC)cc1`

Checking the second junction, the second ring's first carbon is written as `[C@H]1`, preceded by the first ring's `(CC1)` branch and then the bond to it. This makes the stereo assignment messy. Because the neighbor order matters, I will keep the pattern simple and consistent, using the same tag for the 1,4 pair in each ring.

Ring 1: `CCC[C@H]1CC[C@@H](CC1)` is how the first ring reads when written as `C[C@H]1CC[C@@H](X)CC1`. Either way, the trans assignment depends on the tag convention, and I use the form `CCC[C@H]1CC[C@H](CC1)[C@H]1CC[C@H](CC1)c1ccc(CC(C)CC)cc1`, which keeps the same tag on each 1,4 pair.

SMILES: CCC[C@H]1CC[C@H](CC1)[C@H]1CC[C@H](CC1)c1ccc(CC(C)CC)cc1

name: rs_1229
text:
The drawing shows a pyrene core with an N-ethyl-N-(4-methylbenzyl)amino group attached at position 1.

**Substituent.** The nitrogen carries an ethyl group (CH2CH3) and a CH2 linked to a benzene ring. That ring has a methyl group para to the CH2, so it is a 4-methylbenzyl group.

**Pyrene core.** Pyrene is C16H10 with four fused rings. I numbered the atoms in the 1-substituted pyrene as follows:
- C1 (bearing N) is bonded to C2 and to C10a.
- C2 and C3 are CH, and C3 connects to C3a.
- C3a connects to C4 (CH), which connects to C5 (CH), which connects to C5a.
- C5a connects to C6, C7 and C8, then to C8a.
- C8a connects to C9, which connects to C10 and then to C10a.
- The inner carbons are C10b and C10c.

A SMILES for the 1-substituted pyrene is c1cc2ccc3cccc4ccc(c1c2c34)N(...). Checking it atom by atom:
- c1 is C2 (CH), and the next c is C3 (CH).
- c2 is C3a.
- cc are C4 and C5.
- c3 is C5a.
- ccc are C6, C7 and C8.
- c4 is C8a.
- cc are C9 and C10.
- c(...) is C10a in the written string, but the substituent position needs care.

Writing it out in full: c1cc2ccc3cccc4ccc(c1c2c34)N(CC)Cc1ccc(C)cc1. The atom before the branch is the substituted carbon, so the ring closures need checking.
- Atoms: a1 c1 (C2), a2 c (C3), a3 c2 (C3a), a4 c (C4), a5 c (C5), a6 c3 (C5a), a7 c, a8 c, a9 c (C6, C7, C8), a10 c4 (C8a), a11 c (C9), a12 c (C10), a13 c( (C10a, bearing the branch).
- The branch (c1c2c34) then supplies the closing atoms: c1 closes the ring to a1, and c2 closes to a3.
- That makes a13 bonded to a14, which is C1 and closes to a1. So the substituted carbon is a14, not a13.
- To avoid this, I rewrote the SMILES with the substituent on the atom that closes ring 1: c1(N(CC)Cc5ccc(C)cc5)ccc2ccc3cccc4ccc1c2c34.

Checking this version:
- C1 carries N and is bonded to C2 and, via the ring closure, to C10a.
- Then c c are C2 and C3, and c2 is C3a.
- cc are C4 and C5, and c3 is C5a.
- ccc are C6, C7 and C8, and c4 is C8a.
- cc are C9 and C10, and c1 is C10a, which closes to C1.
- c2 is C10b, bonded to C10a and closing to C3a.
- c34 is C10c, bonded to C10b and closing to C5a and C8a.

All 16 carbons are accounted for and the connectivity matches pyrene.

SMILES: CCN(Cc5ccc(C)cc5)c1ccc2ccc3cccc4ccc1c2c34

name: rs_1248
text:
The image shows a copolymer with two repeat units, a norbornane unit (subscript 51) and a methacrylonitrile-type unit (subscript 49).

**Norbornane unit.** The bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane is drawn with its backbone bonds leaving at the two top vertices, which are adjacent carbons (C5 and C6 of the norbornane). The bridgehead carbons are at the left and right. The left bridgehead is joined to the lower-left CH2, and the right bridgehead is joined to the quaternary carbon bearing CF3 and CO2tBu. The one-carbon bridge is the short line across the middle. The ring bonds are:

- C(a) top-left, linked to the left bridgehead C1 and to C(b) top-right.
- C(b) top-right, linked to the right bridgehead C4.
- C1 to C7 (bridge) and C1 to C2 (the CH2 at lower left).
- C2 to C3, the quaternary carbon bearing CF3 and CO2tBu.
- C3 to C4.
- C4 to C7.

Reading the drawing: the left bridgehead is at (100,138) and the right bridgehead at (235,138). The top vertices at (133,78) and (205,78) are the chain-attached carbons. The lower-left CH2 at (135,198) joins the quaternary carbon at (198,198), which joins the right bridgehead at (235,138). So the ring is: top-left carbon, top-right carbon, right bridgehead, quaternary C, CH2, left bridgehead, back to top-left, with the bridge CH2 linking the two bridgeheads. This gives a 7-carbon bicycle.

SMILES for the unit, with open ends marked by the first and last ring atoms: C1(C2CC(C1)C(C(F)(F)F)(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C2)... I need the correct connectivity here, so I write it explicitly. Let the top-left carbon be Ca and the top-right carbon be Cb. Ca is bonded to the left bridgehead C1, and Cb is bonded to the right bridgehead C4. C1 is bonded to the CH2 (C2) and to the bridge C7. C2 is bonded to C3, which is bonded to C4. This gives:

[*]C1C2CC(C1[*])... 

Written out as a ring: C1(Ca) – C2 … Ca–Cb, Cb–C4, C4–C3, C3–C2, C2–C1, C1–Ca, C1–C7, C7–C4. In SMILES: C1(*)C2CC(C1... this is the ring Ca, C1, C7, C4, Cb which is a five-membered ring, so I write it as

`*C1C2CC(C1*)C(C(F)(F)F)(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C2`

Here Ca is C1 (ring label 1), then C2 as the left bridgehead (ring label 2), then the bridge CH2, then the right bridgehead C(...), which closes to Cb via C1*. Then the quaternary carbon, and finally the CH2 that closes ring 2 to the left bridgehead. This matches the connectivity above.

**Second unit.** The unit is CH2–C(CH3)(CN), written as `CC(C)(C#N)` with ends at CH2 and the quaternary carbon.

**Combining.** I write the copolymer as the two units in sequence with the repeat counts shown:

`[*]C1C2CC(C1[*])C(C(F)(F)F)(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C2` is not a clean linear chain, so I write the two units in brackets with the counts:

SMILES: *C1C(*)C2CC1C(C(F)(F)F)(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C2.*CC(C)(C#N)*

name: rs_1258
text:
This SMILES was read from the drawing region by region and checked atom for atom.

**Left to right:**
- **Imidazole end:** a 2-aminoimidazole (ring `c1cnc[nH]1`) whose exocyclic NH leads into a three-carbon chain, `NCCC`.
- **Indazole:** the chain is attached to N1 of the indazole. N2=C3 sits at the top of the five-membered ring, and the benzene ring carries the carbonyl at C5.
- **Amide and amino acid:** the C5 carbonyl is an amide, `C(=O)NC`, joined to a 2,3-diaminopropionic acid unit. Its α-carbon carries the wedged NH–SO2 group and the free CO2H.
- **Aryl sulfonamide:** the sulfonyl group is on a 2,6-dimethylphenyl ring. The para position bears an O–CH2CH2CH2–C(=O)NH ether-amide chain.
- **Linker and cap:** the chain continues through –NHCH2CH2NH– into the C(=O) of a cysteic acid residue (CH2SO3H side chain), whose NH carries Boc, `NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C`.

**Stereochemistry:**
- **Diaminopropionic α-carbon (wedged N):** the priorities are N > COOH > CH2N. Viewed from the front with H at the back, N → COOH → CH2 runs counterclockwise, so this centre is S. That corresponds to `[C@H]` with neighbour order CH2, H, N, COOH.
- **Cysteic acid α-carbon (hashed CH2):** the priorities are N > CH2SO3H > C(=O). With H toward the viewer, the apparent counterclockwise sequence reverses to clockwise, so this centre is R (the L configuration). That corresponds to `[C@H]` with neighbour order C(=O), H, CH2, N.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@H](CS(=O)(=O)O)C(=O)NCCNC(=O)CCCOc1cc(C)c(c(C)c1)S(=O)(=O)N[C@@H](CNC(=O)c1ccc2c(c1)cnn2CCCNc1ncc[nH]1)C(=O)O

Rechecking, I wrote the last stereocentre as `[C@@H]` in that line, but my derivation gave `[C@H]` for S with the neighbour order CH2, H, N, COOH. In this line the order is N (preceding), H, CH2, COOH, which is an odd permutation of (CH2, H, N, COOH) (a swap of N and CH2), so `[C@@H]` is the correct form here. The line is consistent.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@H](CS(=O)(=O)O)C(=O)NCCNC(=O)CCCOc1cc(C)c(c(C)c1)S(=O)(=O)N[C@@H](CNC(=O)c1ccc2c(c1)cnn2CCCNc1ncc[nH]1)C(=O)O

text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H at its upper position and is joined to the second ring at the meta position, so it is a 3-carboxyphenyl group. On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring sits next to the carbon bearing OH. The next carbon carries the NH of the hydrazone. So the substituent pattern on this ring is C1 (aryl), C2 (OH), C3 (NH–N=).

**Hydrazone linker.** The ring–HN–N= unit connects to C3 of the indolin-2-one, so the drawing shows an isatin 3-hydrazone.

**Indolinone core.** C3 is double-bonded to N, C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a 3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group. The CF3 on the benzo ring is at position 6. This follows from the ring layout: C3a is the fused carbon attached to C3, then C4 is the top vertex, C5 is the top right, and C6 is the right vertex carrying CF3. C7 is the bottom vertex, attached to C7a, which is bonded to N.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N double bond has a defined geometry in the drawing. Taking the carbons in the image, the NH is drawn on the lower left of N, and on C3 the C2 (C=O) lies below while C3a lies to the right. The N= sits above C3, with its NH substituent going up and to the left. The ring substituent on C3 that is cis to NH is therefore the one on the same side.

C3 sits at about (320, 465) and N at about (292, 413). NH is at (210, 380), to the left of N. On C3, the C2 carbonyl is at (290, 525), which is lower left, and C3a is at (400, 490), to the right. The N=C bond runs from lower right (C3) to upper left (N), and NH goes further left-down from N. Relative to the C=N axis, NH is on the left side, as is C2, so NH and C2 are cis (Z).

**SMILES.** Writing the N as N/N=C... with the Z geometry:

OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3cccc(c3)C(F)(F)F)c3cc(ccc23)C(F)(F)F)c1O

Check on the stereo: in "N/N=C2/C(=O)...", the bond N/N means the NH is "below" the first N. Then =C2/C(=O) puts C(=O) "above" the C. Opposite sides would be trans, so this notation puts NH and C2 trans, the opposite of what I want. To make them cis, I use N/N=C2\C(=O).

name: rs_1288
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H and is attached at the meta position to a second ring. On the second ring, the carbon bearing the first ring is next to the C–OH carbon, which is next to the carbon bearing the NH. So the second ring is 1-aryl, 2-OH, 3-NH.

**Linker.** The ring NH is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C3 of the oxindole: ring–NH–N=C3.

**Oxindole.** C3 is bonded to C2(=O), which is bonded to N1. N1 carries the aryl group and is also bonded to the fused benzo ring.

**N-aryl group.** A para-substituted phenyl bearing CH(OH)CF3.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry, but the CH(OH)CF3 centre has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label. For the C=N geometry, the NH on N points down-left. At C3, the C2 (carbonyl) side lies on the lower left, and the benzo ring is on the right. The N is above C3, with the NH to its left (the N=C bond runs from N at about (300,410) to C3 at about (300,485)).

I wrote the SMILES as NH/N=C3/..., then checked the geometry. The NH is at lower left of N, at x≈245, y≈380. N is at (300,410), and C3 is at (305,485), directly below N. On C3, the carbonyl C2 is at lower left (265,520) and the benzo carbon is at lower right (340,510). Within the N=C bond, the NH substituent lies on the left of N, and C2 lies on the left of C3, so they are on the same side (Z).

SMILES for Z: `N(/N=C1/C(=O)N(c2ccc(cc2)C(O)C(F)(F)F)c2ccccc12)` with the aryl attached before it. Writing it fully as c1(NN=...) needs the bond marks placed carefully. For the written form `Ar-N/N=C1\C(=O)N(...)c2ccccc12`: the bond N/N means the first N is below the second N, so the aryl-N is "below" the N=. Then `C1\C(=O)` places C2 as "below" C3 as well, and these are on the same side, giving Z. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(cc3)C(O)C(F)(F)F)c3ccccc23)c1O

Checking the bond marks in this final string: `N/N=C2/C(=O)`, where the first N is before the "/" and C(=O) comes after the "/" following C2. The pattern F/C=C/F is trans (E). Here N/N=C2/C(=O) would put the aryl-NH and C2 on opposite sides, which is E, not the Z I wanted. To get Z, I use `N/N=C2\C(=O)`.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(cc3)C(O)C(F)(F)F)c3ccccc23)c1O

name: rs_1369
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents.

- NH2 is on the upper-right carbon.
- CN is on the lower-right carbon, adjacent to the carbon bearing NH2.
- Br is on the lower-left carbon, which is meta to the NH2 carbon and para to... let me check positions.

I label the ring vertices: C1 top (the NH2 carbon, upper right), C2 the CN carbon (right-lower), C3 bottom, C4 lower-left (the Br carbon), C5 upper-left, C6 top.

In the image, the ring vertices run roughly as follows: top (~110,10), upper-right (~175,45) with NH2, lower-right (~175,110) with CN, bottom (~110,145), lower-left (~45,110) with Br, upper-left (~45,45).

Relative to the NH2 carbon, the CN carbon is adjacent (ortho). Going from the NH2 carbon through the CN carbon to the bottom carbon and then to the Br carbon, Br is 3 bonds away, so it is para to NH2. Going the other way, from NH2 through the top carbon and the upper-left carbon to Br, it is also 3 bonds, which confirms para.

Relative to CN, Br is two bonds away (CN carbon, bottom carbon, Br carbon), so it is meta to CN.

So the compound is 2-amino-5-bromobenzonitrile. Numbering from the CN carbon as C1, NH2 is at C2 and Br is at C5 (para to NH2, meta to CN), which fits.

name: rs_1381
text:
Reading the left ring: the top carbon carries OH, and the upper right carbon carries the CH2 bridge. The lower right carbon is a CH, and the bottom carbon carries OH. The lower left carbon carries OCH3, and the upper left carbon is a CH.

Numbering the left ring from the CH2-bearing carbon as C1:
- C1 bears CH2.
- C2 (top) bears OH.
- C3 (upper left) is CH.
- C4 (lower left) bears OCH3.
- C5 (bottom) bears OH.
- C6 (lower right) is CH.

The left ring is therefore 2,5-dihydroxy-4-methoxyphenyl.

The right ring is a mirror image. The CH2 attaches at its upper left carbon, with OH at the top, then a CH at the upper right, OCH3 at the lower right, OH at the bottom, and a CH at the lower left. This is the same substitution pattern as the left ring.

SMILES for the left ring: c1(C)c(O)cc(OC)c(O)c1, written with the CH2 attachment at the first atom.

Full molecule: COc1cc(O)c(Cc2cc(O)c(OC)cc2O)cc1O

Check on the left ring: c1(OC) is C4, then cc(O) gives C3 (CH) and C2 (OH), then c(C...) is C1 bearing the CH2, then c is C6 (CH), and c1O is C5 (OH). This matches.

Check on the right ring: c2 is C1, c is CH, c(O) is the OH carbon at the bottom, c(OC) is the OCH3 carbon, c is CH, and c2O is the top OH carbon. This matches.

SMILES: COc1cc(O)c(Cc2cc(O)c(OC)cc2O)cc1O

name: rs_1375
text:
I read the drawing as an antimycin-type 9-membered dilactone carrying a substituted picolinamide.

**Pyridine part:** The ring has N, then C2 bearing the amide C(=O)NH, C3 bearing the OC(=O)CH2CH2OMe ester, C4 bearing OMe, and C5 and C6 as CH.

**Dilactone ring (9 atoms):** Going around the ring:
- lactone C(=O)
- ring O
- CH(CH3)
- CH(OPiv), where Piv is pivalate, OC(=O)C(CH3)3
- CH(CH2Ph)
- lactone C(=O)
- ring O
- CH2
- CH(NH), which closes back to the first C(=O)

**Stereochemistry:** I assigned the four stereocentres from the wedges and hashes, then set the SMILES @/@@ to match:
- CH(N), with the N on a hashed bond: S
- CH(CH3), with the methyl on a wedge: S
- CH(OPiv), with the O on a hashed bond: R
- CH(CH2Ph), with the benzyl on a wedge: R

SMILES: COCCC(=O)Oc1c(OC)ccnc1C(=O)N[C@H]2COC(=O)[C@H](Cc3ccccc3)[C@@H](OC(=O)C(C)(C)C)[C@H](C)OC2=O

name: rs_1380
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right:

1. A methyl sulfone, CH3–SO2–, is attached through a CH2 to a benzene ring at a meta position.
2. The same ring carries a three-carbon chain, CH2CH2CH2, at its other meta position, ending in an NH.
3. The NH is bonded to a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
4. The para position of that ring carries CH2–CH(OMe)–CO2Et.

For the stereocentre, the OMe is on a bold wedge and the H is on a hashed bond. The CIP priorities are OMe > CO2Et > CH2Ar > H. With H pointing away from the viewer, OMe → CO2Et → CH2Ar runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S.

In the SMILES `CCOC(=O)[C@@H](OC)Cc1ccc(...)cc1`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is C(=O), H, OMe, CH2. Moving H to the front shows that `@@` for this order corresponds to S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@@H](OC)Cc1ccc(NCCCc2cccc(CS(C)(=O)=O)c2)cc1

name: rs_1382
text:
The structure has four parts.

**Thiazolidinedione ring.** The ring is NH–C(=O)–C(=CH–Ar)–S–C(=O), so the ring atoms are C1(=O)NC(=O)C(=C...)S1. The exocyclic double bond runs from C5 to the CH that attaches to the aryl ring.

**Central benzene ring.** Reading the ring in the drawing:
- The top-left carbon bears the CH= substituent.
- The carbon at lower left bears OH.
- The next carbon bears the NH–N hydrazone link.
- The CH= carbon and the NH carbon are para to each other, which I checked against the ring positions in the drawing.
- The OH is ortho to the NH, so the ring is c1(C=)ccc(NN=)c(O)c1.

**Hydrazone.** The NH–N= unit joins the central ring to C3 of the oxindole.

**Oxindole.**
- C3 is double-bonded to the hydrazone N.
- C2 is the carbonyl, and N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group.
- On the fused benzene ring, F sits at C4 and CF3 at C6.

Written as a SMILES, the oxindole is O=C1N(Ar)c2cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(F)c2C1=NNAr'.

I did not assign stereochemistry. The drawing does show double-bond geometry, but I could not read it reliably, so the SMILES leaves it unspecified.

Full SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)C(S1)=Cc1ccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(F)c23)c(O)c1

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)C(S1)=Cc1ccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(F)c23)c(O)c1

name: rs_1383
text:
The drawing shows a 2,5-diphenylpyrrole whose ring nitrogen is bonded to an exocyclic imine nitrogen (N-amino pyrrole, a hydrazone).

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Pyrrole ring:** the N is bonded to C2 and C5, and each of these carries a phenyl (Ph). C3 and C4 are the two CH carbons, with double bonds C2=C3 and C4=C5.
- **Hydrazone link:** N(pyrrole)–N=C, so the imine carbon is attached to the exocyclic N by a double bond.
- **Chain:** the imine carbon bears a methyl and a C(=O)CH3 group. The carbonyl is on the left (O=C), with a methyl at the bottom left. This is the monohydrazone of butane-2,3-dione.

The imine C=N geometry is not clearly specified by wedges, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CC(=O)C(C)=NN1C(c2ccccc2)=CC=C1c1ccccc1

name: rs_1385
text:
The drawing shows a 4-phenoxybenzamide whose amide nitrogen is joined through a three-carbon chain to a Boc-protected amine.

- **Left ring:** a phenyl ring attached to an oxygen (the ether linkage).
- **Middle ring:** a para-substituted benzene bearing that ether oxygen on one side and a C(=O)NH group on the other.
- **Chain:** the amide NH connects to three CH2 groups. The zigzag shows the N, then three vertices, then the second N. The second NH carries the Boc group.
- **Boc:** tert-butoxycarbonyl, C(=O)OC(C)(C)C.

There are no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NCCCNC(=O)c1ccc(Oc2ccccc2)cc1

name: rs_1386
text:
The drawing shows a 2-(trifluoromethyl)benzamide whose amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl ring.

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying CF3 on the carbon next to the carbonyl-bearing carbon (ortho).
- **Amide:** C(=O)–NH linking the left ring to the right ring.
- **Right ring:** a benzene ring with the NH on one carbon and, on the adjacent (ortho) carbon, a CH(CH3)–CH2–C(CH3)3 chain. This is a 1,3,3-trimethylbutyl group, written as CH(CH3)CH2C(CH3)3.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccccc1C(C)CC(C)(C)C)c1ccccc1C(F)(F)F

name: rs_1384
text:
The drawing shows a cyclopenta[b]indole: a benzene ring fused to a pyrrole, which is fused to a cyclopentane.

**Substituents on the benzene ring:**
- F is at the upper left.
- The methylsulfonyl group (SO2CH3) sits at the lower left, adjacent to the carbon bonded to N.
- N carries a CH(CH3)(4-chlorophenyl) group.

**Pyrrole and cyclopentane rings:**
- The pyrrole carbon next to N (C2 of the indole) is fused to the cyclopentane CH bearing CH2CO2H.
- The pyrrole C3 is bonded to the CH2 of the cyclopentane at the top and to the benzene ring.
- The cyclopentane ring runs C3(indole)–CH2–CH2–CH(CH2CO2H)–C2(indole).

**Benzene ring atoms:**
- C3a is bonded to C3 and is at the top right of the benzene ring.
- The top-left carbon is CH, which is bonded to C3a.
- The next carbon, bearing F, follows that CH.
- Then comes a CH, then the C–SO2Me carbon, then C7a, which is bonded to N.

**SMILES:**
Starting from the acid, `OC(=O)CC1CCc2c1n(C(C)c1ccc(Cl)cc1)c1c(S(C)(=O)=O)cc(F)cc21`

Check of the ring closures:
- `c2` is the indole C3, which is bonded to the CH2 on the cyclopentane.
- `c1` closes the cyclopentane ring and is the indole C2, bonded to the CH bearing the acetic acid group.
- `n(...)` is the indole N.
- `c1c(S...)cc(F)cc21` starts at C7a, which opens a new ring 1. Then come C–SO2Me, CH, C–F and CH. The last atom is C3a, which closes ring 2 to C3 and ring 1 to C7a. This is consistent.

There are no wedges or hashes in the drawing, so no stereochemistry is specified.

SMILES: OC(=O)CC1CCc2c1n(C(C)c1ccc(Cl)cc1)c1c(S(C)(=O)=O)cc(F)cc21

name: rs_1387
text:
The drawing shows a tetrahydroquinoline whose ring nitrogen is attached through a CH2 to a biphenyl, which is linked through a benzylic CH2–O to a nicotinic acid.

**Tetrahydroquinoline part.** The saturated ring is N1, then three CH2 groups (C2, C3, C4), then C4a and C8a. C8a is bonded to N. On the benzene ring, C8 is the vertex next to C8a, and the CF3 sits on the next carbon, C7. In the drawing, the CF3-bearing carbon is the bottom vertex adjacent to the CH vertex that is adjacent to C8a, so CF3 is at position 7.

**Linker and biphenyl.** The N–CH2 group is attached to a meta-substituted phenyl ring. That ring connects to a para-substituted phenyl ring, which carries CH2–O.

**Pyridine part.** The O is attached to a pyridine ring at C5, and the COOH is at C3. The ring nitrogen is at position 1, so the O-bearing carbon and the COOH-bearing carbon are both meta to N, which makes this a 5-substituted nicotinic acid.

**SMILES construction.**
- Tetrahydroquinoline: N1(CCCc2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc21) — N1, C2, C3, C4, then C4a (c2), C5, C6, C7 (bearing CF3), C8, and C8a (c21).
- Full molecule: OC(=O)c1cncc(OCc2ccc(cc2)-c2cccc(CN3CCCc4ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc34)c2)c1

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cncc(OCc2ccc(cc2)-c2cccc(CN3CCCc4ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc34)c2)c1

name: rs_1390
text:
The drawing shows Compound 76, which I read as follows.

- **Triazole core:** a 1,2,4-triazole. N1 carries the acyl group, N2 is =N, C3 carries the NH-aryl group, N4 is =N, and C5 carries NH2.
- **Acyl group:** a 2,6-difluorobenzoyl group, C(=O)c1c(F)cccc1F, attached to N1.
- **Aryl amine:** the NH at C3 links to a para-substituted benzene ring. The other para position carries S(=O)(=O)NHEt.

I wrote the triazole ring bond by bond:
- N1 (acylated) is bonded to N2 and to C5.
- N2=C3, with C3 bearing the NH-aryl group.
- C3–N4, and N4=C5 (C5 bearing NH2), which closes the ring back to N1.

This gives the SMILES: CCNS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(Nc2nc(N)n(C(=O)c3c(F)cccc3F)n2)cc1

Checking the ring atoms in that string: c2 is C3, n is N4, c(N) is C5, n(C(=O)Ar) is N1, and the final n2 is N2, which closes onto C3. The ring has 5 atoms, as it should.

SMILES: CCNS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(Nc2nc(N)n(C(=O)c3c(F)cccc3F)n2)cc1

name: rs_1388
text:
The drawing shows three parts joined by two amide links.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying an amidine group, C(=N)N, at one end. At the other end it carries a C(=O)NH group.

**Central ring:** a benzene ring.
- The NH from the left amide is attached at the bottom-left carbon.
- The adjacent carbon bears C(=O)NH–pyridyl.
- The OMe sits at the top, on the carbon para to the NH-bearing carbon.
- Taking the NH-bearing carbon as C1, the amide-bearing carbon is C2, then C3 is CH, C4 carries OMe, C5 is CH, and C6 is CH.
- In the drawing, the ring's top-right carbon is attached to the C(=O) carbon via the carbon below it. The OMe carbon is at the top, so OMe is meta to the carboxamide carbon and para to the NH carbon. This matches the 5-methoxy-anthranilamide pattern.

**Right ring:** a pyridine attached through its 2-position to the amide NH, with Br at the 5-position. The ring N is adjacent to the attachment carbon, and Br is on the carbon para to that attachment point.

SMILES for the central ring: c1(NC(=O)c2ccc(C(=N)N)cc2)ccc(OC)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1

The ring closure works as follows: c1 (NH-bearing), then c, c, c(OC), c, and c1 with the amide. Starting from the NH carbon, going c, c, c(OC) puts OMe at position 4, para to the NH carbon. Then c is C5 and the last c1 is C6, which bears the amide. This is the ortho arrangement relative to C1, so the amide-bearing carbon is adjacent to the NH carbon, as required. The OMe carbon is then meta to the amide carbon, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccc(NC(=O)c2ccc(C(=N)N)cc2)c(c1)C(=O)Nc1ccc(Br)cn1

name: rs_1389
text:
The drawing shows a 3-hydroxy-4-methoxypyridine-2-carboxamide whose amide nitrogen is attached to a substituted cyclohexane, which carries an aryl ether.

**Pyridine ring (left).** The ring nitrogen is at the bottom left. C2 carries the C(=O)N group, C3 carries OH, C4 carries OMe, and C5 and C6 are plain CH.
SMILES for this part: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N...)c1O

**Cyclohexane ring (centre).** C1 bears the NH. Going around the ring:
- C2 is CH2.
- C3 is C(CH3)2, the quaternary carbon at the top.
- C4 is CH–O.
- C5 is C(CH3)2, at the bottom.
- C6 is CH2.

The ring is therefore N–C1H, CH2, C(Me)2, CH(OAr), C(Me)2, CH2, back to C1.
SMILES for this part: C1CC(C)(C)C(Oc...)C(C)(C)C1

**Pyridine ether (right).** The ether oxygen is attached to C2 of a pyridine, which is next to the ring nitrogen. Going round the ring: N1, C2 (O), C3 (CH), C4 (CF3), C5 (CH), C6 (CF3). This is a 4,6-bis(trifluoromethyl)pyridin-2-yl group.
SMILES for this part: c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)n1 (written with the O attached at the first atom)

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereochemistry is included.

Combined SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2CC(C)(C)C(Oc3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)n3)C(C)(C)C2)c1O

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NC2CC(C)(C)C(Oc3cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)n3)C(C)(C)C2)c1O

name: rs_1393
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with an F3CO group (trifluoromethoxy) at one position and a plain line at the para position, opposite it. The plain line ends in no label, so it is a methyl group. The molecule is therefore 4-(trifluoromethoxy)toluene.

Written as SMILES, this is FC(F)(F)Oc1ccc(C)cc1. The ring has six vertices, the two substituents are para to each other, and there are no stereocentres.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc1

name: rs_1392
text:
The drawing shows a Cbz-protected amino acid methyl ester with a 6-benzyloxypyridin-3-yl side chain.

- **Cbz group:** a benzyl ring attached through CH2–O–C(=O)–NH to the alpha carbon.
- **Alpha carbon:** bonded to CO2Me and to a CH2 that leads to the pyridine ring. It is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is assigned.
- **Pyridine ring:** the CH2 attaches at C3. The ring nitrogen is N1, and C2 lies between N and C3 (the position below the N label in the drawing). The benzyloxy group sits on the carbon adjacent to N on the other side, which is C6.

Ring atoms in order: N1, C2(H), C3(CH2), C4(H), C5(H), C6(OBn), which gives c1(CC...)cnc(OCc2ccccc2)cc1.

SMILES: COC(=O)C(Cc1ccc(OCc2ccccc2)nc1)NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1

name: rs_1394
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring with these substituents:
- 4-OMe
- 3-OH
- 2-C(=O)NH-CH2-, where the CH2 is attached to a cyclopropane

The cyclopropane carries a gem-dimethyl carbon and a 2-methylprop-1-enyl group (CH=C(CH3)2). This is the chrysanthemyl amine unit.

SMILES for the pyridine portion: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NCC2C(C=C(C)C)C2(C)C)c1O

Checking the pyridine ring: N is at the bottom left, C2 is bonded to the carbonyl, C3 carries the OH, C4 carries the OMe, and C5 and C6 are CH. In the SMILES, c1(OMe) is C4, then c is C5, c is C6, n is N1, c(C(=O)...) is C2, and c1O is C3. This matches the drawing.

The cyclopropane has no wedges or hashes in the drawing, so no stereochemistry is specified.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NCC2C(C=C(C)C)C2(C)C)c1O

name: rs_1395
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole, which I read as follows.

**Left part.** The top-left ring carries CO2H and is linked to a second ring. On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring is adjacent to the C-OH carbon. The next carbon after C-OH bears the NH. So the ring is biphenyl-substituted at C1, OH at C2 and NHN= at C3. The acid sits at the meta position of the first ring, which gives 3'-hydrazinyl-2'-hydroxybiphenyl-3-carboxylic acid.

**Hydrazone.** NH–N= connects the second ring to C3 of the oxindole.

**Oxindole.** C3 is double-bonded to N, C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a 3,4-dimethylphenyl group. The CF3 is on the benzo ring. Numbering the benzo ring from C3a, the carbons run C4, C5, C6, C7, C7a. C4 is the carbon next to C3a, and the CF3 is on the carbon one position further, which is C5.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing does not show clear cis/trans geometry for the C=N bond, so I leave it unspecified.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc23)c1O
- Oxindole: C2(=NN...)C(=O)N(Ar)c3ccc(CF3)cc32. Here c3 (C7a) is attached to N, then c c is C7 and C6, then c(CF3) is C5, then c is C4, and c32 is C3a closing onto C3. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(C)c3)c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc23)c1O

name: rs_1391
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Aromatic ring:** the vinyl substituent sits at C1, the OH at C3 (meta to the vinyl) and the NO2 at C4 (para to the vinyl, adjacent to the OH).
- **Side chain:** Ar–CH=C(NHCbz)(CO2Me). The Cbz group expands to the benzyl carbamate NH–C(=O)OCH2Ph, and CO2Me is the methyl ester.
- **Double bond geometry:** the aryl group on the CH and the NHCbz on the other alkene carbon appear on the same side of the double bond, so the alkene is Z (N outranks the ester carbon, and aryl outranks H). The ester is therefore trans to the aryl, which is what `/C(...)=C/` encodes in the SMILES below.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C(NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)=C/c1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])c(O)c1

name: rs_1398
text:
The drawing shows a thiophene ring with a dimethylamino group at C2 and an azo group (N=N) at C5. The azo group links to a para-nitrophenyl ring.

The azo bond is drawn as a plain double bond with no cis/trans geometry marked, so I have left out stereo descriptors.
