SMILES: CN(C)c1ccc(s1)N=Nc1ccc(cc1)[N+](=O)[O-]

name: rs_1400
text:
The drawing shows a cyclopropane ring with two substituents on one carbon. One is a benzyl group (Ph–CH2). The other is a sulfonyl group, S(=O)(=O), attached to NH–C(CH3)3 (tert-butyl).

This is 1-benzyl-N-tert-butylcyclopropane-1-sulfonamide. No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NS(=O)(=O)C1(Cc2ccccc2)CC1

name: rs_1397
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left end:** a methanesulfonate ester, CH3–S(=O)(=O)–O–, attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Linker:** the ring carries a trans CH=CH (drawn as an E alkene), then CH2, then NH. The NH is bonded to a second para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Right end:** the second ring carries CH2–CH(OEt)–COOEt. The OEt on the stereocentre is on a bold wedge. The other drawn bonds are plain, so this is the only stereocentre marked.

**Stereocentre assignment:** the OEt is wedged toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. The CIP priorities are OEt > COOEt > CH2Ar. Going from OEt (up) to COOEt (lower right) to CH2 (lower left) is clockwise, so the centre is R.

**SMILES chirality tag:** with neighbour order CH2, H, OEt, COOEt, the tag `@@` corresponds to R. The alkene is written as E.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)/C=C/CNc1ccc(cc1)C[C@@H](OCC)C(=O)OCC

name: rs_1399
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine-2-carboxamide with a 3-hydroxy and a 4-methoxy group. The amide nitrogen carries a three-carbon chain ending in a pyridin-3-yl ring.

**Left ring (pyridine):**
- The ring nitrogen is at the lower left.
- The carbon next to it at the lower right (C2) bears the C(=O)NH group.
- C3 bears OH.
- C4 bears OMe.
- C5 and C6 are CH, and C6 is bonded to the ring nitrogen.

**Side chain:** C(=O)–NH–CH2–CH2–CH2–(pyridin-3-yl).

**Right ring:** The attachment carbon is C3. The ring nitrogen sits two atoms from the attachment point, with one CH between them, which makes it a 3-pyridyl group.

SMILES for the left ring: c1(C(=O)NCCCc2cccnc2)nccc(OC)c1O

Check: the ring atoms are c1 (C2), n, c, c, c(OC), c1(O). That gives C2, N1, C6, C5, C4(OMe), C3(OH), and C3 closes back to C2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)NCCCc2cccnc2)c1O

name: rs_1396
text:
I read the structure in four parts and assigned stereochemistry only where the drawing shows it.

- **Left ring:** a pyrrolidin-2-one (γ-lactam). The C=O is drawn at the top left, N is at the top of the ring, and the ring carbon at the lower right carries the side chain.
- **N-substituent:** an N–CH2CH2 chain leading to a para-substituted benzene ring that bears CO2H, so the acid is a 4-substituted benzoic acid.
- **Side chain on the ring carbon:** a bold wedge leads to a CH=CH double bond, which is drawn trans (E). The alkene then connects to a CH(OH) carbon. That carbon is bonded to a quaternary cyclopentane carbon bearing a 3-fluorophenyl ring (F meta to the attachment point).
- **Stereocentres:**
  - The ring carbon is the only centre with a wedge. Its priorities are N > vinyl carbon > ring CH2 > H. With the wedged vinyl toward the viewer and H pointing away, N (up), vinyl (down-right) and CH2 (left) run clockwise, so the centre is R. Written in SMILES order (CH2, H, N, vinyl), this is `[C@@H]`.
  - The CH(OH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccc(CCN2C(=O)CC[C@@H]2/C=C/C(O)C2(CCCC2)c2cccc(F)c2)cc1

name: rs_1401
text:
The drawing shows a pyrimidine ring with a pyrrolidine and a mesylate-bearing chain attached.

- **Pyrimidine ring:** the two nitrogens sit at positions 1 and 3, with C2 between them at the right of the ring. The top-right vertex is N, the bottom vertex is N, and the carbon between them carries the side chain. The carbon at the left carries the pyrrolidine nitrogen, so that carbon is C5. The other two ring carbons are CH.
- **Pyrrolidine:** the ring nitrogen is bonded directly to C5 of the pyrimidine, and the ring is a saturated five-membered ring (N plus four CH2).
- **Side chain:** C2 of the pyrimidine bears CH2CH2–OMs, where Ms is methanesulfonyl, S(=O)(=O)C, so the chain ends in OS(C)(=O)=O.

name: rs_1406
text:
The image shows a copolymer of two norbornane repeat units, with subscripts 45 and 55. Each unit is a bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane that is attached to the polymer chain through its C2 and C3 positions (the top two bonds).

**Unit 1 (45):** The norbornane carries a quaternary carbon bearing CF3 and CO2C(CH3)3. The ring is drawn with the top two carbons as chain-connection points, a bridge CH2 at the middle, and bridgeheads on the left and right. The substituted carbon sits at the lower right, next to the lower-left CH2, which in turn connects to the left bridgehead.

Numbering the ring: C1 is a bridgehead (left), C2 is the top-left carbon, C3 is the top-right carbon, C4 is the right bridgehead, C5 is the lower-right carbon bearing CF3 and the ester, C6 is the lower-left CH2, and C7 is the bridge.

Written as a repeat unit with open chain ends: [C]1(top-left) and [C] (top-right) are each CH with an open bond.

SMILES for unit 1: `*C1C(*)C2CC1C(C(F)(F)F)(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C2`

Checking the connectivity: C1(*) is the top-left carbon, bonded to C(*) the top-right carbon, then to bridgehead C2, then CH2 (the bridge), then back to the ring closure at the left bridgehead. The left bridgehead continues to the substituted carbon, which closes to bridgehead C2 through the ring-closure CH2. This SMILES is a bit tangled, so I rewrite it more cleanly.

Atoms: a = top-left CH(*), b = top-right CH(*), c = right bridgehead, d = bridge CH2, e = left bridgehead, f = CH2 (lower left), g = substituted carbon (lower right).

In the drawing, the substituted carbon is bonded to the right bridgehead and to the lower-left CH2, which is bonded to the left bridgehead. So g is bonded to c and f, f is bonded to e, e is bonded to a, and a is bonded to b, which is bonded to c. The bridge d connects c and e.

SMILES: `*C1C(*)C2CC1CC2(...)` does not fit this connectivity, so I write it as `*C1C(*)C2CC1CC2(C(F)(F)F)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C`. Here the ring closure 2 opens at c and closes at g. That gives a bonded to b, b to c, c to d, d to e, e to a (closure 1), e to f, f to g, and g to c (closure 2). This matches the connectivity.

**Unit 2 (55):** The substituent is CH2C(CF3)2OH on the lower-right carbon, which is bonded to the right bridgehead and to the lower-left CH2.

SMILES for unit 2: `*C1C(*)C2CC1CC2CC(O)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F`

**Combined:** I join the two units as a polymer fragment with the repeat counts, keeping the open bonds as `*` and the ring connectivity as above.

SMILES: `*C1C(C2CC1CC2(C(F)(F)F)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C1C(*)C2CC1CC2CC(O)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F`

This is only a sketch of the combined polymer. As a cleaner two-unit representation I give the repeat units joined end to end:

SMILES: `*C1C2CC(C1*)C(C2)(C(F)(F)F)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C.*C1C2CC(C1*)C(C2)CC(O)(C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F`

text:
This is my reading of the drawing, with the stereochemistry worked out from the wedges.

**Fragments**
- **Indazole:** the left-hand bicycle has an N=CH at the top and an NH at the bottom. The carbonyl is on the benzo carbon that sits next to the carbon beside the ring-fusion carbon bonded to NH, which makes it an indazol-6-yl group. It is joined through C(=O) to the ring nitrogen of the tetrahydroisoquinoline.
- **Tetrahydroisoquinoline:** the nitrogen carries the indazole carbonyl and has CH2CH2 on one side and a benzylic CH2 on the other. On the aromatic ring, one Cl sits next to the ring-fusion carbon on the CH2CH2 side. The next carbon bears the amide C(=O)NH. The next carbon bears the second Cl, and a CH closes the ring. This is a 5,7-dichloro-6-carboxamide pattern.
- **Amino acid:** the amide NH is attached to the α-carbon. That carbon carries CO2H and a CH2NH group that leads to a urea, NH–C(=O)–N(piperidine).
- **Piperidine:** the urea nitrogen is the ring nitrogen. The ring has two adjacent OH groups at C3 and C4, both on bold wedges.

**Stereochemistry**
- **α-carbon:** the CH2 is on a wedge, and the priorities are N > CO2H > CH2N > H. This gives S, the same arrangement as in L-alanine, so I wrote `N[C@@H](CN…)C(=O)O`.
- **Piperidine C3:** the OH is on a wedge and the priorities are OH > C4 > C2 > H. This gives S.
- **Piperidine C4:** the OH is on a wedge and the priorities are OH > C3 > C5 > H. This gives R.
- **Result:** the ring is (3S,4R), written as `N3C[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CC3`.

SMILES: O=C(c1ccc2cn[nH]c2c1)N1CCc2c(C1)cc(Cl)c(C(=O)N[C@@H](CNC(=O)N3C[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CC3)C(=O)O)c2Cl

N#Cc1ccc(S(F)(F)(F)(F)F)cc1C

name: rs_1446
text:
I read the molecule as a 3-hydroxy-4-methoxypyridine-2-carboxamide whose amide nitrogen is bonded to a norbornane (bicyclo[2.2.1]heptane) ring. That norbornane is fused to an N-isobutyl succinimide (a 2-methylpropyl group on the imide nitrogen).

**Pyridine part.** The ring carbon next to N bears the C(=O)NH group (C2). The adjacent carbon carries OH (C3), and the next carbon carries OMe (C4). The remaining ring positions are CH, CH and N.

**Bicyclic part.**
- The carbon bearing NH is bonded to a bridgehead carbon and to a CH2.
- That CH2 leads to the second bridgehead carbon.
- The one-carbon bridge (CH2) joins the two bridgeheads.
- Each bridgehead is also bonded to one of the two ring-fusion carbons that carry the imide C=O groups.

**Stereochemistry.** Only the C–NH bond is drawn as a wedge, so only that carbon gets a stereo label. Its substituents rank N > bridgehead carbon > CH2, with H pointing away. In the drawing the sequence N → bridgehead → CH2 runs clockwise, which gives R. In the SMILES below the neighbour order at that carbon is N, H, ring-closure bridgehead, CH2, and R corresponds to `@@` for that order.

**SMILES:** `COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@@H]2CC3CC2C2C3C(=O)N(CC(C)C)C2=O)c1O`

I checked this against the drawing atom by atom: the ring closures, the bridging CH2, the imide ring and the isobutyl group all match.

name: rs_1459
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl core carrying a carboxylic acid, a hydroxyl and a hydrazone-linked oxindole.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring bears CO2H and is attached to the second ring at the meta position, so it is a 3-carboxyphenyl group. On the second ring, the carbon bonded to the first ring (C1) is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH (C2). The next carbon (C3) carries the NH–N= group.

**Oxindole part.** The hydrazone N= is double-bonded to C3 of the oxindole. C2 of the oxindole is C=O, and the ring nitrogen N1 carries a 4-fluorophenyl group. The oxindole benzo ring is fused to C3 and to N1.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry. The NH sits at the upper left of the N=, and the oxindole C3 has the C=O side to the left (lower) and the benzo ring to the right. The hydrazone N is attached to C3, whose substituents are C2 (the carbonyl carbon, toward the lower left) and C3a (toward the right).

I assign the geometry from the drawn coordinates. HN is at about (215, 380), N at (295, 400), C3 at (325, 460), C2 at (290, 510) and C3a at (400, 440).

- At N, the HN substituent lies to the left of the N→C3 bond.
- The C=N bond runs from (295, 400) down-right to (325, 460). The HN position relative to this line is to the left and up, which puts it on the upper-left side.
- At C3, the C2 substituent at (290, 510) lies on the lower-left side of the line.
- Both HN and C2 are therefore on the same (left) side, which makes them cis.

Writing the SMILES with N(H) before the double bond: `Nc...` as `[NH]/N=C3/C(=O)...` would be trans, so for cis I write `N\N=C3/C(=O)N(...)c4ccccc34`. Here the pattern `X\N=C/Y` places X and Y on the same side, which is the cis arrangement I want.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N\N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(F)cc3)c3ccccc23)c1O

name: rs_1458
text:
I read the structure as a morpholine amide, a cyclohexylmethyl-bearing succinamide, and a 4-(trifluoromethoxy)anilino-substituted phenylbutyl amine.

- That stereocentre carries a CH2-cyclohexyl group (hashed bond) and a C(=O)NH amide.
- The amide nitrogen is attached to a second stereocentre. This carbon carries a CH2CH2Ph chain (wedged bond) and a CH2-NH-aryl group.

**Stereochemistry (CIP assignment from the wedges and hashes)**

- Second stereocentre: the priorities are N, then CH2NHAr, then CH2CH2Ph, then H. The phenethyl group is wedged, so H points away. The 1→2→3 path is counterclockwise, which gives **S**. In the SMILES this is `[C@@H]`.

name: rs_1465
text:
The drawing shows a [1,2,4]triazolo[4,3-b]pyridazin-3-one core, built from a five-membered triazolone fused to a six-membered pyridazine.

**Triazolone ring (five-membered):**
- N= (upper left) is double-bonded to the fusion carbon C8a.
- N2 (upper right) carries the CH2 substituent.
- C3 is the C=O carbon.
- N4 is the bridgehead nitrogen, which is also part of the six-membered ring.
- C8a is the other fusion carbon.

**Pyridazine ring (six-membered):**
- C8a is bonded to CH (C8).
- C8 is bonded to C7, which carries the 4-chlorophenyl group.
- C7 is bonded to C6, which carries the 2-chlorophenyl group.
- C6 is double-bonded to N, and that N is bonded to the bridgehead N4.
- N4 is bonded back to C8a.

The ring bonds are C8a=N (in the triazole), C8=C7, and C6=N.

The substituent is therefore (6-trifluoromethylpyridin-3-yl)methyl. In the SMILES, Cc2ccc(nc2)C(F)(F)F places CH2 on c2, followed by c, c, then c(CF3) next to n, then c2 closing the ring. The ring atom bearing CF3 is adjacent to n, and n is adjacent to the CH that closes the ring back to the CH2-bearing carbon, so the CH2 carbon is position 3 and CF3 is position 6, as drawn.

**Check of the core string:** C1(=O) is bonded to N(CH2Ar), then N=C3 (C8a), then C=C(Ar) (C8=C7), then C(Ar')=N–N13, where the final N closes ring 1 to the carbonyl carbon and ring 3 to C8a. This matches the drawing.

text:
I read the molecule as 4-{2-[(2S)-2-((E)-3-hydroxyoct-1-en-1-yl)-5-oxopyrrolidin-1-yl]ethyl}benzoic acid. The (2S) label is not cross-checked by CIP ranking; the stereo marker in the SMILES comes directly from the drawn hash.

- **Lactam ring:** a five-membered ring of N, C=O, two CH2 groups and one CH. The carbonyl oxygen is at the top left.
- **N-substituent:** an N–CH2–CH2 chain leads to a para-substituted benzene ring carrying CO2H.
- **Ring CH substituent:** a hashed bond goes from the ring CH to a trans CH=CH. The next carbon is CH(OH), followed by a pentyl chain (four CH2 groups and a terminal CH3). That makes eight carbons from the vinyl CH to the CH3, so the chain is oct-1-enyl.
- **Ring CH stereocentre:** the hashed bond points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Looking from the ring CH2 neighbour, the sequence H, vinyl, N runs clockwise, which gives `@@` with neighbours written in the order CH2, H, vinyl, N.
- **Other stereo:** the double bond is drawn trans, so `/C=C/`. The carbinol carbon has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo marker.

SMILES: O=C1CC[C@@H](/C=C/C(O)CCCCC)N1CCc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)O

name: rs_1468
text:
The drawing shows a dibenz[b,e][1,4]oxazepine core: 6,11-dihydrodibenz[b,e][1,4]oxazepine, with N11 carrying a side chain, a CH2 at position 6, and an O bridging to the second benzene ring.

**Pyrazine ring.** The ring atoms run C2 (bearing the chain), N, C(OMe), CH, N-adjacent CH, and so on. Reading the drawing, the top N is attached to the carbon that bears the chain (upper right), and the lower N sits between the C–OMe carbon and the CH that is attached to the chain-bearing carbon. The ring is therefore c1(CCN...)cnc(OC)cn1, which is a 2-substituted 5-methoxypyrazine (1,4-diazine).

**Side chain.** The pyrazine carries CH2CH2 to N(CH3), then CH2CH2 to the ring nitrogen N11 of the oxazepine.

**Tricyclic core.**
- The chlorinated benzene ring is attached to N through one carbon and to the CH2 through the adjacent carbon.
- Cl is on the carbon para to the CH2-bearing carbon... checking the drawing: the ring has the C–N carbon at lower left, the C–CH2 carbon at lower right, Cl at the top left, and a CH between the Cl carbon and the C–N carbon. So Cl is meta to N and para to the CH2-bearing carbon.
- Writing from N: N1c2cc(Cl)ccc2COc2ccccc12. Here c2 is the C–N carbon, then cc(Cl) puts a CH followed by C–Cl, then cc, then c2 is the carbon bearing CH2. This gives Cl meta to the C–N carbon and para to the C–CH2 carbon, which matches the drawing.

**Full SMILES:** COc1cnc(CCN(C)CCN2c3cc(Cl)ccc3COc3ccccc23)cn1

Checking the pyrazine in this SMILES: c1(OMe), c, n, c(chain), c, n1. The C–OMe carbon is adjacent to a CH and to N1. The chain carbon is adjacent to N and to a CH. The second CH is bonded to N1, and N1 is bonded back to C–OMe. This gives C(OMe)–CH–N–C(chain)–CH–N–back to C(OMe), with the N atoms para to each other, which is correct for a pyrazine.

SMILES: COc1cnc(CCN(C)CCN2c3cc(Cl)ccc3COc3ccccc23)cn1

name: rs_1469
text:
The drawing shows a benzimidazole with a thiophene-amine substituent, as the hydrochloride salt.

**Benzimidazole core.** The benzene ring carries Cl at the top-left carbon (C4, next to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the N= nitrogen). CF3 is on the lower-left carbon (C6). The imidazole ring has N= at the top and NH at the bottom, and C2 carries the NH substituent.

**Thiophene substituent.** The thiophene is attached through its C3 position to the NH. The ring is C3 (bearing NH), C4 (bearing methyl), C5, S, C2. Reading the drawing, the NH-bearing carbon is at the left and the methyl-bearing carbon at the upper right. The bottom-left carbon is CH, S is at the bottom, and the right carbon is CH. So the ring is c1(N)c(C)csc1, which is a 4-methylthiophen-3-yl group.

**SMILES assembly.** Benzimidazole: Clc1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc2[nH]c(Nc3cscc3C)nc12. Here c1 carries Cl and is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon c12, which bears the n (the N= nitrogen). The ring-fusion carbon on the other side carries [nH] and is attached to the CH that neighbors the CF3 carbon. This matches the drawing.

The HCl is written as a separate component.

SMILES: Clc1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc2[nH]c(Nc3cscc3C)nc12.Cl

name: rs_1457
text:
I read this as an antimycin-type nine-membered dilactone carrying a substituted picolinamide.

**Pyridine part:** The ring has a 4-OMe and a 3-O-acyl group. The acyl chain has 8 carbons after the ester carbonyl, so it is a nonanoyl group. The 2-position carries a C(=O)NH amide link to the ring.

**Nine-membered ring (going round):**
- C(=O) ester carbonyl
- ring O
- CH(CH3)
- CH(O-isobutyryl)
- CH(CH2Ph)
- C(=O) ester carbonyl
- ring O
- CH2
- CH(NH), which closes back to the first carbonyl

**Stereocentres:** All four ring stereocentres are drawn with wedges or hashes.
- CH(NH): hashed bond to N.
- CH(CH3): wedged methyl.
- CH(O-isobutyryl): hashed bond to O.
- CH(CH2Ph): wedged benzyl.

I assigned each centre from the drawn geometry and checked the resulting @/@@ against the neighbour order written in the SMILES.

SMILES: COc1ccnc(C(=O)N[C@H]2COC(=O)[C@H](Cc3ccccc3)[C@@H](OC(=O)C(C)C)[C@H](C)OC2=O)c1OC(=O)CCCCCCCC

name: rs_1470
text:
I read the structure region by region.

**Left fragment.** A 1-methyl-4,5-dihydroimidazol-2-yl ring (imidazoline) is attached to a benzene ring. In the ring, N1 carries the methyl, C2 is double-bonded to N3, and C4 and C5 are CH2 groups. The imidazoline is bonded to the benzene at the position para to the carbonyl-bearing carbon. A fluorine sits on the carbon ortho to the carbonyl.

**Central part.** The benzoyl C(=O) is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a second benzene ring. On that ring, the carbon bearing the NH has the amide-bearing carbon ortho to it. The OMe sits para to the NH carbon: going around the ring from the NH carbon, one neighbor is the carbon bearing C(=O)NH-pyridyl, and the OMe carbon is the next one after that, meta to the NH carbon's neighbor... checked below.

Ring positions: C1 bears NH, C2 bears the C(=O)NH-pyridyl, C3 is CH, C4 bears OMe, C5 is CH, C6 is CH. In the drawing, the OMe carbon is at the top, and the carbon bearing the amide is at the right. The NH carbon is at the lower left, so the OMe is para to the NH carbon.

**Right fragment.** The amide NH is attached to a pyridin-2-yl ring with chlorine at position 5 (para to the ring N-bearing carbon... that is, on the carbon three bonds from C2).

**SMILES assembly.**
- Left ring: Fc1cc(C2=NCCN2C)ccc1C(=O)N
- Central ring: c1(NC(=O)...)ccc(OC)cc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(Cl)cn1

Full SMILES: CN1CCN=C1c1ccc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(OC)cc2C(=O)Nc2ccc(Cl)cn2)c(F)c1

Atom check: C count = 1 (NMe) + 2 (CH2CH2) + 1 (C2) + 6 + 1 (C=O) + 6 + 1 (OMe) + 1 (C=O) + 5 = 24. N count = 5 and O count = 3, matching the formula C24H21ClFN5O3.

SMILES: CN1CCN=C1c1ccc(C(=O)Nc2ccc(OC)cc2C(=O)Nc2ccc(Cl)cn2)c(F)c1

name: rs_1473
text:
The drawing shows a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline: a benzene ring fused to a saturated six-membered ring that contains the nitrogen.

**Benzene ring.** The vertices run as follows:
- Top: carbon bearing CH3 (C8).
- Top right: carbon bonded to N (C8a).
- Bottom right: carbon at the ring fusion (C4a).
- Bottom: carbon bearing CH3 (C5).
- Bottom left: carbon bearing OH (C6).
- Top left: carbon bearing CH3 (C7).

**Saturated ring.** N1 carries an ethyl group and connects to C2, C3 and C4, with C4 bonded to C4a.

**Substituents.** The methyls are at C5, C7 and C8, and the hydroxyl is at C6.

**SMILES.** Writing the ring starting from N:
CCN1CCCc2c(C)c(O)c(C)c(C)c12

Atom check:
- N1 is bonded to CCC, then to c2, which is C4a.
- C4a is bonded to c(C), which is C5 with its methyl.
- Next is c(O), C6 with the hydroxyl.
- Next is c(C), C7 with its methyl.
- Next is c(C), C8 with its methyl.
- The final c12 is C8a, which closes both rings by bonding to N1 and to C4a.

SMILES: CCN1CCCc2c(C)c(O)c(C)c(C)c12

text:

name: rs_1471
text:
The drawing shows a carbazole core with N-ethyl on the ring nitrogen. Carbazole positions 3 and 6 each carry a CH2CH2 linker to a para-substituted phenyl ring, and each phenyl ring ends in N(CH2CH3)2.

Writing the SMILES: start from one diethylaminophenyl group, CCN(CC)c1ccc(cc1), then the linker CCc..., then the carbazole.

The carbazole is built as c1ccc2c(c1)c1cc(ccc1n2CC)... with the substituents placed at positions 3 and 6.

Numbering the carbazole: N9 is bonded to C9a and C8a. Ring A runs C1, C2, C3, C4, C4a, C9a. C3 is para to C9a, meaning it is separated from C9a by C4a-C4 on one side and C2-C1 on the other, so it is para to the carbon attached to N.

SMILES: n1(CC)c2ccc(CCAr)cc2c2cc(CCAr)ccc12

Checking the first ring: c2 (C9a), c (C1), c (C2), c(CCAr) (C3), c (C4), c2 (C4a). C3 is two atoms from C9a via C1 and C2, and C3 is adjacent to C4, which is adjacent to C4a. That fits. Then C4a bonds to C4b, which starts the second ring: c2 (C4b), c (C5), c(CCAr) (C6), c (C7), c (C8), c12 (C8a), which closes to N. C6 is para to C8a, which is correct.

Full SMILES: CCN(CC)c1ccc(CCc2ccc3c(c2)c2cc(CCc4ccc(N(CC)CC)cc4)ccc2n3CC)cc1

Checking this one: c2 (C3) c (C2) c (C1) c3 (C9a, bonded to N) c(c2) (C4a, closing to C4, which is bonded to C3). Then c2 (C4b) c (C5) c(CC...) (C6) c (C7) c (C8) c2 (C8a) n3 closes to C9a. This is consistent.

SMILES: CCN(CC)c1ccc(CCc2ccc3c(c2)c2cc(CCc4ccc(N(CC)CC)cc4)ccc2n3CC)cc1

name: rs_1475
text:
The drawing shows a quinoline core: a pyridine ring fused to a benzene ring.

**Pyridine ring.** N sits at the upper left of the fused junction. Going around the ring, N is bonded to C2, then C3, then C4, then C4a, then C8a, and back to N.

**Benzene ring.** The ring-fusion carbon C8a is bonded to N and to C8, which carries the nitrile (C≡N). Next come C7 and C6, both CH, then C5, which carries the OMe group, then C4a. The nitrile is on C8, adjacent to C8a, which is bonded to N. The OMe is on C5, adjacent to C4a.

- c and c are C7 and C6.
- c(OC) is C5, bearing the methoxy group.
- c2 is C4a.

- n is N1.

This matches the drawing.

name: rs_1478
text:
The drawing shows a 2-methylbenzothiazole joined through a sulfonamide to an isophthalic acid.

**Benzothiazole part.** S is at the top left and N at the bottom left of the thiazole ring. The methyl group sits on C2, between S and N. The fused benzene ring lies to the right of the thiazole.

**Position of the sulfonyl group.** The thiazole ring atoms are S1, C2, N3, C3a (bottom, bonded to N), the benzene carbons C4, C5, C6, C7, and C7a (top, bonded to S). Going around the benzene ring from C7a at the top: the next vertex at the top right is C7, then C6 (the upper right vertex, which carries SO2), then C5, C4, and C3a.

The SO2 attaches at the upper vertex of the benzene ring, the one at about x=290. In the drawing, C7a is at about (165, 70) and C7 at about (225, 40). The next vertex, C6, is at about (290, 70), and that is where SO2 attaches. So the sulfonyl is on C6, which is bonded to C7 (adjacent to C7a, the carbon bearing S).

**SMILES for this half.** Cc1nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)N...)cc2s1. Here C3a is bonded to N, then C4 and C5 are the "cc", then C6 carries the sulfonyl, and C7 is the final "c" before C7a (c2) and S.

**Isophthalic acid part.** The NH is attached to a benzene ring that carries COOH groups at positions 3 and 5 relative to it, giving c1cc(C(=O)O)cc(C(=O)O)c1.

SMILES: Cc1nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Nc3cc(C(=O)O)cc(C(=O)O)c3)cc2s1

name: rs_1479
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole.

**Top ring (benzoic acid).** CO2H sits on one carbon, F on the adjacent carbon, and the biaryl bond is at the carbon meta to the CO2H. Numbering from the CO2H carbon, F is at position 2 and the biaryl bond is at position 5. The ring is c1(C(=O)O)c(F)ccc(c1)-Ar.

**Middle ring.** It carries the biaryl bond at one carbon, OH on the next carbon, and the NH–N= hydrazone on the carbon after that. The ring is c1(Ar')c(O)c(NN=...)ccc1.

**Oxindole.** The N-aryl nitrogen is bonded to C2 (C=O). C3 is the hydrazone carbon (=N–NH). The CF3 sits on the benzo ring at C6, which is the carbon meta to the C3a ring-fusion carbon and attached to C7. In the drawing, the benzo ring runs from C3a (attached to C3) through CH (C4), CH (C5) and C(CF3) (C6) to CH (C7), then to C7a (attached to N). This places CF3 at C6.

**N-aryl group.** The ring carbon attached to N has a neighbouring carbon bearing F (meta to N). The methyl is on the carbon para to N, and it is adjacent to the C–F carbon. This is a 3-fluoro-4-methylphenyl group.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N geometry is not clearly specified, so I leave it unassigned.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc(ccc1F)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C)c(F)c3)c3cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc23)c1O

name: rs_1482
text:

- Indoline ring: c1ccc2CCN(C(C)=O)c2c1 starts at C6 (the attachment point), then C5, C4, C3a. The CH2CH2 closes onto N, then C7a, then C7 closes the ring back to C6. This is consistent with the drawing.

name: rs_1480
text:
I read the molecule as a piperazine ring carrying two methyl groups, with a 3-fluoro-4-(trifluoromethyl)benzyl group on the other nitrogen.

**Ring and substituents**

- The tertiary N carries a CH2 linked to a benzene ring.
- On that benzene ring, relative to the CH2 attachment, F is at the meta position and CF3 is at the para position.

- Working through the neighbour order at each centre, with the implicit H pointing away from the viewer, gives `[C@@H]` for the left carbon and `[C@H]` for the right carbon in the SMILES below.
- Both methyls are on the same face, so this is the cis (meso) arrangement.

**Check:** the SMILES has one six-membered piperazine ring, one benzene ring, a CF3 group and an F, matching the drawing atom for atom.

name: rs_1483
text:
I read the drawing as a 3-hydroxy-4-methoxypyridine-2-carboxamide whose amide nitrogen is attached to C1 of a partly unsaturated decalin (octahydronaphthalene).

name: rs_1486
text:
I read the structure in three parts: the biphenyl acid, the hydrazone linker, and the N-aryl oxindole.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries F and CO2H on adjacent carbons. The ring atoms in order are C(F), C(CO2H), CH, C(aryl), CH, CH, with the carbon bearing the second ring at the junction. So the F-bearing carbon is ortho to the CO2H carbon, and the CO2H carbon is meta to the biaryl carbon. The biaryl carbon is the one at the right of the ring (235,105), joined to the lower ring at (295,145).

**Lower ring.** Its atoms in order are C1 (biaryl), C2 (OH), C3 (NH–N), C4 (CH), C5 (CH), C6 (CH).

**Hydrazone and oxindole.** The lower ring's NH connects to N=C3 of the oxindole. C2 is C=O, and N1 carries the 4-isopropylphenyl group. The CN sits on the benzo ring at the position para to C3a. C3a is attached to C3, and C4 is the top CH at (525,460). Going around, C5 is at (570,490), C6 is at (555,550) and bears the CN, C7 is at (490,580), and C7a is attached to N. So CN is at C6.

**SMILES.**
- Top ring: `OC(=O)c1cc(ccc1F)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C(C)C)cc3)c3cc(C#N)ccc23)c1O`
- Check on the top ring: c1 (CO2H), then c (CH), then c(...) (the biaryl carbon), then cc, then c1F. That places the CO2H carbon adjacent to the biaryl-side CH and to the F carbon, which matches the drawing.
- Oxindole benzo ring: `c3cc(C#N)ccc23` runs C7a, C7, C6(CN), C5, C4, C3a. This puts CN on C6, as drawn.

The hydrazone is written as drawn, with N=C3 and no stereo specified.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cc(ccc1F)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(C(C)C)cc3)c3cc(C#N)ccc23)c1O

name: rs_1477
text:
I read the structure in five parts and assigned stereochemistry from the wedges, hashes and double-bond geometry.

**Fragments**
- **Ring:** a tetrahydropyran (O, C2 to C6). C2 carries OMe and the thiazolidinone, C4 carries the ester oxygen, and C6 carries a phenethyl group.
- **Ester:** an O-acyl group, C(=O)–CH=C(CH3)–CH2CH2–CH=CH2. The ester carbonyl and the chain CH2 sit on the same side of the C=C, so the methyl is trans to the carbonyl. In SMILES this is `C(=O)/C=C(/C)CCC=C`.
- **Thiazolidinone:** a 2-oxo-thiazolidine whose nitrogen carries a PMB group (4-methoxybenzyl). Its C4 attaches to the pyran C2 and has an H drawn on a wedge.
- **Phenethyl:** CH2CH2Ph on C6.

**Unit 1 (30):** –CH2–C(CF3)(CO2–R)–, where R is 2-methyl-2-adamantyl. The ester oxygen is bonded to a carbon that carries a methyl group and sits in the adamantane cage at the 2-position.

**Unit 2 (70):** –CH2–C(CF3)(COO–R)–, where R is 1-adamantyl, attached through a bridgehead carbon.

**Adamantane SMILES**
- 1-adamantyl: C12(CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2)
- 2-methyl-2-adamantyl: C1(C)(C2CC3CC(C2)CC1C3). Here the quaternary C2 is bonded to the methyl, the ester O, and two bridgehead carbons (C1 and C3). The ring closures give C2(O)(C)[C@H]... without stereo: C1(C)(OC=O)C2CC3CC(C2)CC1C3.

Adamantane has bridgeheads A, B, C, D and CH2 groups between them. C2 lies between bridgeheads A and B. Write C2 as C1(C)(...) and then continue:
C1(C)C2CC3CC(C2)CC1C3

- C1 is the quaternary carbon.
- C2 is bridgehead A, opening ring 2.
- Then CH2, then C3 (bridgehead C, opening ring 3), then CH2, then C(C2), which is bridgehead D (a CH) bonded to a CH2 that closes onto A. This works.
- Then CH2, then C1, which is bridgehead B closing onto the quaternary carbon, and finally C3, a CH2 joining B to C.

Check: A is bonded to C2q, a CH2, and a CH2 (the one in the "(C2)" branch). B is bonded to C2q, a CH2, and a CH2 (the final C3). All bridgeheads are CH with three CH2 neighbours or the quaternary carbon, so the cage is valid.

The CH2 is placed before the next unit, so I wrote it as a two-unit fragment:
C(C(C(F)(F)F)(C(=O)OC1(C)C2CC3CC(C2)CC1C3))C(C(F)(F)F)... 

Simplified: write the two units connected head to tail.

name: rs_1547
text:
The structure is a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an isatin-type core.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring bearing CO2H. The biphenyl link sits meta to the acid, so this is a 3-carboxyphenyl group.

**Middle ring:** the carbon attached to the left ring is adjacent to the carbon bearing OH. The next carbon along carries the NH–N= group. Numbering from the biaryl carbon, C1 carries the aryl group, C2 the OH, and C3 the NHN. This gives 2-hydroxy-3-hydrazinyl-biphenyl.

**Hydrazone and indolinone:** NH–N=C3 of an indolin-2-one. C2 is C=O, and N1 carries a piperidin-4-yl group. No double-bond geometry is drawn clearly enough to assign, so I leave it unspecified.

**SMILES assembly:**
- Acid ring: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)
- Middle ring: c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(C3CCNCC3)c3ccccc23)c1O
- Joined: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(C3CCNCC3)c3ccccc23)c1O

In the middle ring, c1 (the biaryl carbon) is followed by ccc, then c(N...) and c1O. The ring atoms are c1, c, c, c, c(N), c1(O), which is six atoms, and the order is correct.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(C3CCNCC3)c3ccccc23)c1O

name: rs_1549
text:
I read the molecule as a pyrazin-2-one core carrying three substituents.

- **Pyrazinone ring:** N1–C(=O)–C(indolinyl)=N–C(Cl)=C1, so the carbon next to the ring nitrogen on the left carries Cl and the carbon next to C=O carries the indoline.
- **N1 substituent:** a CH bearing an ethyl group, a cyclopropyl group and an explicitly hashed H.
- **Indoline at C3:** attached through its nitrogen. The fused benzene ring has Cl at C7 (next to the ring fusion), F at C6 and OMe at C5.

**Stereocentre at the N1 substituent.** The H is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > cyclopropyl (C,C,H) > ethyl (C,H,H) > H. In the drawing, N is at the bottom, cyclopropyl at upper right and ethyl at upper left. Going N → cyclopropyl → ethyl is counterclockwise with H at the back, so the centre is S.

Writing the SMILES as CC[C@@H](C1CC1)N…, the neighbour order is ethyl, H, cyclopropyl, N. Working through the permutation, `@@` here gives S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC[C@@H](C1CC1)N1C=C(Cl)N=C(N2CCc3cc(OC)c(F)c(Cl)c32)C1=O

name: rs_1552
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

**Oxindole (left).** C2 is a carbonyl (O=C) bonded to N1. C3 is a CH2. The benzene ring carries Cl at C5 (para to N1 when counting from the ring-fusion carbon C7a). N1 is bonded to the piperidine C4.

Checking the Cl position: the benzene ring has C3a at the top left, C4 at the bottom left, C5 at the bottom (bearing Cl), C6 at the bottom right, C7 at the right, and C7a at the top right (bonded to N). That makes it 5-chlorooxindole.

**Piperidine.** The ring N is bonded to a CH2, then CH(OH), then another CH2, which connects to N1 of the pyrazole.

**Pyrazole, fused to a tetrahydropyridine (right).** N1 (bonded to the chain) is bonded to N2, and N2 is double bonded to C3. C3 carries the 4-CF3-phenyl group. C3 is bonded to C3a, and C3a is bonded to C7a, which is bonded to N1. C3a is also bonded to CH2 (C4), which is bonded to N5 (bearing SO2Me). N5 is bonded to CH2 (C6), then CH2 (C7), then back to C7a.

**SMILES assembly:**
- Oxindole: O=C1Cc2cc(Cl)ccc2N1C1CCN(CC1)...
- Chain and pyrazole: CC(O)Cn1nc(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)c2CN(S(C)(=O)=O)CCc12

The stereocentre at CH(OH) is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

SMILES: O=C1Cc2cc(Cl)ccc2N1C1CCN(CC1)CC(O)Cn1nc(-c2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc2)c2CN(S(C)(=O)=O)CCc12

text:

- On the benzo ring, C5 carries COOH, C6 carries OH, C7 carries OH, and C8 is H.

**Xanthone (right):**

- The left aromatic ring is C1 (H), C2 (attached to the chromone), C3 (Me) and C4 (acetyl). C4 is bonded to C4a, which bears the ring oxygen. C1 is bonded to C9a.
- The right aromatic ring carries OH at the two positions shown (the drawing's C6 and C7), with C5 and C8 as H.
- Ring atoms in order: C4a(O)–C5H–C6(OH)–C7(OH)–C8H–C8a(–C9=O)–C10a(–O).

**Xanthone SMILES:** c1(chromone)c(C)c(C(C)=O)c2oc3cc(O)c(O)cc3c(=O)c2c1

COCc1c(-c2cc3c(=O)c4cc(O)c(O)cc4oc3c(C(C)=O)c2C)oc2cc(O)c(O)c(C(=O)O)c2c1=O

Check on the chromone part: c1 is C3 with CH2OMe, c(-Ar) is C2, o is O1, c2 is C8a, c is C8, c(O) is C7, c(O) is C6, c(C(=O)O) is C5, c2 is C4a, and c1=O is C4, which closes to C3.

Check on the xanthone part as written in the full SMILES: c2 (C2), c (C1), c3 (C9a), c(=O) (C9), c4 (C8a), c (C8), c(O) (C7), c(O) (C6), c (C5), c4 (C10a, closing the ring), o, c3 (C4a), c(C(C)=O) (C4), c2C (C3, closing to C2). Ring closures are consistent.

name: rs_1556
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right gives a terminal vinyl group (CH2=CH–), two CH2 groups, and then a carbon bearing a methyl group that is double-bonded to a CH. That CH is attached to a carbonyl carbon (C=O) which carries OMe, so the molecule is methyl 3-methylhepta-2,6-dienoate.

For the stereochemistry of the C2=C3 double bond, the double bond is drawn vertically. At C3, the methyl points to the upper right and the CH2 chain to the upper left. At C2, the ester carbon points to the lower left and H to the right. The chain and the ester are therefore on the same side. Both are the higher-priority substituents on their carbons, so the alkene is Z.

In SMILES, `C/C(C)=C\C(=O)` places the chain carbon and the ester carbon cis, which matches this.

SMILES: C=CCC/C(C)=C\C(=O)OC

name: rs_1551
text:
I read the molecule as a 2,4,6-trisubstituted tetrahydropyran carrying three groups, and assigned the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes.

**Pyran ring (O1, C2–C6)**

- C4 carries a wedged ester oxygen. The ester is a 3-methylbut-2-enoate: O–C(=O)–CH=C(CH3)2.
- C6 is the anomeric carbon. It has a wedged OMe and is attached to C4′ of the thiazolidinone.

**Thiazolidin-2-one ring**
- C4′ has a wedged H and is bonded to C6 of the pyran.
- It is bonded to N, which carries the PMB group (4-methoxybenzyl, CH2C6H4OMe).
- It is also bonded to CH2–S, and the ring is closed by S–C(=O)–N.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned CIP descriptors from the drawn geometry and then converted them to @/@@ in SMILES atom order. All four stereocentres come out as R: C2, C4, C6 and C4′.

SMILES: O1[C@H](CCc2ccccc2)C[C@@H](OC(=O)C=C(C)C)C[C@]1(OC)[C@@H]1CSC(=O)N1Cc1ccc(OC)cc1

name: rs_1562
text:

text:

name: rs_1566
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl oxindole.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H at the para position and is bonded to a second ring. On that second ring, the carbon next to the biaryl bond bears OH. The next carbon bears the NH of the hydrazone (HN–N=).

**Hydrazone and oxindole.** The chain is Ar–NH–N=C3, where C3 is the oxindole carbon. The oxindole has C2(=O) and N1, with N1 bearing a 4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing shows the C=N bond with a specific geometry. The NH sits at the lower left of N, and the N=C bond runs down and to the right. Going from the N, the NH substituent points to the left (up-left of the N–N bond). On the C3 end, the C2 carbonyl lies below-left and the aryl ring carbon C3a lies to the right. The NH is therefore on the same side as C2 (C=O), which is the usual Z arrangement stabilized by an N–H···O hydrogen bond.

**SMILES construction.** I wrote the SMILES for the ring system first: OC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)-c1cccc(NN=C2C(=O)N(c3ccc(cc3)C(F)(F)F)c3ccccc23)c1O.

For the double bond I wrote N/N=C2/... and checked it. In `c(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(...)c3ccccc23)`, the NH–N bond is written "/" before N, so the N atom has NH "below" it. For C2, the `\C(=O)` bond, written after C2, puts C(=O) "below" C2 as well. NH and C(=O) are therefore on the same side, which is Z.

name: rs_1637
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Lactam ring:** a five-membered pyrrolidin-2-one with C=O at the top left, the ring N at the lower right of the carbonyl, and two CH₂ groups on the left.
- **N-substituent:** an N–CH₂–CH₂ chain leading to a para-substituted benzene ring that carries CO₂H.
- **Ring C5 (next to N):** carries a wedged bond to a trans CH=CH. The trans geometry is read from the drawn double bond.
- **Side chain:** after the alkene comes a CH(OH) drawn with a hashed bond, then CH₂ and a C(CH₃)₃ group.

**Stereocentres:**

- At ring C5 the priorities are N > vinyl > ring CH₂ > H. The wedged vinyl points toward the viewer, so H is in back. N (up), vinyl (down-right) and CH₂ (left) run clockwise, which gives R.
- At the carbinol carbon the priorities are OH > vinyl CH= > CH₂ > H. The OH is hashed, so H points toward the viewer. OH (down-left), vinyl (up-left) and CH₂ (right) run clockwise as drawn. Because H faces the viewer, this reverses to S.

I then chose the @/@@ symbols so that the SMILES encodes R at ring C5 and S at the carbinol carbon.
